events.venue: Awhi Yoga and Wellbeing Centre, 15 Johnston St., Wellington
events.long_description:
AWHI Yoga and Wellbeing’s accredited 200hr YTT program is a comprehensive and thorough journey into becoming a 200 hr certified Yoga Teacher. We are the only vinyasa yoga teacher training in the world that blends Te Ao Māori and ancient yoga wisdoms, offering a uniquely 'Aotearoa' experience while retaining universal relevance for teaching and practicing yoga in any part of the world.

Our training is suitable for individuals interested in becoming a yoga teacher, or those looking to take a personal journey towards deepening your own practice and knowledge. Either way, we guarantee a transformative and life-changing experience that will deepen your relationship to yoga, others, Aotearoa and your self.

Our uniquely Aotearoa Teacher Training explores the beautiful marriage between ancient Yoga and Te Ao Māori teachings over five separate modules during our three months together. Our course follows the Māori hauora/wellbeing model of Te Whare Tapa Whā, which takes the same holistic view of health taken by traditional Yoga. As we work through each pillar we start tapping into something way greater than ourselves, enabling us to connect with our purpose in life and how we might share this in service to the world!

A $1,000 deposit reserves your spot.

events.long_description:
Overview

Would you like to become less busy and more productive? Then our Time Management workshop is for you.

You've all heard the expression 'Time is money' Well actually time is more valuable than money because time is a non renewable resource. Do you ever have those times when you've been busy all day but feel that you have not achieved what you need to?

Effective Time Management is crucial in today's busy and competitive world. Successes and failures in work and daily activities largely depend on how time is managed. Therefore Time Management is the number one skill to master.

Do you ever feel overwhelmed by the sheer volume of work to be done? Would you like to become less busy and more productive? Then our Time Management workshop is for you. Let us show you and your organisation how to get the most out of a day with better time management skills.

WORKSHOP OBJECTIVES

Plan and prioritise each day’s activities in a more efficient and productive manner
Overcome procrastination quickly and easily
Handle crises effectively and quickly
Organise your workspace and workflow to make better use of time
Become less stressed, less busy and more productive
Delegate more efficiently
Handle interruptions and beat time wasters
Use rituals to make your life run smoother
Plan meetings more appropriately and effectively

Time management training most often begins with setting goals. These goals are recorded and may be broken down into a project, an action plan, or a simple task list. Activities are then rated based on urgency and importance, priorities assigned, and deadlines set.

This process results in a plan with a task list or calendar of activites. Routine and recurring tasks are often given less focus to free time to work on tasks that contribute to important goals. This entire process is supported by a skill set that includes personal motivation, delegation skills, organisational tools and crisis management tools.

For more information or to book: email info@biztrainers.co.nz or call 06 354 5555

events.long_description:
Overview

Defining change with clarity and agility. Discover how to apply the core skills and techniques of elicitation, analysis, and communication.

Description

The business world is demanding faster change, the ability to adapt and solutions that are fit for purpose. As a business analyst, you're counted on for your skills as a conceptual and practical thinker, a relationship builder, and a translator. You're relied upon to identify and describe the change required to address business issues. Sometimes there are problems that require a fix, opportunities that need to be realised or situations where the business simply doesn't know but is prepared to "give it a go" and experiment to gain insights to what it should do next.

In this course, you'll be introduced to a series of context aware, business-focussed approaches that you can apply to:

Work with stakeholders to uncover the business issue that needs to be addressed
Define the change required within its context
Prioritise and scope the requirements based on business value and
Specify requirements clearly to those delivering the solution

Designed and delivered by our Equinox IT team of practicing business analysts, this course covers how to structure your analysis activities based on the context and the issue at hand to describe requirements that fully represent the change required.




Outline
Day 1
Overview and concepts
What is business analysis?
Requirements analysis framework
Discover – understanding context
Understanding a business domain
Adjusting to different types of initiative
Stakeholders – identification, classification and engaging
Techniques (root cause analysis, 5 whys, diverge, converge, etc.)
The discovery canvas
Focus topic: Elicitation –gathering information and understanding
Purpose and context
Selecting the right technique (interviews, workshops, research, observation, brainstorming, etc.)
Planning a session
Running a session
Post session activities
Main exercise - role play
Day 2
Define – understanding the change required
Introduction to capabilities
Information and data – concept/domain Modelling
Business process – tips on modelling
Business rules – their relationship with other business concepts
Scenarios – use cases
Change strategy map
Change aspect map
Defining user and other stories
Scope – understanding priority and value
Helping the business to assess value
Techniques
User story maps
Day 3
Focus topic: Workshop Facilitation–gaining consensus
Being self-aware
Facilitation
Preparation
Group dynamics
Handling various situations
Main exercise - role play
Deliver – packaging for delivery
Backlog refinement
Developing good acceptance criteria
Understanding various types of solution requirements and contributing elements
Focus topic: Communication – telling the story
A brief overview of the difference between specification and communication




Learning outcomes

Upon completion of this course, students will be able to;

Analyse and understand the kind of business issue that needs to be addressed
Engage stakeholders and analyse their business needs
Define a change strategy
Define the aspects of change required
Understand various business models e.g. business process, information, business rules
Define a user story and associated requirements
Use effective techniques to elicit requirements
Understand how to plan and facilitate a requirements workshop
Understand scoping based on business value
Analyse, document and review solutions and detailed requirements
Define acceptance criteria
Understand how to communicate with a variety of audiences




Accreditation and certification

This course aligns with the Business Analysis Body of Knowledge v3.0®.




Audience

The primary audience for this course is business analysts, systems analysts and enterprise analysts of all experience levels. The course will also be of value to any project team members involved in requirements definition activities.




Prerequisites

There are no prerequisites for this course, however, some experience in business analysis will help.




Read less

events.long_description:
Explore Stonehenge Aotearoa at Your Own Pace

Our self-guided tour includes a map and a 12-minute audio-visual presentation to help you uncover the secrets of the henge. Afterward, head down to the stone circle and try out its unique acoustics — clap your hands and hear the echo respond, or whisper and see how far your voice carries.

A self-guided tour typically takes around 30 minutes, but many visitors stay longer simply because it’s so much fun. The bigger your group, the better the experience!

Please arrive at least 30 minutes before closing time.
Available during our opening hours: 10 AM – 4 PM.

events.long_description:
A high tea to delight your eyes and taste buds – with new menu inspired by Slow Burn: Women and Photography.

Inspired by Slow Burn: Women and Photography, the latest Eat Your Art Out high tea menu takes its cue from the world of photography.

From the delicate A Heart Exposed and the rich depth of The Chocolate Camera, to the savoury kick of The Apricot Proof, each item has been crafted by our award-winning chefs and is ready for its close-up.

Your high tea includes your choice of tea or coffee, with alcoholic beverages available to purchase. Dietary options are available on request.

Every purchase helps support Aotearoa New Zealand’s national museum.


Set Menu
(Includes one of each item per person)

A Heart Exposed
A delicate petite gâteau of tropical guava mousse layered with a vibrant raspberry centre, finished with refined textures and a balance of sweetness, bright berry acidity, and silky indulgence.

The Matcha Take
A refined Japanese-inspired madeleine infused with premium matcha, baked to a tender crumb with gentle earthy depth. Paired with luscious matcha ganache and sharp citrus bursts of yuzu gel.

The Chocolate Camera
An elegant chocolate creation showcasing the rich, velvety depth of premium Whittaker’s chocolate balanced with the vibrant citrus brightness of calamansi.

Golden Hour
A radiant tropical dessert crafted with luscious mango mousse and vibrant passionfruit notes, layered to create a light yet indulgent finish.

The Apricot Proof
A savoury petite muffin featuring sweet roasted capsicum folded through a soft, buttery crumb with delicate pockets of apricot for subtle fruity warmth.

Chicken Strut
Delicately layered smoked chicken paired with crisp cucumber ribbons, peppery rocket, and vibrant red pesto, nestled between soft artisan bread.

Green Screen Sandwich (V)
A beautifully balanced vegetarian finger sandwich showcasing tender grilled courgette, slow-roasted vegetable chutney, and fresh baby spinach.


Dietary Menu
(Includes one of each item per person)

The Mango Still (VE/GF)
A smooth mango mousse encased in a delicate chocolate shell, showcasing the fruit’s natural sweetness.

Peanut Butter Proof (VE/GF)
A rich peanut butter slice topped with a chocolate finish, balancing salty depth with a smooth, indulgent crumb.

Chocolate Darkroom (VE/GF)
Dark chocolate cups filled with smooth espresso-infused ganache, rich and intense from start to finish.

Matcha Moment (VE/GF)
Matcha chocolate shells with a bright citrus centre, balancing earthy green tea notes against a fresh citrus snap.

Apricot Aperture (VE/GF)
A vibrant apricot fruit jelly with an intense natural fruit flavour, finished with a delicate sugar coating for a clean, bright bite.

The Garden Negative (VE)
Tender grilled courgette layered with slow-roasted vegetable chutney and fresh baby spinach.

Fritter in Focus (VE)
Golden corn fritters served with beetroot mayonnaise, mesclun leaves, and vine-ripened tomatoes.


Paired with your choice of coffee or tea.

Alcoholic beverages are available for purchase.

Pre-booking is essential for any dietary requirements.

Dietary sandwiches can be made gluten-free on request.

events.long_description:
Ngā Mokopuna: A Living Building Story Tour

Join us for an introductory guided tour of Ngā Mokopuna, Te Herenga Waka Victoria University of Wellington's pioneering regenerative building project.

This experience explores the vision, values, and aspirations behind a building designed to tread lightly on the environment while creating lasting benefits for people and place. Grounded in principles of kaitiakitanga and inspired by mātauranga Māori, Ngā Mokopuna reflects a commitment to caring for our natural world and future generations.

During the tour, you'll learn about the Living Building Challenge, one of the world's most ambitious sustainability frameworks, and discover how Ngā Mokopuna has been designed to meet its rigorous standards. The project represents a significant step towards becoming one of Aotearoa New Zealand's next recognised Living Buildings.

From outside the building and surrounding precinct, you'll hear the stories behind its design, sustainability features, and cultural foundations. You'll also meet staff and student ambassadors who work and study within Ngā Mokopuna and learn firsthand how the building supports teaching, learning, wellbeing, and community.

The tour also provides an opportunity to view Te Tumu Herenga Waka Marae and hear how the marae and Ngā Mokopuna together express values of sustainability, kaitiakitanga, belonging, and connection.

Whether you're interested in sustainable design, Māori worldviews, education, architecture, or the future of the built environment, this tour offers a unique insight into a project that seeks to demonstrate what regenerative design can achieve.

Come and discover how sustainability and kaitiakitanga are being brought to life at Ngā Mokopuna.

events.name: Calligratherapy - Beginners
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Calligratherapy - Beginners
Many of us live sedentary lifestyles, sitting for up to eight hours or more a day hunched over our keyboard - all the while rarely taking a proper breath! Even if we wanted to take a deep enriching breath into the lower lobes of our lungs, we are limited due to our posture. Often due to the stresses and strains of a busy work and life balance, our unconscious brain can develop a pattern of holding, irregular and shadow breaths.
Does this sound like your experience? 
Not being able to breathe properly is the key cause of many chronic respiratory diseases (Nestor, 2020)
Calligratherapy combines science journalist James Nestor's theory on proper breathing with the philosophy of ancient Chinese calligraphy to promote a state of optimal wellbeing.
Calligratherapy has been developed specifically for those who have never practiced calligraphy before and who are interested in deriving the benefits without having to learn the language or all the characters. It integrates the simple and intuitive act of inhaling and exhaling into calligraphy practice with Eastern philosophy behind it.
A range of different breathing exercises are embedded into each 90 minute session focusing on different calligraphy scripts.  Over the five weeks, you will develop and practice the awareness of healthy breathing, while learning new techniques of Chinese soft brush calligraphy covering five different scripts. 
All materials included in course fee.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
Start a new creative practice in Chinese soft brush calligraphy
Develop your own mindfulness strategy
Better manage everyday stress levels and access a calm, empowered and positive state of mind
Find ways to explore eastern philosophy and develop deeper connections with your spiritual self. 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.long_description:
Scriptwriting
During this course, you will develop and build on your writing skills so you can confidently produce scripted narrative. You will learn how the basics of scriptwriting work, whether it be for stage or screen.
 Topics discussed and practised include the three act structure, script format, the differences between writing for film, theatre and television, creating dialogue, world building and more.
 We’ll take part in exercises, watch clips and have group discussions. In workshops, you’ll give and receive feedback, developing your scriptwriting skills through both. By the end of the course, you’ll be ready to finish your script, and take the next steps toward bringing it from page to stage (or screen!).
 Bring pen and paper.

- Analyse film, television, and theatre with a new lens for the way scripted stories work
- Develop character arcs and dynamics
- Create and build worlds
- Write effective dialogue and work with subtext
- Develop and implement a writing routine that works for your life
- Give and receive constructive feedback on your writing
- Have the confidence to put your work out into the world

events.long_description:
Sewing - All Levels
All levels welcome! Beginning sewers will learn basic skills and techniques and those with some experience will improve their skills and learn tips and tricks.
Beginners - If you're a beginner, you'll start by making a lined bag, which teaches all the basic skills involved. After that you'll move on to a project of your choice, in consultation with the tutor.  Please bring: 1 metre of firm cotton fabric for your bag outer and 1 metre of a lighter cotton fabric for the lining. You'll also need to bring scissors, a Bernina bobbin (this can be purchased from the CEC office on the day of the course for $7), pins, thread to match your outer fabric, an 18 cm zip and tape measure to the first session.
 If you're a returning student, or have already mastered the basic skills, you'll work on your own project so please bring along whatever you're currently working on (or something new) and your sewing kit. 
Please note PDF patterns are not suitable for this course unless you are very experienced in using them;  we strongly recommend patterns from the following companies:  Simplicity, Butterick, New Look or Quicksew.
By the end of the course, you'll have been introduced to basic skills in dressmaking, if beginners, or further skills for the more experienced.
You'll be able to:
• Use all sewing machine equipment and demonstrate basic sewing techniques (basic seams and finishes)
• Begin to read a commercial pattern and select appropriate materials for task
• Cut out and construct a garment using techniques learned
• (In addition), use a variety of advanced sewing techniques e.g. rolled hems, various zip insertions (invisible and standard), make buttonholes or line garments.

events.venue: Stonehenge Aotearoa, 51 Ahiaruhe Rd, Carterton
events.long_description:
Experience Stonehenge Aotearoa at its most breathtaking — as the sun dips below the Wairarapa horizon.
Our Sunset Guided Tour blends astronomy, storytelling, and the natural beauty of twilight for an evening you will never forget.

Led by one of our knowledgeable guides, this 90-minute experience explores how ancient cultures used the Sun to track time and mark the turning of the seasons. You’ll discover the scientific and cultural thinking behind the Henge’s unique Southern Hemisphere design before watching the sunset alignment from inside the stone circle.

Weather permitting, you’ll witness how the setting Sun interacts with the structure — a striking moment that links ancient knowledge with the rhythms of the natural world.

Duration and Schedule
• Allow: Approximately 90 minutes
• Start Time: Begins one hour before sunset
• Availability: Offered any day with advance booking

events.long_description:
As part of Wellington Jazz Festival, The Undercurrent presents Cranberry Trio!

Cranberry Trio are a Tāmaki Makaurau/Auckland based trio made up of Iggy Nama Ruci (alto saxophone), Ryan Tomov (upright bass), and Finn McNeill (drums). 

The group have an exciting and original style shaped by their years of playing together, their shared musical influences and philosophies and an interest in exploring collective improvisation, rhythmic complexity and melodic interplay. Influenced by the sounds and theories of Ornette Coleman (most notably his theory of harmolodics), Anthony Braxton, John & Alice Coltrane and Derek Bailey - The Cranberry Trio will present a set entirely made up of their original compositions, some unearthed for the first time for curious ears to discover - at Undercurrent Books this Wellington Jazz Festival! 

Thursday Oct 15
Doors 6pm
Music 6:30pm
$20 ($10 students)

Tickets available online and at the door!

Snacks, a range of refreshing drinks, tea & coffee, and of course...books available for purchase!

Official Jazz Festival info here https://www.jazzfestival.nz/.../lil-chuck-the-one-man.../
Li'l Chuck The One man Skiffle Machine is an authentic one man band performing “good time music with old time style”
Having spent a lifetime rummaging through the drawers of 1930's - 50's music, Chuck’s songs are inspired by the sounds of the era - Blues, Early Jazz, Western Swing, Ragtime etc. and are uniquely presented in the style of street performers from those glory days. Sticking to the traditional one man band format, Chuck plays all the instruments simultaneously.
Captivating storytelling intertwines effortlessly with heart stopping harmonica. Multiple guitar styles are underpinned by his left and right feet frantically pounding the kick and hi hat. The listener is left simply wondering, How the hell does he do that?
Originally hailing from the UK, Li’l Chuck has been stomping his music in NZ since 2003.
Stunning vocal stunning harmonica and acoustic guitar that needs no window dressing
Blues matters magazine (UK) May 2019
A true multi-instrumentalist & multi-tasker in addition to a talented artist.
No depression magazine USA. March 2017
Li'l Chuck combines almost every element of pure joy. 4 1/2 stars (out of 5)
NZlListener. March 2017.
Sublime harp and heartfelt vocals leave the listener wanting more
Blues matters magazine (UK) June 2017

events.name: Pōneke La Pompe
events.venue: Superfina, Wellington
events.long_description:
Pōneke La Pompe is Wellington’s answer to a smoky Parisian side street, 1930s edition, minus the smoke, plus a bit more Cuba Street chaos.

Named for Pōneke, one of the city’s Māori names, fused with “la pompe” (the relentless rhythm-guitar heartbeat of jazz manouche), the quartet steals shamelessly from Django Reinhardt and Stéphane Grappelli and gets away with it. Violinist Ana Henderson and clarinettist Josh Buckler duel it out on the melodies while guitarists Mike Kingston and David Harris hold the whole thing together with hands fast enough to set the strings on fire. Expect hot club standards, a few originals, and the kind of swing that makes sitting still very difficult.

Koha is welcomed :)

events.venue: Penthouse Cinema & Café,205 Ohiro Road, Brooklyn, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
La Bola Negra - fundraising screening
Join the Wellington Pride Festival for a fundraising screening of 'La Bola Negra' on 15 October at the Penthouse Cinema in Brooklyn.

LA BOLA NEGRA tells the story of three men whose lives are intimately connected through desire, pain and inheritance, across three different eras - 1932, 1937, and 2017.

- Winner, Festival De Cannes: Best Director
- "A work of staggering genius" - Indiewire.com
- "Extraordinary" - Deadline

Starring Spanish music sensation Guitarricadelafuente, Miguel Bernardeau, Carlos González, Milo Quifes, Lola Dueñas, Julio Torres, Penélope Cruz and Glenn Close. From Cannes-winning directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi (Los Javis).

Ambrossi says "....For me, it’s part of the ongoing fight, it’s even a political decision. To have three openly gay men leading a major film, that’s still rare. Even today, many LGBTQ+ stories are told by straight actors. We wanted this film to truly be made by gay men, not just about them."

___Accessibility___

- The film is in Spanish and will also be screened with English captions
- The theatre is wheelchair accessible and wheelchair accessible bathrooms are available
- Parking is available right next door in the Penthouse carpark
- You are more than welcome to wear a mask.

Tickets $25 waged, $20 low or unwaged. Your money goes to supporting the Wellington Pride Festival, Aotearoa's longest-running Pride Festival.

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
The Joy of Improvisation
Improv is theatre without a script and a fun way to build your skills in many areas, including team work, public speaking, storytelling and on-your-feet creative thinking.
This is the perfect place for absolute beginners to get acquainted with the joy and art of improvisation, inspired by the generous creative philosophy of Keith Johnstone. It's also a great place to get back into improv if you've been away from it for a while.
WIT has been teaching this course in association with the CEC for almost 20 years now. It uses fun games and structured exercises to teach the foundation skills of improv. These are a prerequisite for further courses and membership of WIT (www.wit.org.nz), as well as useful in themselves.
If you have questions about the course, please contact WIT directly on info@wit.org.nz.
By the end of the course, you'll have: 
• Explored basic principles of improvisation
• Enjoyed interacting in a friendly, positive and supportive environment
• Developed more confidence, presentation and communication skills
• Experienced joyful moments of improvisation
The course will end with a directed demonstration of class exercises for invited friends and family.
[This is a physical activity that involves an element of risk.  While all possible measures are taken to prevent accidents or injury, please note that participation is at your own risk]. 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. As part of Wellington Jazz Festival, The Undercurrent presents John Rae’s BOP-IT!

John Rae’s BOP-IT! returns to the festival after last year's sell-out concert that had the crowd going wild.

Featuring a stellar lineup of Aotearoa’s finest jazz musicians, John Rae’s BOP-IT! delivers a high-energy celebration of the hard bop era. events.long_description:
His improvisations consistently reveal an immersion in the tradition balanced with a fearless, joyful and searching personality of his own.” - UK Jazz News

After releasing his last album 'Elegant Calamity' to a sold-out crowd at last Wellington Jazz Festival, flamboyant saxophonist Oscar Lavën makes his return to the Rogue and Vagabond this festival to release a brand new album, 'Flamingovision'.

Oscar Lavën has played with many notable artists such as John Beasley's MONKestra, Steve Gadd, James Carter, Dave Weckl, Peter Erskine, Lalah Hathaway, Clay Jenkins and more. His effervescent style draws on an eclectic musical background of early swing music, New Orleans traditional, straight-ahead, spiritual jazz, classical music, blues, and 50s bar-walking rock and roll sax.

Prepare for a colourful, kaleidoscopic performance featuring Duncan Haynes (piano), John Rae (drums), Michael Taylor (trumpet) and Patrick Bleakley (double bass) as they play through the album live in an exciting release of new original New Zealand music.

$15 online, $20 on the door

events.id: Cornelia Parker-City Gallery Wellington-Wellington NZ
events.name: Cornelia Parker
events.venue: City Gallery Wellington
events.long_description:
After three years of closure, the newly renovated and strengthened City Gallery Wellington Te Whare Toi will host the art of Cornelia Parker. The British visual artist is best known for her innovative and contemporary sculpture and installation art. Her large-scale, immersive installations explore themes of destruction and reconstruction, transformation and metamorphosis. Objects are exploded, crushed, and suspended in a world upended and remade anew.
Curated by independent UK-based curator Andrea Schlieker and City Gallery Wellington’s Senior Curator Aaron Lister, City Gallery Wellington’s exhibition will encompass Parker’s long career as an artist. This includes an immersive sound-and-light installation, ‘Stolen Thunder’. The work gathers the sounds of approaching storms from around the globe and across time. The exhibition will also showcase her paintings, photos, films, and sculptures.
“I have always said this is the one exhibition I want to do before I die,” said Charlotte Davy, Ringatohu Toi Director, Art and City Gallery Wellington. “I have been following Cornelia Parker’s work for the last twenty years. Bringing her mischievous, dark, and literally explosive work to Wellington is incredible.” 
Parker’s work often fills entire rooms and invites the viewer to move through and around the art. Given its physical scale, the blank canvas of the reopened gallery offers the perfect opportunity to host the exhibition. The exhibition will kick off in October 2026 and run through March 2027. 
Charlotte notes the exhibition’s themes are also of particular relevance to Wellington. “I hope that the exhibition and our return to Te Ngākau Civic Square will reflect our city and also help remake it. We are looking forward to opening with a bang.”

events.id: Secret Screenings: With Beau Miles tickets-Meow Nui, Wellington, New Zealand-Ticketek
events.name: Secret Screenings: With Beau Miles tickets
events.venue: Meow Nui, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Presented by: TEG Live
TEG Live is proud to present Secret Screenings with Beau Miles, an intimate live touring show bringing Beau’s unreleased and unfinished film collection — none of it yet on YouTube — to venues across Australia and New Zealand in 2026.
The premise is straightforward: three or four of Beau’s new films, shown somewhere between a first and final draft. The audience won’t know the titles before they see them. The films aren’t finished, but are entirely watchable. And in between screenings, Beau tells the stories behind them - why they exist, why they look the way they do, and why a man who lives on a small farmlet in Victoria keeps putting himself through things that are, by his own admission, sometimes remarkable, often mundane, and occasionally disgusting.
It’s an evening that moves between film and live performance - part director’s commentary, part stand-up tangent, part confessional. The stories may or may not connect to the films. The Q&A that closes the evening has been independently verified as world-class by one audience member. That audience member was Beau. He’s confident.
Beau Miles has built a devoted following through a body of work that resists easy categorisation - adventure films that aren’t really about adventure, mundane experiments that turn out to mean something, and a stubborn commitment to doing things slowly and in person. Secret Screenings brings that sensibility into the room: unmediated, unfinished, and told by the person who made it.

Expect familiar melodies, unexpected turns, and a celebration of jazz. For two nights only, Set Fire to the Brass brings a two-part show to The Opera House. First on stage, say ‘Hello’ to Kiwi vocalist Joanna Darling. She gives English singer-songwriter Adele’s songs a lush, jazz-infused edge. She’ll give full-hearted renditions of hits like Rolling in the Deep and Skyfall. Members of the Rodger Fox Big Band and local musicians lead the second half with improv solos and classic jazz standards. 

Joanna has performed in musicals, cabarets, and as a soloist on international cruise lines. She combines a powerful vocal belt with piano and guitar. The Rodger Fox Big Band has played at prestigious jazz festivals and won six Tui Awards for the best New Zealand jazz recording. Together, they deliver the emotional depth of Adele’s lyrics with the warmth of live jazz.

events.long_description:
Inside Circa Theatre’s waterfront venue, you’ll find two performance spaces. Both offer a smorgasbord of professional theatre throughout the year. Playwrights from international heavy hitters to brilliant Kiwi voices are represented. It also includes programming from comedies and cabarets to contemporary dance and pantomime. 
Before or after your show, visit the on-site café, brasserie and restaurant, Chouchou. It opens out onto a deck, where you can take in views across the harbour. Look up to admire the art installation above. Called ‘Velarium’, it undulates in the wind, mirroring the water in the harbour. 
Circa Theatre began its life in 1976. A breakaway group of actors and theatre practitioners decided that Aotearoa needed a new and innovative approach to theatre. Five decades later, it is still pushing boundaries, making people laugh and cry, and creating theatrical memories. 
If you don’t have your own Circa memory yet, there’s an opportunity to create one nearly every night of the week.

events.long_description:
Elegance - Wellington
Dynamic British Isata Kanneh-Mason make her NZSO debut in a concert featuring Mozart, Brahms and Andrée.

Programme:
Andrée Andante Recitative
WA Mozart Piano Concerto No. 27
Brahms Serenade No. 1

Isata Kanneh-Mason, the eldest sibling in a dynasty of extraordinary musicians, is being lauded as a pianist who is “the real deal” (classical-scene.com). What a treat to hear her bring such intelligent elegance to Mozart’s last piano concerto. Praised by BBC Music Magazine as capable of making “lines sing beautifully and virtuosic passages dance, finding intimacy and eloquence at telling moments”, Kanneh-Mason is the perfect performer to bring this mature, serenely lovely concerto to Aotearoa New Zealand audiences.

To round out this programme, the NZSO performs two works that deserve a wider audience. Brahms’ Serenade harks back to Mozart’s own delightful serenades, while Elfrida Andrée’s Andante Recitative, written in 1878, was only rediscovered in the 1980s, and “open[s] in broody darkness, but quickly blossom[s] into optimistic, songful melody” (Michael Clive).

events.long_description:
The Triple Swing Bill | Wellington Jazz Festival
The Guiding Tones, Arēki Trio and Uncle Chipper are teaming up this Wellington Jazz Festival to bring you a triple-header afternoon of swing at the iconic Old St Paul's!

The Guiding Tones is an unconventional jazz trio based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. Consisting of Vadim Fong on clarinet, Zylah Vivace on guitar and Joseph Coleman on piano accordion, they bring unique instrumentation and a fresh voice to classic swing repertoire. The group plays a range of material, focusing mainly on swing music à la Duke Ellington, but also branching into jazz manouche and even bebop.

Arēki Trio is also based in Wellington and features Alex Christensen on guitar, Ned Rainey on drums, and Mathieu Ornberg on bass. The trio formed in their first year at Te Kōkī / New Zealand School of Music through their shared studies in jazz, and continue to create music together. The trio plays a range of music, including classic ballads, modern jazz, and atmospheric pieces aiming to create an environment where grooving rhythms and improvisation flow.

This group endeavours to make Uncle Chipper proud through their performance of various elegant jazz tunes. Come along to witness this flock of friends experimenting with collaborative ideas. Max Stopyra will be in attendance, holding down the bass lines. Sascha Hunt will be too, but more in the strumming department. Ranu Wijesuriya and his cymbal (+ kit) will collaborate with the aforementioned Max to groove. Logan Heppell will oversee the department of ivory tickling, while Sylvester Green will add elements of melody at times.

The Wellington Jazz Festival is on 14-18 October.

Tickets are on sale from Wednesday 2 September with pricing starting at $10.

As part of Wellington Jazz Festival, The Undercurrent presents Song For Iqbal, Song For Pat - Miro Holland Group!

After a stellar year, an album release and Aus/Aotearoa tour, Miro Holland Group returns to the Festival with special guests. The band grew up learning to play together, and have continued. Miro's compositional theory is an attempt at highlighting that history. 

'Song For Iqbal, Song for Pat' is a dedication to both the philosopher Muhammad Iqbal -a major creative and moral influence for Miro- and to Miro's Great Aunt Pat, whose life was lived entirely in the service of others. Both figures are moral influences for Miro, though at different points in his development. 

Tonight, the group will feature two very special guests:

Lucas Kewell, an internationally acclaimed pianist fresh from completing studies at the renowned JAZZCAMPUS in Basel, Switzerland.
Patrick Bleakley, who has appeared on many internationally acclaimed albums, and had a legendary stint in the infamous Aotearoa group BLERTA.

The weekend flow: 🎨🧘🌿




Friday

Arrive at the retreat centre, dinner together and a quick catch-up




Saturday

🧘 60 min Yoga session

🥐 Breakfast

🎨 Watercolour adventure walk to the river

We will take a slow-paced stroll to the local Ōtaki River together and stop along the way at some beautiful, scenic spots to create some watercolour art guided by our host Neve.

🪨 Positive habits + rock painting workshop with Karuna

This workshop will start with an opportunity to reflect on your values and priorities in life and a chance to learn about how to build and stick to positive habits. You will then create your own visual daily habit tracker through the medium of rock painting to help you work towards your goals and become the best version of yourself.

🍲 Lunch

🍷 Paint & Sip with Neve

This event will start with a calming warm-up activity where we will explore the playful combination of painting along to various types of music. Then we will flow into creating a master ' peace ' inspired by things that bring us peace and joy on a canvas while we sip on chai or mocktails (tbc!)

🍛 Dinner

🎶 Music meditation (Kirtan) jam night




Sunday

🧘 60 min Yoga session

🥐 Breakfast

🌲 Forest bathing + collaborative nature mandala art with Karuna

A grounding guided meditation in the native bush to de-stress and connect with nature. After this we will create some collaborative mandalas using the meditation as inspiration for our creations.

✏️ Breathe & Draw art workshop with local artist Anja

Our (Beginner-friendly)Breathe and Draw workshop will be an art class focusing on drawing itself rather than the outcome of your work. This class is all about turning inner chaos into calm, visual order through mindful drawing. Starting with simple, spontaneous lines and adding as we go

events.long_description:
Secret Screenings with Beau Miles (Wellington)
Beau Miles is taking his Secret Screenings on the road - bringing a collection of new, unreleased films to intimate venues across Australia and New Zealand in 2026. None of them are on YouTube yet. You’ll see them first.

The idea is simple: three or four of Beau’s films, shown somewhere between a first and final draft. None of them fully finished, but are entirely watchable. None of them named in advance. You won’t know what you’re watching until it starts - and each one has a story to tell beyond what’s on screen.

In between films, Beau tells a bunch of stories about why the films are the way they are. Why he loves finding things. Why he needs to shower more. Why a man living on a small farmlet in regional Victoria keeps dragging himself into rivers and eating spotty bananas and filming it all. The stories may or may not have anything to do with the films being shown. That’s part of the deal.

The evening finishes with a Q&A - voted the best thing ever witnessed by one audience member. That audience member was Beau. He stands by it.

Presale commences: 11am, Thu 11 June
General sale commences: 11am, Fri 12 June

Register for presale: https://ffm.link/bm26reg

events.long_description:
500 Days in the Wild | Q&A Screening
Director and Star Dianna Whelan joins Penthouse Cinema for an exclusive screening of 500 Days in the Wild, following with a Q&A session after the film.

500 Days In The Wild follows the epic 6-year journey of filmmaker Dianne Whelan as she sets out to reconnect with nature and become the first person to travel the world’s longest trail.

The 24,000 km Trans Canada Trail stretches across the continent of North America, connecting the Atlantic, Arctic and Pacific oceans. It is the longest trail in the world. For six years filmmaker Dianne Whelan traveled the entirety of the land and water trails, the only person to ever accomplish this journey. 500 Days in the Wild recounts Dianne’s journey by bike, canoe, skis, snowshoes and on foot and her cross-cultural visits with those who live close to the land.

This feature doc culled from 800 hours of footage is an intricate weave of adventure film, personal reflection and stunning captures of wildlife and landscapes. Using humour, adventure, beautiful cinematography and a great soundtrack (including songs from Joni Mitchell, First Aid Kit, Xavier Rudd, and The Tragically Hip), 500 Days in the Wild will entertain audiences and inspire hope for the future.

She started out alone, disillusioned with state of the world, to look for different ways of caring for the land and for each other. She ended the journey a bit wiser, more hopeful, in love and with a passion to share this story.

Winner - Grand Prize VIMFF
Winner - Best Film World Trail Film Festival
Winner - Best Film Nordic Adventure Film Festival
Winner - Audience Award - Victoria Film Festival

events.long_description:
Fresh off their June 2026 debut album release, Star Time returns to the Wellington Jazz Festival for yet another epic showdown at San Fran!

Star Time is a high energy Afrobeat jazz ensemble which arose from the ever growing jazz and African music scenes in Te-Whanganui-A-Tara. Led by the charismatic Rwandan-born vocalist Francois Judah, and backed by a massive 8-piece band, they aim to deliver a sonically unforgettable experience in the form of traditional Afrobeat dance rhythms, and spontaneous live arrangements which have set audiences on fire since their formation in 2024.

Star Time has continuously honed in on their signature fusion of afrobeat, dance music and jazz in a way that highlights their undeniably contagious energy as a group. Releasing their debut album ‘WE ARE HERE’ in 2026, this body of work boldly cemented their sound, rooted in homage to African music and rhythms, with the aim of uniting all people on the dance floor.




San Fran holds a Supervised License. Minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue.

events.long_description:
The Wellington Comedy Club, with Jamaine Ross, Joe Daymond, Lily Catastrophe
The Wellington Comedy Club returns, with a big night of laughs featuring New Zealand's best.

Joe Daymond
Joe has performed at Sydney Opera House as part of Just for Laughs Australia, as well as appearances on Have You Been Paying Attention?, 7 Days and Celebrity Treasure Island. Having already begun to make strides in the US, he became only the second Kiwi ever to perform in the Main Room at the world famous Hollywood Comedy Store and was invited to join social media sensation Noel Miller on his US tour.

Jamaine Ross
Jamaine is a born and bred Christchurchian who is becoming a well-known comedic face on the stand-up circuit as 'The Maori guy with the beard and the hat'.
Over his stand-up career he has achieved a number of accolades, including winning the Raw Comedy Quest in 2012, garnering a Billy T Award nomination in 2014, and winning the inaugural NZ International Comedy Festival's 'Best Facial Hair' award in 2014. He has also opened for Tenacious D on their New Zealand tour in 2013, and opened for Demetri Martin at his Christchurch show in 2019.

Lily Catastrophe
Lily is an award-winning comedian and cabaret performer based in te Whanganui-ā-Tara.
A rising star in the Wellington scene, Lily won Best New Comedian at the Wellington Comedy Awards 2024.
"Lily's outstanding crowd work has us eating out of her hand" - Regional News
"A gorgeous performer both technically and energetically" - Art Murmurs

Also featuring
Bronson Toghill
Keegan Thomas
Mamaeroa Munn (Fri only)
Ralph Hilaga (Fri only)
Lydia Sainsbury (Sat only)

For this Wellington Comedy Club we're partnering with WELLFed
Since 2016, WELLfed's mission has been nourishing communities through food and connections. They are dedicated to helping individuals and families thrive by growing skills and confidence, improving health and wellbeing, and strengthening community connections.

events.long_description:
Future soul singer Wallace presents an evening of songs from the movies and musicals that soundtracked her childhood - The Wizard of Oz, Singing in the Rain, Some Like It Hot, Sabrina and more.

From a young age, Wallace was captivated by music from the golden age of Hollywood, singing along to the likes of Judy Garland, Marilyn Monroe and Doris Day. That early love became a gateway into jazz and ultimately set her on her musical path.

After more than a decade living and touring overseas, Wallace is now back home in Wellington. Her international career has seen her tour alongside artists including Sampa the Great, and support heavyweights such as Little Simz, Morcheeba, Jordan Rakei, Rag'n'Bone Man, Slum Village and Masego. Now, with a six-piece band, led by the incredible Daniel Hayles, she returns to the music where it all began.

Wow, what a voice... Just good soul music - Gilles Peterson

$20 online $25 on the door

Part of the Wellington Jazz Festival 2026

As part of Wellington Jazz Festival, The Undercurrent presents A Game of Two Solos!

How well do jazz musicians really know jazz?

Hosted by the ever-witty John Rae, A Game of Two Solos pits two teams of top musicians against each other in a fast-paced quiz packed with musical puzzles, obscure trivia, listening challenges, and plenty of good-natured rivalry. Team captains Ben Wilcock and Dan Yeabsley lead their sides through a series of rounds that test everything from jazz history and legendary recordings to harmony, improvisation, and the unexpected.

Imagine University Challenge meets a comedy panel show, with live music thrown into the mix. Expect brilliant performances, quick-fire banter, surprising revelations, and the occasional spectacular wrong answer. Whether you're a lifelong jazz aficionado or simply enjoy great entertainment, this is a lively celebration of the music, its history, and the people who love it. Followed by the Undercurrent legendary Jam Session.

Come and cheer on your favourite team, test your own jazz knowledge from the audience, and enjoy an evening where virtuosity and comedy share the same stage.

events.name: Financial Planning for Retirement
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Financial Planning for Retirement
Massey University's annual Retirement Expenditure Guidelines study (2019) found:
Just 40% of pre-retirees believed they were well-prepared for retirement, and 57% considered retirement to be a concern.  They also confirmed, New Zealand Superannuation is not sufficient to fund the retirement most people want.
Ministry of Social Development (2020):
22% of all people receiving New Zealand Superannuation also receive additional support payments, with over 44,000 superannuants receiving additional accommodation support,
And if you needed to obtain Government assisted accommodation, at the end of March 2020, more than 16,300 households were waiting for state or social housing.
Living in a motel or boarding house with strangers (who may have other vulnerable backgrounds) is not an ideal or safe location to spend your retirement years.   But for many, it is the only option they can afford.
If you have not planned for your retirement, then this course is you! 
This course has been developed for people in their 50’s or 60’s that are looking at retirement and have no idea if they can financially survive it: what to do, what $’s they need, how or where they can generate additional income, or even where to go to get help. 
It is targeted towards those that still have some time (for some - not much) to make adjustments, learn some basic financial skills, make some big decisions, and positively influence the quality of their pending retirement. 
You will be introduced to a simple step by step guide to developing a financial plan for retirement. 
You will work though a case study in class, and can then go away and repeat the process with your own data/details.  You will be provided with comprehensive course notes to enable you to update the case study information with your own information. 
At each step, key considerations and financial concepts will be defined, explained and discussed to help you understand the financial requirements of retirement.  
Are you ready for the retirement lifestyle you hoped or dreamed of?  If not, then this course is for you.
A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.
Disclaimer:  The tutors are not financial advisors.  No investments, products nor specific recommendations will be provided.  A step by step planning process will be taught by working through a case study.  Key considerations that should be used by the participants when looking at their own options to bridge the financial gap between what is available through superannuation and what is required to meet lifestyle goals will be provided and discussed.  Product names may be used in examples and explanations to help participants understand the financial concepts and the planning process.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Got your test results back and still wondering what a centiMorgan or a shared match is?  Find out what the size of your match means and the tools available to help you work out possible family relationships.
We'll start by looking at Clustering and how the Grouping tool on Ancestry.com can help with this.  We'll also look at the ThruLines and Common Ancestors tools to see how they can provide suggestions for knocking down brick walls in your research.
Also covered during this course are other websites you can upload your results to, how to manage other family member's DNA test results and other tools available when you get a bit more advanced - and just in case you need help in the future, we'll look at some of the places you could get this from.

-  Understand the information provided by Ancestry.com about your DNA matches

events.long_description:
Getting the Most from AI: Practical Skills for Everyday Use
(NZ Citizens and residents pay $29 with ID, all others pays $120).
AI tools are everywhere, but knowing which one to use — and how to use it well — makes all the difference. In this hands-on workshop, Jon Bell will guide you through practical techniques to make AI a genuinely useful partner in your work and life. Whether you've tried it a few times or use it regularly, you'll leave with real skills you can apply straight away, with no technical background needed.
We'll start with a quick tour of the main tools — ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Copilot — so you understand what makes each one different. (They're less different than you might think!) Then we'll spend most of the day going deep on Claude, which Jon considers the easiest to use, while also being the most powerful.
We'll cover real examples, answer your questions as they come up, and spend plenty of time experimenting together.
By the end of the workshop, you'll be able to:
- Write effective prompts that get clearer, more useful responses
- Use AI for research, brainstorming, writing, and creative work
- Understand the differences between the major tools and when to use each
- Recognise the tools' limitations (and how to work around them)
- Apply practical strategies for using AI in your personal or professional projects
- Confidently troubleshoot when AI gives unexpected or unhelpful answers
Please bring: A phone or laptop with ChatGPT and Claude installed and signed in to both. Enough battery to last the day.

Join us for a fun and creative fused glass workshop where you’ll design and decorate your very own miniature glass house.

Create Your Own Mini Fused Glass House

In this hands-on workshop, you’ll design and decorate your very own mini fused glass house.

You’ll have a selection of coloured glass, textures and decorative elements to choose from, allowing you to create a unique little house in your own style. You’ll learn the basics of working with fused glass and be guided through the process from design to finishing touches.

Each participant will create one mini glass house during the class. Once complete, your piece will be carefully fired in the kiln to fuse the glass together.

As kiln firing takes time, your finished house will not be available to take home on the day. It will be ready for collection at a later date once the firing process is complete. Collection details will be provided at the workshop.

events.long_description:
Sculpture - Intro to Creature Sculpting
Join us for a fun day of creature making! Design and sculpt a one-of-a-kind character in your own style from polymer clays in a full spectrum of colours!

Working with oven-cured clays and wrapped wire armatures, this workshop offers a variety of modelling methods and approaches - a great opportunity to turn sketches & ideas into tangible 3D forms. Modern clay inventions mean we can create translucent, glittery, semi-flexible, UV reactive or even glow-in-the-dark elements to add more realism or a touch of the surreal into each creation!

Students will be coached through designing and creating a small-scale creature sculpture, beginning simple, and building to a more complex final form as we get familiar with materials.

The class offers beginner students a fun introduction to sculpting organic forms from scratch, and for those with some hands-on creative experience, it offers a great opportunity to experiment, hone and advance your making skills to new levels.

If you can, bring along some design ideas, sketches or reference images to help kick start the sculpting process on the day.

Please wear closed-in footwear suitable for a workshop environment. bring a work apron if you have one or wear clothes you don’t mind getting a little grubby. Remember to bring your reading glasses if you have them.

events.long_description:
Our on-farm Craft Open Days are aimed primarily at knitters, spinners, crocheters and other fibre crafters.

Nestled in the small rural community of Tinui is Rewa Rewa Station. Operating as a hill country Sheep & Beef breeding farm with a strong focus on NZ Wool & Fibre. Romney, Corriedale cross Romney, Polwarth & Gotland sheep provide the fleeces to create fibre products for crafters, which are sold via the Rewa Rewa Station website, and at Fibre Markets. Our Studio Shop is also open during Craft Days or by appointment outside of these days.

Our Craft Days allow you to work on your own project, seek advice, learn a new fibre skill or maybe just spend time with fellow fibre crafters while potentially ticking off a project or two in the process.

Please bring your knitting, crocheting, spinning, hand sewing, or any project you are working on and enjoy a drive in the country!

Coffee, tea and snacks provided, but bring your lunch and stay awhile.

Everyone is welcome, the more the merrier!

Note: Craft Days are primarily held on the 3rd Saturday of every mont,h but occasionally we do have to juggle the dates.

events.long_description:
Overview

Our women's workshop is probably the most intense, comprehensive, enjoyable & hands-on self-defence syllabus in New Zealand & Australia.

The workshop is rated R13 so only those aged 13 and above can attend due to the content taught. There are a limited amount of spaces available so book early. Please note that this is a one-day workshop.

Don't let the price deceive you; we're firm believers that every woman and family deserves the opportunity to participate in workshops like this without having to break the bank.

So, what sort of things can you expect to learn at this workshop?

You learn the vital parts of the body - parts of the body that are vulnerable & easy to attack.
Learn how to block an attack confidently.
Learn how to defend yourself against slaps, punches, pushes & grabs.
Learn to defend yourself against headlocks, hair grabbing, and wrist grabs.
Learn how to defend yourself against chokeholds, and bear hugs.
Learn how to defend yourself on the ground.
Learn effective rape defence techniques.
Learn how to use your hands, legs, knees & elbows as weapons.
Learn to defend yourself against many other types of attacks with confidence.

Plus, lots, lots more. (depending on the time allowed & the participant's progression)
What we teach is how to deal with the worst-case scenario, when the awareness, avoidance and de-escalation have failed, it all turns physical, there's no obvious way to escape & you must fight back.

"... a massive shout out to Charlie Riley for all the amazing work he does. Charlie, you are a champion among champions. Thank you. Ladies, if you loved #reebokunleashed or if you missed out, please check out Charlie and find a course near you."
Zoe Bell - Hollywood Stunt Woman, Actress & Producer

This is the 17th year that we've been running our women's workshop for the community in New Zealand and this is the second year in Australia. All you need to take with you is a positive attitude, comfortable clothing, a drinks bottle & towel plus something to eat during the breaks. Please note that the workshop takes people out of their comfort zone & can be both physically & mentally demanding at times if unsure seek your doctor's advice before undertaking any form of physical training or have a word with the instructor.

For more details contact Charlie (MINDSET Self Defence & Close Quarters Combat) at:

'It's in the Ballot' takes the format of the Kiwi TV classic 'It's in the Bag' game show and puts a political twist to it.

Contestants of 'It's in the Bag' become political candidates in 'It's in the Ballot' Meet the Candidates.

Candidates choose a numbered box which has a question that has been submitted online by voters before the show.

events.long_description:
After God
From the creators of the wildly praised, fiercely original verbatim plays TRANSMISSION and TRANSMISSION:BETA, the New Zealand premiere of AFTER GOD is a theatrical journey across continents and conversations, with one of Aotearoa’s most distinguished actors, Michael Hurst, joining director Miranda Harcourt and writer Stuart McKenzie to explore big questions about meaning, madness and metaphysics.

With a hungry mind and burning questions, McKenzie hits the road — travelling from Wellington to Kathmandu, London and New York. Along the way, he encounters a vivid cast of real-life characters: theologians, Tibetan rinpoches, philosophers, cosmologists, taxi drivers, hotel receptionists, a famous singing nun — and his own mother. Each has their own radically different way of making sense of existence.

Created entirely from real conversations, AFTER GOD is a new verbatim theatre work, transforming interviews, ideas and personal stories into an exhilarating theatrical experience.

It’s a funny, provocative and hopeful exploration of what we believe, what keeps us going and what it means to be alive right now.

events.long_description:
Blue Moon was alone. With many dreams in her heart. Without a chance to leave home.

Now she’s free, and ready to roam!

Her first order of business is to bring us an elegant evening of heartwarming music. Showcasing a love of the classics, a touch of future classics and an eclectic assortment of Jazz, Blues, Country, Soul, and anything else that makes her feel good inside. Come get cozy with Zeze and her magic mambo mixture of melodic mellifluousness!

Limited seats available! So get in quick!

Z o E M o o N is an Artist with a wealth of songs bursting from her soul. Hawaiian-born, Aotearoa bred: Legends of this fledgling of a musical dynasty’s spellbinding performances have proven to be true. Fresh off her debut solo release ‘Bubbles’ where we hear Zoe’s voice effortlessly glide from resonant low notes to angelic upper registers, and her Duet ‘Sister’ with her real-life big sister Deva Mahal she’s certainly proven to be one to watch and remember.

For Zoe, music is the very fabric that connects and transcends, music is family. Truth-seeking with a keen ear for harmony, a dynamic stage presence and a depth of feeling that must be seen to be believed, she weaves a world of influences into an undulating dance between strength and softness.

After opening for, and singing on the Grammy award-winning TajMo tour, honing her skills touring the world twice over, Zoe comes to us now crystallized by the world stage. Swirling with the experience of performing on stages like North Sea Jazz Festival, Montreux Jazz Festival, Jools Holland show, and even the Hollywood bowl, she is no stranger to putting on a true performance. You may have even seen her alongside longtime friend and partner in crime Estère, or recognize her from local legendary band Brockaflower.

No longer apologising for who she is, where she’s from or what she has to say, treat yourself to an artist who makes every show a captivating memory to treasure.

$20 online, $25 on the door

Part of the Wellington Jazz Festival 2026

Hospital Records’ 30th anniversary celebrations
Hospital Records to Celebrate 30th Anniversary with Hospitality 2026

Hospital Records is one of the most influential labels in dance music and a cornerstone of the drum & bass movement right from its foundational year, is entering its 30th year. To kick off the celebrations, the label has announced its return to NZ on Saturday, 17 October 2026 celebrating three decades of Hospital Records.

For this special anniversary edition, Hospital Records will spotlight a vibrant spectrum of drum & bass talent from across the scene, celebrating the label’s ever-evolving identity across three decades featuring standout performances from DJ DANNY BYRD + Unglued + Hoax set to ignite the stage.

Part of Hospital Records’ global 30th anniversary celebrations. Since its founding in 1996 by Tony Colman and Chris Goss, Hospital Records has grown into the world’s largest independent drum & bass label, recognised for its consistency, creative vision and the strong sense of community at the core of its music and events. Through its flagship brand Hospitality, the label has built a worldwide reputation for high-quality DnB experiences across the world.

events.id: Porirua Parkrun-Bothamley Park, Champion Street, Porirua - Mana-Event Finder
events.name: Porirua Parkrun
events.venue: Bothamley Park, Champion Street, Porirua - Mana
events.long_description:
What is Porirua parkrun? It is a free 5km walk or run event - It’s not about coming first or winning. You can go at your own pace and just enjoy being with other people. It is inclusive and the perfect way to start your weekend in the outdoors chatting to people.

The start occurs just upstream of the Bothamley Park carpark. This car park is off Champion street, opposite the intersection with Windley Street. Head to end of carpark where the concrete ends and there is a gate. For location see https://goo.gl/maps/wEohfp9bRu82.

The course is following the old coach road (circa 1870's) established for the early farms in the area. Today this historic track is located within a park, away from cars and now used by walkers, runners and cyclists.

The track is generally 3 metres wide with a gentle gradient and a compacted gravel surface beside the Kenepuru Stream through a picturesque wooded wild valley. (Note there is a pinch point for a short section after the 2km marker where participants need to go single file each direction for approx 30 metres)

The valley runs east-west with mature trees which means this has to be one of the most sheltered places, out of the wind to exercise in Wellington.

What does it cost to join in? Nothing - it's free! but please register before your first run or walk, so you can get your timing results. You only need to register with parkrun once, to participate at any of the parkrun events around the world. Don't forget to bring a copy of your barcode. If you forget it, you won't get a time.

How fast do I have to be? Walking is fine as long as you can finish the 5km. Please come along and join in whatever your pace!

One dog per adult is welcome, as long as it is on a short hand held lead.

Children welcome but those 10 years and under need to be kept within arms reach of a supervising adult.

Note there is no toilets in the park, so go before you go.

We're friendly! Every week we grab a post park run/walk coffee/tea at Get Fixed within Kai Tahi at 20 Parumoana Street, to mix exercise with socialising.

There are volunteering opportunities even week. So those doing Duke of Edinburgh or similar challenges can get volunteer credits. Ensure you contact us well in advance at "porirua@parkrun.co.nz"

events.long_description:
Overview

A multisport event for kids aged between 4 - 18 years from all around the region.

The kids duathlon is back again for 2026!

We are delighted to have the support of Brancott Estate Vineyard who offer us their beautiful, off-road vineyard setting for the Harcourts Marlborough Kids Duathlon.

Brancott Estate Vineyard, 180 Brancott Road, Fairhall, Blenheim

The Duathlon will operate regardless of weather conditions. The entry fee per child is payable upon registration. You must select what course you want your child to take part in. There are 3 options available this year.

Short Race Run 1km | Bike 3km | Run 1km

Course is open to kids 6-18yrs. You are welcome to walk or run. Choose your course according to your age and fitness level. Please note that distances are approximate.

Long Race Run 2km | Bike 5.5km | Run 1km

Course is open to kids 6-18yrs. You are welcome to walk or run. Choose your course according to your age and fitness level. Please note that distances are approximate.

Beat the Bear 500m walk/run

Course is open to kids 4-7yrs. Parents are welcome to join their child on this one if they wish to support and encourage.

Race Number Collection

We recommend you collect your race number and t-shirt (if you ordered one) before the day, as it will be very busy at the venue.

Race numbers and t-shirts will be available at Bike Fit Marlborough, 24 Market Street, Blenheim on Saturday 17th of October from 10am and 12pm and at the venue on Sunday 18th October between 8:30am – 9am.

Start times

Beat the Bear 9.20am

Short Race 9.40am

Long Race 10.15am

All races will start when previous particpants have finished the course, so times may vary.

We ask that everyone please be present for the briefing which starts at 9:15am at the finish area. All bikes must be ready and in transition by 9.00 am

Drinks and water

To minimise waste and our environmental impact, please bring your own reusable drink bottle. There will be water available to refill your bottle on site.

T Shirts

The 2026 collectors t-shirt is available in sizes 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, adult medium, large and extra large. T-shirts must be pre-ordered and paid at time of entry. T-shirt orders are not available after 30th September 2026.

Entries close

14th October 2026. Limited registrations will be taken on the day. Any entries after 14 October are not eligible for spot prize draws. Entries are strictly limited to 500 and will be accepted on a first-come-first-served basis.

Race briefing and rules

Briefing starts at 9:15am at the Finish area. All participants are eligible for the major spot prizes of a bike and helmet from bike fit. Every race number will go into the draw that we do on the day but participants must be present at prize giving to claim them.

A list of other spot prize winners will be displayed and prizes available for collection at the registration tent. Late entries (after 14th October) are not eligible for minor spot prizes, sorry.

Refunds

We are not able to refund any entry fees after the closing date or t-shirt payments after 30th September 2026.

Quiet the mind, open the heart, and reconnect with our highest self through Kundalini Yoga, breathwork, meditation and sound.

This workshop is part of an 8-part chakra journey across 2026. Each session stands alone or can be experienced as part of the full series.

Join us for an uplifting afternoon as we explore the Crown Chakra (Sahasrara) through the transformative practices of Kundalini Yoga and the deeply restorative sounds of a Gong Bath.

The Crown Chakra is the centre of connection, awareness, peace, and spiritual consciousness. When balanced, it helps us experience a sense of purpose, inner peace, and connection to something greater than ourselves. Through movement, breathwork, meditation, and sound, we'll create space to quiet the mind, open the heart, and reconnect with our highest self.

Experience a 90-minute Kundalini Yoga class designed to activate and balance the Crown Chakra through breathwork (Pranayama), dynamic movement and postures, meditation, and deep relaxation.

☕Herbal Tea Break | 3:00pm – 3:30pm

Take time to relax, enjoy a cup of herbal tea, oracle cards and connect with others in a welcoming and supportive environment.

🎶Gong Bath | 3:30pm – 4:30pm

Lie back, get comfortable, and allow the soothing sounds and vibrations of the gong to guide you into a deeply restorative state of relaxation. A gong bath can help calm the nervous system, release stress, and leave you feeling refreshed and centred.

✨Choose the experience that suits you—you are welcome to attend either the yoga or the gong bath sessions or enjoy the full afternoon.

💫Suitable for beginners and experienced practitioners alike - no experience with yoga or sound healing needed. Modifications are offered throughout the yoga class.

events.long_description:
Crafternoon + Tunes with Eliza
We had such a lovely time sharing craft and music I'm doing it again!
This time lazy Sunday afternoon vibes :)

Key info
- Rock up anytime from 2:30
- Craft supplies provided (or feel free to BYO)
- entertainment starts around 3:30 (songs, poems, traveling bard style)
- Chai and beer on tap till it runs out


The kaupapa for this event is to create a low stakes, high inspiration zone for people to enjoy crafting, connecting and listening.

I often feel inspired to make things while I'm at music gigs and frustrated that I can't put that into action there and then.
This is an opportunity to listen and channel your inspiration into drawing, collaging, clay modeling, kitting, whatever (the craft options are endless!)

If you're not sure what to make or need some help getting started I'll be available to help get the ball rolling from 2:30 - 3:30. I teach creativity for a living so I know everyone is creative, sometimes we just need a little push in the right direction.

It's also chance for me, as a budding musician, to practice performing my songs in a space where there are other offerings for people to enjoy.

FREE event
but any donations towards my upcoming exhibition and workshop series gratefully appreciated.

- I’ll have some zines and prints available to buy too

Crafty friends welcome

Overview

'It's in the Ballot' takes the format of the Kiwi TV classic 'It's in the Bag' game show and puts a political twist to it.

Contestants of 'It's in the Bag' become political candidates in 'It's in the Ballot' Meet the Candidates.

Candidates choose a numbered box which has a question that has been submitted online by voters before the show.

It’s in the Ballot” is a community-led awareness and participation initiative. We aim to increase voter interest in the general and council elections nationally.

By using broadcasting and web-based technologies to deliver in-studio; online on Facebook, YouTube and Twitch; and edited as YouTube videos we aim to enable voters to make informed voting decisions.

This means you can send the weblink of the YouTube Video of your electorate show to your friends and whanau to encourage them to watch the show before they cast their votes.

Enrolments cut off date is Sunday 25th October 2026

Enrol at - https://vote.nz/enrolling/enrol-or-update/enrol-or-update-online

Early voting starts Monday 26th October 2026

Acclaimed Ruawaipu and Ngati Porou dummer-composer Hikurangi Schaverien-Kaa is the 2026 Wellington Jazz Festival commissioned artist. A defining force in Te Whanganui-a-Tara's music community for two decades, he has brought his distinctive voice to stages and studeios across Aotearoa and beyond.

Created especially for the Festival, Te Ao Kohatu draws on the striking claim that while the iwi of Te Tairawhiti arrived on many waka, some also descend from the stones themselves. Wellington, get ready to party with BJÖRN AGAIN!

The only ABBA-endorsed tribute show hits the stage for one spectacular night that is bound to be a Super Trouper celebration of ABBA’s timeless discography.

This internationally acclaimed show brings the glitter, the glam, and all the greatest hits with dazzling energy, spot-on vocals, and outrageous costumes. It’s a full-blown ABBA revival where audiences of all ages can sing, dance, and party like it’s 1979.

Expect all the classics —SOS, Mamma Mia, Dancing Queen, Gimme! Gimme! Gimme! —plus ballads like The Winner Takes It All, Fernando, and Knowing Me, Knowing You, performed with incredible musicianship, a cheeky sense of humour, and that signature Björn Again magic.

With performances in over 120 countries, including The Royal Albert Hall, Wembley Stadium, the Sydney Opera House, and Glastonbury Festival, BJÖRN AGAIN is a global sensation.

Praised by rock royalty and media worldwide —Metalica, Nirvana, Sir Tom Jones, and ABBA themselves – the show has earned glowing reviews:

“Fans better make the most out of Björn Again because that’s the closest they are going to get to seeing ABBA. ABBA will never reform!” – Benny Andersson, ABBA

“One of the most entertaining live shows in the world today.” – Time Out New York

“Fabulously flawless!” – Rolling Stone

Tell your mum, tell your grumpy teenager, tell Fernando – tickets won’t last!

events.long_description:
Overview

The health and safety reforms are coming. If your business hasn't got its head around what that means yet, now is the time.

Critical Conversations with Site Safe CE, Brett Murray

The health and safety reforms are coming, and critical risk management is set to be WorkSafe's number one focus going forward. If your business hasn't got its head around what that means yet, now's the time.




That's why Site Safe Chief Executive Brett Murray is taking to the road this September and October to talk directly with the industry about what's ahead - and how to prepare for it.




This is a free, in-person event for construction and safety professionals across the regions, built around three things we think matter:

· A fireside chat with Brett Murray on the H&S reforms:

As the former head of WorkSafe’s High Hazard Unit, Brett brings an extensive background in health and safety regulation, and he'll walk through what the reforms mean in practice. Brett will focus on the shift towards understanding and managing critical risks, and what that obligation will look like for your business. This will be followed by an open Q&A, so bring your questions.

· A chance to meet your local Site Safe team

Stick around afterwards and take the opportunity to meet your regional manager and your local Site Safe Safety Advisor. These are valuable contacts to have on hand for local health and safety support.

· Food, drinks, and networking

The event is fully catered, with time built in to connect with other safety-minded construction companies in your region.




Spaces are limited, so please register to secure your seat.




Other events:

During this roadshow, Brett will also take Critical Conversations to the following regions. Pass this invitation along to your nationally based colleagues or peers.

Dunedin - Tuesday 15 September

Invercargill - Tuesday 15 September

Queenstown - Wednesday 16 September

Nelson - Wednesday 7 October

Taranaki - Friday 16 October

Palmerston North - Monday 19 October

Hawke's Bay - Tuesday 20 October

Overview

'It's in the Ballot' takes the format of the Kiwi TV classic 'It's in the Bag' game show and puts a political twist to it.

Contestants of 'It's in the Bag' become political candidates in 'It's in the Ballot' Meet the Candidates.

Candidates choose a numbered box which has a question that has been submitted online by voters before the show.

It’s in the Ballot” is a community-led awareness and participation initiative. We aim to increase voter interest in the general and council elections nationally.

By using broadcasting and web-based technologies to deliver in-studio; online on Facebook, YouTube and Twitch; and edited as YouTube videos we aim to enable voters to make informed voting decisions.

This means you can send the weblink of the YouTube Video of your electorate show to your friends and whanau to encourage them to watch the show before they cast their votes.

Enrolments cut off date is Sunday 25th October 2026

Enrol at - https://vote.nz/enrolling/enrol-or-update/enrol-or-update-online

Early voting starts Monday 26th October 2026

Election Day is Saturday 7th November 2026

Agenda


🕑: 06:30 PM - 06:50 PM
Audience and candidates arrive so they are seated by 7pm

🕑: 06:50 PM - 07:00 PM
Candidate briefing and pre-broadcast checks


Info: We check that the technology is working, including those candidates who are attending online.



🕑: 07:00 PM - 08:00 PM
First half of the show


Info: The ‘It's in the Ballot’ host will introduce the local host who joins us to present the questions in the boxes. Each candidate starts with an Opening Statement (1 minute) on why you should give them your electoral and party vote. The candidates choose a numbered box and speaks to the question (1 minute). Candidates are given the same number of questions. Candidates are sent the question sheet 24 hours before the show so they can prepare their responses.



🕑: 08:00 PM - 08:10 PM
Midshow break

🕑: 08:10 PM - 09:00 PM
Second half of the show


Info: Three Hard Hitting questions (1 minute) are answered by all candidates followed by a Closing Statement (1 minute).



🕑: 09:00 PM - 09:30 PM
After show 'meet and greet 'with candidates, hosts and production team


Info: We encourage all attendees to stay after the show to talk to the candidates in person. You may also like to take a photo with the candidates to use on social media to encourage your followers to watch the recorded show before they cast their postal votes from Tuesday 9th September 2025 and must be casted into voting drop box by 12pm Saturday 11th October 2025
