Overview

Learn ways to resolve conflict with customers and co-workers, influence successful outcomes and develop a peaceful workplace.

Transform conflict and difficult situations, people/customers into opportunities by equipping your staff with the skills and techniques required to manage these situations with confidence, professionalism and pride.

We have all experienced the stress that comes from having unresolved conflicts with our customers and co-workers. Conflicts that are ignored or resolved poorly don’t go away, they cause people to feel resentful and to avoid each other. The effects on the business are a loss of productivity, turnover and absenteeism. Wherever two or more people come together, there is bound to be conflict. This workshop will give participants a six-step process that they can use and modify to resolve conflicts of any size. Participants will also learn crucial conflict resolution skills, including dealing with anger and using the Agreement Frame.


Learning Outcomes:

Transform conflict into opportunity
Develop constructive strategies for dealing with difficult behavior
Develop communication skills to diffuse the situation
Increase confidence and assertiveness in dealing with difficult behaviour
Manage your emotions and deal with stress
Understand the power of words and how to use them to your advantage


For more information or to book: email info@biztrainers.co.nz or call 04 974 8790

events.long_description:
Overview

Decode your mind through the Enneagram and discover new ways to understand yourself, navigate differences and deepen your relationships.

Inspire me workshops




The Blueprint of the Mind- understanding yourself through the Enneagram




You may know the situation when your partner, friend, boss or spouse does things or says things where you might wonder how this person could ever say/do things like that, because it's completely opposite of how you would handle the exact same situation.

The result of it is often endless frustration, disappointment, misunderstandings and many more emotional disturbances due to seeing the world fundamentally different from other persons that we're dealing with.

If we, however get a better understanding of the core mentality, fears and desires of different types of people that are in our environment incl our own triggers and blinds pots, dealing with people will be so much easier and it will lay the foundation for much more meaningful and deep relationships.

In this workshop we'll discover different aspects of the Enneagram, which is an ancient map of nine personality types - nine different core motivations and fears that quietly shape how we think, feel and react in our day to day life.
If you want to understand your own strengths and points of improvements while also being able to relate to the people in your environment better, come to our workshop

End the session on a high note with a delicious plant-based dinner, dessert, and good conversation.
Meet your host Gopi

Gopi helps spiritually minded professionals achieve clarity, overcome negative thought patterns and habits through his unique integration of hypnotherapy and palmistry. During his former life as a monk, he delved into the timeless wisdom of astrology, palmistry, and the ancient knowledge of the mind and consciousness, gaining deep insights into human psychology. He combines these powerful teachings with modern, effective tools as a certified practitioner in applied hypnotherapy, trauma informed coach, along with the knowledge he gained through his diploma in psychology and counseling.

Inspire me workshops The Blueprint of the Mind- understanding yourself through the Enneagram You may know the situation when your partner, friend, boss or spouse does things or says things where you might wonder how this person could ever say/do things like that, because it's completely opposite of how you would handle the exact same situation.
The result of it is often endless frustration, disappointment, misunderstandings and many more emotional disturbances due to seeing the world fundamentally different from other persons that we're dealing with.
If we, however get a better understanding of the core mentality, fears and desires of different types of people that are in our environment incl our own triggers and blinds pots, dealing with people will be so much easier and it will lay the foundation for much more meaningful and deep relationships.
If you want to understand your own strengths and points of improvements while also being able to relate to the people in your environment better, come to our workshop End the session on a high note with a delicious plant-based dinner, dessert, and good conversation.
Meet your host Gopi Gopi helps spiritually minded professionals achieve clarity, overcome negative thought patterns and habits through his unique integration of hypnotherapy and palmistry.

events.long_description:
Take a walk back in time to enjoy some of the most famous music of the 60s and 70s. Creedence Clearwater Revival was a juggernaut of phenomenal proportions. From their album debut in 1968 to their last album in 1972 the band produced some highly memorable songs. Many of them are still regularly played today. The Creedence Clearwater Collective recreates the success of the original band. The St James Theatre stage in Wellington will come alive with a six-piece tribute band. There’ll be a guest saxophonist and a vocalist who emulates the distinct sounds of original vocalist John Fogerty. 
The night promises to be full of iconic tunes including songs they wrote and songs they covered. Listen to hits like Have You Ever Seen The Rain, Fortunate Son, Bad Moon Rising, and Proud Mary.

A perfect next step for those who've done an intro course this year, want to give narrative improv a go, or are looking for a refresher on the basics of character and narrative.

This 6 week course runs 6:30-8:30pm on Wednesdays from October 21st to November 25th. Classes will be at the Toi Aro Arts Centre at 3 Market Lane, Te Aro.

Save 10% by booking early. Early bird registration is available until October 31st.

ABOUT THE TEACHERS

TARA MCENTEE has been improvising professionally for more than 15 years and has trained and performed with Improsaurus, The Court Jesters, Playshop and PopRox Improv! She's taught improv all over Aotearoa, and has a passion for narrative improv based on strong characters. She has been described as "a chaotic evil" improviser.

AUSTIN HARRISON is one of Aotearoa's most experienced improvisers and teachers with over 15 years experience. He holds a Master of Fine Arts in Theatre from Victoria University of Wellington and is the current Artistic Director of the New Zealand Improv Festival.

Austin believes improv is a powerful connector which builds communities, boosts confidence and reminds us all how to have fun. He's taught improv in a variety of environments, from intermediate schools, right through to over-65s classes. He's an award-winning performer and producer, a founding member of PopRox Improv and has taken shows to the Edinburgh Fringe and Melbourne International Comedy Festival.

THE STAND-BY LIST
PopRox firmly believes that improv is for everyone, especially when it comes to sharing skills and knowledge. So we're offering "the stand-by list" for all our workshops in 2026. We'll giveaway any spots remaining the week before this course, on a first-come-first-serve basis. No need to provide a reason, no questions asked. If the registration fee is a barrier for you to come along, then simply email and we'll pop you on the SBL. Everyone on the list will be notified whether there was a place available for them at least 5 days before the course begins.

Now Hear This (Wellington)
Award-winning political satirist Sameena Zehra. Columnist and three-time Test the Nation winner Raybon Kan. 2025 NZ Comedy Festival breakout Mo Munn.

Part of James Nokise's 2026 election tour.

Some say art shouldn't be political. This show isn't that. A lineup of comedians with short, sharp political takes — Now Hear This offers a night where the audience can enjoy comedy that's specifically, unapologetically political.

Not every comedian is a political comedian, but most have some pretty funny opinions on the state of the world. This celebration of speaking truth to power is as much an outlet for the performers as it is for the audience.

Hosted by Sameena Zehra, featuring Raybon Kan, Mo Munn, Orin Ruaine-Prattley and James Nokise.

You've read Raybon Kan going from lawyer to the country's funniest columnist over 31 years. You've watched Sameena Zehra hold power to account from Edinburgh to here. And you'll want to catch Mo Munn now, while she's still the Comedy Festival's reigning Spirit of the Festival winner — reviewers say she "draws laughs instead of blood." Now hear all three, plus Orin Ruaine-Prattley and James Nokise, in one room.

—

"The cheapest group therapy session you'll find this election season." — A Concerned Constituent, seeking professional help (allegedly)

—

THE DETAILS
The Hannah, Wellington
Wed 21 October, 8pm.
Early bird $35, then $40 general admission from 11 September. Door sales $45. Booking fees apply.
Adult themes, coarse language, and political satire throughout. Recommended 16+.
Full tour dates and more info at jamesnokise.com

Overview

Unwind with slow Yin Yoga and soothing sound, creating a peaceful evening of deep relaxation, stillness and restoration.

Yin Yoga & Somatic Sound




A nurturing evening of slow, restorative Yin Yoga accompanied by the soothing sounds of singing bowls and handpan.

Through gentle, supported poses and calming sound vibrations, you’ll be invited to soften the body, quiet the mind, and settle into a deeper state of relaxation.




Please note our events now start at 6pm. Please try to arrive by 545pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.

Please stay for a delicious plant-based dinner and dessert afterwards, included in your ticket!

Meet Your Host: Lynn

Lynn Tiang is an Integrative Somatic Coach, breathwork facilitator, and Reiki practitioner based in Aotearoa, New Zealand. Her work combines somatic breathwork, Yoga, Reiki, and life coaching to support nervous system regulation, emotional wellbeing, and grounded personal transformation in a practical, trauma-aware way.

Meet Your Host: Alexandra

Alexandra is a sound healing practitioner devoted to nurturing healing in both mind and body. She believes that sound vibration holds the power to expand consciousness and restore harmony and balance in our lives. Her journey into sound healing began with the realization of how deeply sound vibration was affecting her psyche, making her more mindful of the music she listens to and the intention it carries. Along the way, she has drawn inspiration from Bhakti Lounge Kirtan. Their music has profoundly influenced her own sound healing practice, inspiring her to explore sound as a tool for transformation, connection, and inner peace.

Meet your host, Kim:

Kim Andrews is a Wellington-based musician, percussionist and drum teacher with a background in jazz performance and a deep love of music as a space for connection and presence.

A lifelong rhythm-maker, Kim has more recently been exploring the handpan, drawn to its warm, resonant sound and meditative qualities. Their love of music sits alongside a long-standing interest in meditation and mindfulness, and a curiosity for the places where music, stillness and connection meet.

events.id: 100 Years of Unity through Sport — New Zealand and India-Frank Kitts Park, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: 100 Years of Unity through Sport — New Zealand and India
events.venue: Frank Kitts Park, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
This spring, Wellington will celebrate 100 years of sporting connection between India and New Zealand. The city will showcase its strong Indian community and cultural connections. This century milestone traces back to 1926, when an Indian Army hockey team toured New Zealand for the first time, bringing players and communities together. Since then, sport has played an important role in connecting our countries — notably through hockey and cricket, but also across many other sports and exchanges. 

From 23 October to 15 November, Frank Kitts Park and the waterfront promenade will host a free public exhibition. Light Box Historic Walk will feature 10 illuminated light boxes that share stories of Wellington-specific links between India and New Zealand. You’ll also find The Fan Hub on 6 and 7 November as well as 14 and 15 November. Enjoy a feast with local food truck favourites, offering a taste of Wellington's rich culinary scene. Or start the day with sunrise yoga sessions hosted by AWHI Yoga against the stunning waterfront backdrop. To cap off all the excitement, the BLACKCAPS take on India three times in Wellington as part of their summer season.

The Sport100 Fan Hub is proudly delivered through collaboration between WellingtonNZ, Sport New Zealand, Wellington City Council, Cricket Wellington, and New Zealand Cricket, creating a festive gathering place for locals and visitors to connect, celebrate, and enjoy the atmosphere whilst Wellington hosts cricketing giants India in the capital.

events.long_description:
The Jackson Street Quest!
This Festival event runs from the 24 October to the 15 November 2026.


Have fun and learn at the same time! Go on a quest to discover historic Jackson Street, and bring the family / whanau along with you.

Go on a Quest (scavenger hunt) along Jackson Street, exploring our history, searching for clues about the area’s shops, industries, sport, and the people who helped build the community.
Especially designed with our younger citizens in mind, however, those young at heart are welcome to go on the quest too!
As each clue is solved, you discover how Jackson Street grew to become the heart of the lively historic neighbourhood it is today.

• Download the sheet of quest clues: www.jacksonstreet.co.nz
• OR pick up a sheet from the Historic Police Station (Mon-Thurs, 9am-1pm)
• OR pick up a sheet from Bin Inn Petone, 211 Jackson Street (open 7 days per week)

• Start from the Historic Police Station, 274B Jackson Street
• Bring a pen
• The Quest can be done anytime of the day
• Takes approx. 45 minutes

For those 4-9yrs & 10yrs + :
When you have completed the Quest, return your sheet (with your contact details) to the black entry box by the front door of the Historic Police Station to go into a draw to win prizes!

Cost: Free

Learn more on our website:
https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/event/the-jackson-street-quest/

This event is part of the 2026 Wellington Heritage Festival, running 24th October - 15th November. Discover over 160 more events on our website:
https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/events/

Health & Safety:
Children need to be supervised by an adult at all times due to the busy nature of Jackson Street's road.

events.long_description:
Ka Mua, Ka Muri - Te Motu Kairangi
This exhibition looks at the early history of the Miramar Peninsula through the lens of estate agent and amateur archaeologist H. N. McLeod.

Hector McLeod stood atop the Miramar Cutting in 1910, on the site of the historic Maupuia Pā. The photograph he captured there and his subsequent annotations, notes, and articles on Māori local histories will be on display in Tō Tātou Pōneke, our new heritage space at Te Matapihi | Wellington Central Library. The exhibit will also explore the development of Miramar as a suburb, and McLeod's own brief time as Mayor of the Borough.

Cost: Free

Learn more on our website:

Ōrongomai Tū Tonu
In August 2026, Ōrongomai Marae marks 50 years in Upper Hutt with an exhibition that brings together the people, moments, and movements that made it possible.

From the bold decision to establish a marae in the heart of a growing city, this exhibition traces how Ōrongomai came into being. It celebrates the visionaries, builders, and cultural leaders who shaped its foundation, including the powerful legacy of Mā-wai-hakona, whose performances carried Ōrongomai onto national and international stages.

At its heart, this is a story of belonging: how a community created a place for itself, and how that place continues to serve, welcome, and grow. Ōrongomai Tū Tonu invites you to experience a living history and the people who continue to shape it.

Join us and learn more about this beautiful town!

🌺 Bienvenue en Nouvelle-Calédonie ! Just a few hours' flight from Aotearoa, this little piece of France in the Pacific is a world of its own: turquoise water, red earth, pine-covered islands and a rich mix of cultures you won't find anywhere else.

Join Djena for a fun and immersive workshop (en français !) and dive into the island's story. You'll learn about its history, from the Kanak people who first settled it to the arrival of James Cook and the French. You'll tour the must-see spots, from Nouméa's beaches to the Centre culturel Tjibaou. And you'll pick up some Caledonian expressions that will surprise even French speakers 😉

And of course, we'll finish on a sweet note with a tasting of poé citrouille, a pumpkin and coconut dessert loved across the Pacific, plus a few surprises! 🥥

🗯️ French A2/B1 level required
🗓️ Saturday, 24 October 2026, 10.30am–12pm
📍 Alliance Française Wellington (78 Victoria Street, Wellington)
🎟️ $30 for AF members & $35 for non-members

events.long_description:
Circa Theatre Behind the Scenes Tour
Discover the 50-year history of Circa Theatre with a 1-hour guided tour of Wellington’s foyer and backstage area at this historical building on the waterfront.

As a leader of arts and culture in Wellington, Circa Theatre brings quality playwriting and performance to the Capital's glorious waterfront. Discover and celebrate the 50-year history of Wellington’s iconic Circa Theatre with a 1-hour guided tour of Wellington’s foyer and backstage area at this historical building on the waterfront.
You will be taken on a unique guided tour of this historic building, including the back of house, which is usually actors only! Learn about the fascinating building move from 7 Harris Street to 1 Taranaki Street – including how the facade of 120-year-old Westport Chambers was trucked across the road and the new theatre built in behind it.

Booking is REQUIRED for this event.
Cost: Free, koha welcome

Learn more and book on our website:

https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/events/

Health & Safety:
Walking tour with stairs to the upper floor. Working theatre, can include moving props and people. Please wear good shoes and dress for the weather. The tour may be cancelled in bad weather.

events.long_description:
Upside Down! Inversion Workshop with Kathleen Kuehn
We get our hearts above our head in this workshop focused on inverted postures - think headstand, handstand and forearm stand! It'll be playful, strong but accessible with loads of options, technique and practice for everyone present.

We'll prep the body for these poses first, then move into the mechanics of each before giving them a go. Expect individualised attention, specific cueing and optional hands-on assists (with consent) to get you upside down!

You'll also get some great takeaway exercises to work on at home if you want to continue the inversion journey!

Why inversions?

Inversions have a host of benefits: they can improve circulation, lymphatic drainage and mental focus; build strength; stimulate digestion and more! But most of all, they're just a lot of fun!

Who is this for?
This workshop is suitable for most levels of practice; you don't need to be an expert, but you'll want at least a few asana classes under your belt. That said, everything you need to know will be offered on the day!

CYTs can also earn 3 CE credits with Yoga Alliance.

This workshop will be capped to keep it manageable -- enrol now so you don't miss out!

About the Facilitator

Kathleen Kuehn (E-RYT 500) who enjoys playful vinyasa classes, challenging asana and stringing them together in creative ways. Anatomy and alignment lover. Can't actually do a handstand herself, but can 100% talk you into getting into (and falling out of!) one yourself in a safe way!

Save $10 with Early Bird Rego by 26 Sept!

events.long_description:
Erskine Chapel Open Day
See the splendid beauty of Erskine Chapel (Sacré Coeur), tucked away in the hills of Island Bay.

Erskine Chapel is an iconic Category 1-listed French Gothic chapel, a sentinel of older times. Located in the core of the former Erskine College building, the chapel’s interior is of great significance.

In 2023, significant strengthening and restoration works were completed on the chapel, including the west façade and entrance, major steel structural upgrades, and a new roof. The chapel is located on the first level, where the restoration reaches a full crescendo of white arched ceilings lit by stained glass. No effort was spared to return the interiors to their original beauty, despite a decade of severe neglect.

Erskine Chapel won the heritage category of the Te Kāhui Whaihanga New Zealand Institute of Architects (NZIA) 2024 Awards, highlighting the work of Tobin Smith of Common Architecture and Adam Wild of Archifact Architecture & Conservation Heritage.

Mark this date in your calendar now and experience the chapel's charm and restored beauty.

Cost: Entry to chapel by Koha for ongoing chapel maintenance.

Learn more on our website:
https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/event/erskine-chapel/

This event is part of the 2026 Wellington Heritage Festival, running 24th October - 15th November. Discover over 160 more events on our website:
https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/events/

Health & Safety:
Please park on nearby streets. Only vehicles with accessibility needs are allowed entry to the complex.
For those driving through, please drive slowly and remain watchful for children and pets.
When leaving the chapel, check for cars. Do not walk on the road and keep to the left of Avon Street.
The lift swings outwards. Please avoid standing within the yellow marked lines.

events.long_description:
Overview

Bruno Groening's legacy continues to inspire people today through the ongoing activities of the Bruno Groening Circle of Friends.

Documentary Film: The Phenomenon of Healing

In the 1950s, Bruno Groening gained international attention as a spiritual figure whose words and presence left a profound impression on thousands. When he passed away in 1959, many thought the movement around him would come to an end — but instead, it continued to grow.

The Phenomenon of Healing is a powerful documentary that follows the journey of the Bruno Groening Circle of Friends, a global community that carries on his Teaching to this day. Through compelling personal interviews, rare archival footage and commentary from healthcare professionals, this three-part documentary film shows how Bruno Groening's legacy continues to inspire people today - regardless of faith, belief, nationality or culture. Through this, many have experienced emotional and physical well-being, as well as a renewed sense of purpose in their lives.

Whether you're curious about spirituality, exploring personal growth, or interested in the historical context of healing traditions, this film offers a fresh and engaging perspective. Everyone is welcome to attend.

Admission is free – voluntary donations are appreciated.

When: Saturday 3 October 2026

Time: 1:00pm to 7:00pm (Includes 2 breaks)

Where: Quaker Hall, 7 Moncrieff Street, Mt Victoria, Wellington

Contact: Anouk - 0210627762 | brunogroeningnz@gmail.com

More information about the film: www.bruno-groening-film.org

Visit our website: www.bruno-groening.org/en

---------------------------

Please note: This film and event are intended for informational purposes only. The personal experiences shared in the film reflect the views and stories of individuals and do not constitute medical advice. No diagnosis, treatment, or healing outcomes are offered or guaranteed. Always seek guidance from a qualified healthcare professional for medical concerns.

events.long_description:
Colourful Enamel Jewellery Day
Learn to create beautiful enamelled jewellery with Lisa Sinclair.

Join us for a full-day enamelling workshop where you’ll explore colour, texture, and fire to create vibrant enamelled jewellery in copper or silver.

This hands-on class focuses on the fundamentals of enamelling, showing you how to apply, fire, and layer enamel to achieve rich, expressive surfaces. You’ll make a simple yet beautifully textured pendant or pair of earrings, then learn how to add a pop (or flood!) of colour to bring your piece to life.

Beginners to metalwork are very welcome - pre-formed shapes are available so you can focus on experimenting with colour, pattern, and mark-making. If you have some metalworking experience, you’re encouraged to take things further by creating and texturing your own metal forms before enamelling.

This is a playful, creative workshop and an ideal class for anyone who loves working with colour, surface, and experimentation - whether you’re new to enamels or keen to deepen your skills.

What you’ll learn:
The basics of enamelling on copper and silver
How to prepare metal for enamelling
Applying enamel using different techniques
Firing enamel and building up layers of colour
Creating texture and pattern in metal
Tips for achieving clean, vibrant enamel finishes

The class fee covers enamel materials but NOT metals. Students can choose from a range of pre-cut copper blanks or use their own copper sheet. Findings and chains are available to purchase at a range of good prices to suit all budgets.

Kids aged approximately 12+ are welcome. Any participant under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

For health and safety reasons, students must wear sturdy closed-toe shoes.

Workshop fee $248, early bird $225 till 28 Sept.

events.name: Rita Angus Cottage open day
events.venue: 194A Sydney St W, Thorndon, Wellington 6011
events.long_description:
Rita Angus Cottage open day
You are invited to come and sketch in the garden at Rita Angus' historic cottage.

The garden at the Rita Angus Cottage (Category 1 Historic Place) will be open to visitors, who are encouraged to stay and sketch the abundant array of flowers and plant life that surround the 1877 cottage where New Zealand artist Rita Angus lived between 1955 and 1970, providing her with much inspiration and subject matter.

Rita Angus Cottage Trustees and volunteer gardeners will be on hand, with drawing material and reproductions of some of Rita’s representations of her Thorndon garden. Some materials will be provided. You are also welcome to bring along your own pens, pencils, pastels and watercolours – and perhaps a picnic.

The house continues as a studio for an artist-in-residence programme and is a part of the legacy that Rita Angus has left to contemporary New Zealand Art.

Cost: Koha

Learn more on our website:
https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/event/rita-angus-cottage-open-day/

This event is part of the 2026 Wellington Heritage Festival, running 24th October - 15th November. Discover over 160 more events on our website:
https://wellingtonheritagefestival.co.nz/events/

Banner image note: Rita Angus Cottage Trust, 2018

events.long_description:
For many of us, music can be like a drug. At first everything and anything feels and is beyond amazing, but over time as our consumption increases, this magical euphoria wears off to a hollow and crushing emptiness. The now discerning music addict desperately searches for that new thing that will make them feel the high that they once had. But it gets harder to again feel this way. Until they stumble across something so unique, original, and idiosyncratic they cannot help but feel giddy, childish excitement.

OvO are one of those bands. Curiously infuriating yet dangerously exhilarating in their inability to be pigeon hold into genre or specific sound. Deftly navigating between noise rock, doom, extreme and blackened metal, industrial sludge and even electronica. “Decibel Magazine” have perhaps described them best by hailing the bands sound as “a David Lynch dance party”. Italy’s OvO, continue to rewrite the definition of what alternative music can be. Something which New Zealand audiences can look forward to seeing this October 2026.

Formed by Stefania Pedretti and Bruno Dorella in Milan, Italy in the late 90s. OvO have taken their inspiration from the likes of Suicide, Swans, and Diamana Galas. Centred around the ear piercing banshee-like vocals of Stefania, and a constant guitar drone and dark menace as the undercurrent of their songs. Bruno, equally essential in their music, pounds a stripped down drum-set as if he were the leader of an invading war party. Coupled with intensive percussion samples to help craft a unique and experimental sound.

With 25 years as a band, 11 albums behind them (including their most recent Gemma), over 1000 shows/festivals across the globe, and sharing stages with many of the biggest names in experimental music; Godflesh, Lightning Bolt, Thurston Moore, Sleepytime Gorilla Music, Psychic TV, Dillinger Escape Plan, Big Brave, Ufomammut, among others - New Zealand audiences have their chance to see one of the most unique and experienced bands still active.

New Jersey hell-raisers Lorna Shore make their first-ever appearance in New Zealand this October. For the past 15 years, the band has pushed beyond the confines of the heavy band genre. Since forming in 2009, Lorna Shore has evolved into a powerhouse of intense brutality and melodic sorcery. To the mainstream, their signature brand of deathcore has become infamous. Their 2020 album ‘Immortal’, along with the guttural vocal acrobatics of vocalist Will Ramos, has catapulted the group beyond cult status and into global renown. 
Lorna Shore offer the ultimate meeting point between unbridled catharsis, raw emotion, searing sonic aggression and cinematic beauty. Their fifth studio album, 2025’s ‘I Feel The Everblack Festering Within Me’, continues to galvanise a significant fanbase. For the Wellington show at Shed 6, they will be joined by fellow American heavy hitters in The Acacia Strain and local New Zealand death metallers Organectomy.

events.name: Understanding and Supporting Your Neurodivergent Child: A Practical Parent Course
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
This course is designed for parents and caregivers of neurodivergent tamariki who want practical, evidence-informed strategies to better support their child’s wellbeing, behaviour, and participation at home and school.
Across three sessions, we will explore the foundations of neurodiversity, including different neurotypes, strengths-based perspectives, and neuroaffirming language. You will gain insight into sensory processing, regulation, and the critical role of connection and co-regulation in supporting your child.
The course also provides guidance on navigating Aotearoa New Zealand’s health, education, and disability systems, including how to access supports and advocate effectively for your child. We will explore common challenges such as school refusal, burnout, and meltdowns, with practical strategies for prevention, in-the-moment support, and recovery.
There will be opportunities for discussion, reflection, and shared learning, as well as a Q&A-style panel session incorporating both professional and lived experience perspectives.
This is a group-based learning environment (not individual therapy), with an emphasis on practical tools, connection, and empowerment.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.id: LA DISPUTE - NO ONE WAS DRIVING THE CAR AOTEAROA TOUR - WELLINGTON-Valhalla, Wellington-Valhalla
events.name: LA DISPUTE - NO ONE WAS DRIVING THE CAR AOTEAROA TOUR - WELLINGTON
events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
The post-hardcore innovators of La Dispute, known for their emotionally charged lyrics and ambitious compositions, are hitting Aotearoa this October. These shows will celebrate their critically acclaimed fifth studio album, No One Was Driving The Car.
It’s been six years since La Dispute released their last album, Panorama. Since then, the Michigan post-hardcore band—made up of Jordan Dreyer on vocals, Brad Vander Lugt on drums, Chad Morgan-Sterenberg and Corey Stroffolino on guitar, and Adam Vass on bass—dealt with the stagnance of the pandemic, celebrated the ten-year anniversaries of Wildlife and Rooms Of The House, and began working on No One Was Driving The Car. The fifth studio LP is the first entirely produced by the group, and it came together in Grand Rapids and Detroit, the United Kingdom, Australia, and the Philippines: “I think the change in environment was really helpful to breathing new life into the process each time we came back to it,” Dreyer says.
Partly inspired by the 2017 psychological thriller First Reformed, No One Was Driving The Car reckons with malaise in the shadow of the looming apocalypse, which has noticeably been worsened by the advancement of tech. The title comes from a quote from a police officer Dreyer read in a news article about a lethal self-driving Tesla crash, an absurd event which raises questions about the amount of control we have in our own lives. In fourteen dynamic tracks, the band grapples with the existential topic and the human need to find comfort and a sense of security in an existence where we’re often thrust into chaos without permission. Dreyer yells with a more primal sense and sings in a more refined way, and the guitars have a sharper edge than ever before. “As much as I don’t enjoy the creative process because it’s taxing and often not fun, I also think it’s the most fun that I ever have,” Dreyer contemplates. “It’s the revelations you make, the breakthroughs. It’s banging your head against a wall and suddenly something clicks in a way that feels almost divine, like it came from somewhere else.”

events.long_description:
Shea McAleese: The Evolution of a Four-Time Olympian
What does it take to perform on the world's biggest stage?

And perhaps more importantly, what happens when the cheering stops, the jersey comes off, and it's time to reinvent yourself all over again?

Join four-time Olympian and New Zealand hockey legend Shea McAleese for an inspiring Learning Lunch exploring the highs, challenges and lessons of a life spent pursuing excellence.

From a young Hawke's Bay athlete with a dream to representing New Zealand at four Olympic Games and four Commonwealth Games, Shea's journey offers a fascinating insight into commitment, resilience and what it really takes to perform at an elite level.

But this isn't simply a story about sport.

It's about leadership, teamwork, personal growth and learning how to evolve through different chapters of life.

Today, Shea works as an international coach and leadership mentor, helping individuals and teams perform at their best. Drawing on lessons from elite sport, he shares a practical and human perspective on building trust, developing culture and creating environments where people thrive.

Expect honest stories, valuable insights and a fascinating look behind the scenes of life as an Olympian, coach and leader.

Meet Shea 🎤

Shea McAleese is one of New Zealand's most celebrated hockey players and a proud son of Hawke's Bay. Over a 16-year international career he represented the Black Sticks 320 times, competing at four Olympic Games and four Commonwealth Games. Since retiring from international hockey, he has transitioned into international coaching and leadership development, working with elite teams and building a global following through his coaching platform, Inside Hockey.

What We'll Explore
• The realities of competing at four Olympic Games
• Lessons from elite sport that apply to everyday life
• Leadership, trust and building high-performing teams
• The transition from athlete to coach
• Resilience, growth and adapting through life's different chapters

events.id: LA DISPUTE - NO ONE WAS DRIVING THE CAR AOTEAROA TOUR - AUCKLAND-Valhalla, Wellington-Valhalla
events.name: LA DISPUTE - NO ONE WAS DRIVING THE CAR AOTEAROA TOUR - AUCKLAND
events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
The post-hardcore innovators of La Dispute, known for their emotionally charged lyrics and ambitious compositions, are hitting Aotearoa this October. These shows will celebrate their critically acclaimed fifth studio album, No One Was Driving The Car.

It’s been six years since La Dispute released their last album, Panorama. Since then, the Michigan post-hardcore band—made up of Jordan Dreyer on vocals, Brad Vander Lugt on drums, Chad Morgan-Sterenberg and Corey Stroffolino on guitar, and Adam Vass on bass—dealt with the stagnance of the pandemic, celebrated the ten-year anniversaries of Wildlife and Rooms Of The House, and began working on No One Was Driving The Car. The fifth studio LP is the first entirely produced by the group, and it came together in Grand Rapids and Detroit, the United Kingdom, Australia, and the Philippines: “I think the change in environment was really helpful to breathing new life into the process each time we came back to it,” Dreyer says.

Partly inspired by the 2017 psychological thriller First Reformed, No One Was Driving The Car reckons with malaise in the shadow of the looming apocalypse, which has noticeably been worsened by the advancement of tech. The title comes from a quote from a police officer Dreyer read in a news article about a lethal self-driving Tesla crash, an absurd event which raises questions about the amount of control we have in our own lives. In fourteen dynamic tracks, the band grapples with the existential topic and the human need to find comfort and a sense of security in an existence where we’re often thrust into chaos without permission. Dreyer yells with a more primal sense and sings in a more refined way, and the guitars have a sharper edge than ever before. “As much as I don’t enjoy the creative process because it’s taxing and often not fun, I also think it’s the most fun that I ever have,” Dreyer contemplates. “It’s the revelations you make, the breakthroughs. It’s banging your head against a wall and suddenly something clicks in a way that feels almost divine, like it came from somewhere else.”

This event is at Hollywood Avondale in Auckland

Tickets here

events.venue: Meow Nui, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
DUE TO OVERWHELMING DEMAND, MUDHONEY HAS UPGRADED VENUES TO MEOW NUI.
For the first time in over a decade, Mudhoney return to New Zealand for a run of intimate shows. Renowned for their ferocious live performances, the band continue to deliver the same high-voltage mix of sludgy riffs, pounding rhythms and Mark Arm's unmistakable snarl that made them one of the most influential rock bands of their era.
Formed in Seattle in 1988, Mudhoney helped define the sound that would become known as grunge, combining garage rock, punk and heavy distortion into something raw, loud and entirely their own. As one of the cornerstone acts of legendary independent label Sub Pop, the band became a crucial influence on the explosion of alternative rock that followed, with tracks like 'Touch Me I'm Sick' and 'Suck You Dry' remaining enduring underground classics.
More than 35 years on, Mudhoney remain as vital as ever, continuing to release acclaimed new music and proving night after night why they are regarded as one of the greatest live rock bands of their generation.
"When it comes to grunge, or even just Seattle, I think there was one band that made the definitive music of the time. It wasn't us or Nirvana, but Mudhoney. Nirvana delivered it to the world, but Mudhoney were the band of that time and sound." – Eddie Vedder (Pearl Jam)
A rare chance to experience genuine grunge royalty up close.

Overview

Discover the key numbers that drive profit and learn how to maximise your returns without working harder.

More work does not always mean more profit

You can have a full calendar, a busy team and plenty of sales coming through the door—and still wonder where the profit has gone.

Often, the issue is not how much work the business is doing.

It is the type of work, the customers being served, the costs that quietly blow out, and whether pricing reflects the true value being delivered.

Profit: Find Your Sweet Spot is a practical 90-minute session designed to help local business owners identify the numbers and decisions that have the greatest effect on profit.

During the session, we will look at:

Which customers, products or job types make you the most money
Which parts of the business may be consuming time without producing enough return
Where time, materials, discounts, stock, rework or debtor costs may be blowing out
Simple ways to protect your margin when unexpected costs arise
How to deliver more value to your best customers
Where pricing may need to be reviewed or better aligned

You will leave with a clearer picture of your business’s profit sweet spot and one practical action you can begin applying immediately.

This is not about working harder, chasing every possible sale or making dramatic changes overnight.

It is about understanding what is already happening inside your business and making more deliberate decisions about where your time, people and resources go.

Who should attend?

This session is suitable for owners of trades, retail, wholesale, manufacturing, professional service and other locally owned businesses.

Event details

Date: 30 October 
Time: 10:30 am–12:00 pm 
Venue: Paraparaumu Beach Golf Club 
Cost: Free

Places are limited, so please register early.

Overview

Discover how your nervous system shapes your habits and learn practical tools to create lasting change and thrive.

Wired to thrive: regulate & rise




Events now start at 6pm. Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.




How might we shift from who we are to who we want to be?

Join this 75-minute practical introductory workshop to get under the hood of what’s really running the show: your nervous system and your neuromodulators.

You’ll learn about serotonin and dopamine, what they do, why they matter, and how understanding them can help you make more supportive choices and shape the life you want.

You’ll explore practical, body-based tools drawn from somatic wisdom, neuroscience and polyvagal theory, with a focus on turning knowledge into habits you can actually use.

Walk away with 5 practical tools you can start using immediately, because theory alone isn’t enough.

And because the real value comes from putting knowledge into practice, you’ll also receive access to a special online community for the month of November, where you’ll take part in the Wired to Thrive 21-Day Challenge.

You’ll receive:

A simple 1-page habit tracker
Daily prompts to help you put the tools into practice
Q&A and ongoing support throughout the challenge
A community of like-minded people
Accountability and encouragement along the way
A reflection and celebration call at the end

Set yourself up for a thriving summer season.




Event followed by a plant-based dinner and dessert, all included in your ticket!
Meet your host, Freda:

I’m a mum, yoga teacher, retreat host, somatic therapy student, ocean swimmer, connector, curator and founder of Goodlife Collective.

Growing up surrounded by the mountains and ocean in Nelson, I’ve always been drawn to nature, connection and wellbeing. I discovered yoga at 18 in a 400-year-old church in Belgium, where, despite not understanding the French, I experienced a profound sense of calm and presence.

My travels, Psychology studies and own journey into health and healing shaped my passion for inner development, holistic wellbeing and creating spaces for meaningful connection. I completed my 200YTT with Nico Luce in 2019 and founded Goodlife Collective to help unlock our collective potential through connection, possibility and hope.

events.long_description:
Mudhoney │Wellington
For the first time in over a decade, Mudhoney return to New Zealand for a run of intimate shows. Renowned for their ferocious live performances, the band continue to deliver the same high-voltage mix of sludgy riffs, pounding rhythms and Mark Arm's unmistakable snarl that made them one of the most influential rock bands of their era.

Formed in Seattle in 1988, Mudhoney helped define the sound that would become known as grunge, combining garage rock, punk and heavy distortion into something raw, loud and entirely their own. As one of the cornerstone acts of legendary independent label Sub Pop, the band became a crucial influence on the explosion of alternative rock that followed, with tracks like 'Touch Me I'm Sick' and 'Suck You Dry' remaining enduring underground classics.

More than 35 years on, Mudhoney remain as vital as ever, continuing to release acclaimed new music and proving night after night why they are regarded as one of the greatest live rock bands of their generation.

A rare chance to experience genuine grunge royalty up close.

events.long_description:
Power Up Central Hutt
Come to the first of the new 2026 Power Up The Hutt information sessions in the Hutt Bowling Club, Myrtle Street on the evening of Thursday 29th October at 7:30pm.

Power Up the Hutt is a free five-part community event series bringing together Hutt Valley residents who want to cut their power bills, reduce their carbon footprint, and future-proof their homes.

New Zealand has reached an electrification tipping point — households can now save money and significantly reduce their emissions by switching their appliances and vehicles to electric. But knowing where to start can feel overwhelming.

These friendly, practical evenings — hosted by local volunteers with experience in electrification and drawing on the research of Rewiring Aotearoa — will walk you through the real options available right now: solar panels and home batteries, electric vehicles, heat pump hot water systems, induction cooking, and making the switch from gas to electricity.

Businesses, schools, or community organisations interested in electrification are also welcome. No jargon. No sales pitch. Just straight talk from your neighbours about what works, what it costs, and how to get started.

🎃🕸️ WELLINGTON HALLOWEEN FRIGHT CRAWL 2026 🕸️🎃

One wristband. 4+ of Wellington's best bars. No cover at any of them. The Fright Crawl kicks off Halloween weekend in Wellington on Thursday, October 29th, 2026: a host who runs the night, a live crawl map that always knows where the party is, and up to 800 people in costume moving through the city together. Thursday is the warm-up, the easiest crawl to get into, and the one your Friday self will thank you for.

📍 Crawl Stops: The Welsh Dragon Bar, Panhead Tory Street, The Rogue & Vagabond and El Horno.

🕙 Kickoff: Doors open at 7:30 PM. Wristbands must be picked up by 10:00 PM. The crawl runs until 2:00 AM.

🎶 Music: Live DJs spinning the biggest hits and Halloween classics all night.

🗺️ Live Crawl Map: frightcrawl.com/map/fright-crawl/wellington. Every stop, every time, updated live on the night.

🎟 Tickets: Prices climb as tiers sell, and the launch tier is capped at a handful of tickets that always go first, so grab yours early. Doing more than one night? The Weekend Pass in the ticket menu covers all four Wellington crawls for less than buying them separately.

Throw on your wildest costume and crawl the city with a crowd that is all in costume. Creepy, cute, or covered in fake blood, this is the crawl to be a part of this Halloween weekend. 🧟‍♀️

⭐ Over 10,000 crawlers joined The Fright Crawl last Halloween.

💬 "There were 9 of us and somehow everyone enjoyed it which is honestly rare for our group 💀" Olivia N., 2025 crawler

💬 "My friends and I did this because nobody wanted to be responsible for planning where to go lol. Made the night way easier and every stop had a pretty good crowd." Samantha L., 2025 crawler

🚨 This event is limited to 800 attendees, so grab your tickets early before they sell out! Kickoff night is where the weekend starts, and the crews doing all three nights lock this one in first. Secure your spot before it's too late.

👉 See last year's photos, the full lineup and more reviews at frightcrawl.com/wellington

How It Works

1. Grab your ticket here. The early tiers go first.

2. On the night, show your QR code at the wristband venue between 7:30 PM and 10:00 PM and get your wristband.

3. Follow your host from bar to bar, with the live crawl map showing every stop. No cover anywhere.

4. Everyone ends up at the final venue for one big party.

events.long_description:
Overview

AELERT Regulatory Masterclass on Regulatory Integrity, Ethics and Professionalism ft. Keith Manch and Dr Marie Doole.

Two of NZ's top regulatory leaders lead a discussion-based masterclass on integrity, ethics and professionalism in Wellington.

AELERT Regulatory Masterclass on Regulatory Integrity, Ethics and Professionalism ft. Keith Manch and Dr Marie Doole

October 30 | Te Iho (Bowen House)

Integrity is the foundation of regulatory legitimacy. When it holds, regulators make defensible decisions, resist undue influence and retain public trust. When it slips, the damage is slow, quiet and hard to reverse.

Across Australia and Aotearoa New Zealand, regulators are being asked to uphold that standard in a harder environment: reform is reshaping mandates, resourcing is stretched, and pressure arrives from regulated parties and from within the authorising environment alike. This masterclass brings together two of Aotearoa's most respected regulatory leaders, Keith Manch and Dr Marie Doole, in central Wellington to work through what integrity, ethics and professionalism require in practice, and how agencies can strengthen them deliberately rather than assume they will hold.

What's included

Full day masterclass (9:00am to 3:30pm) with Keith Manch and Dr Marie Doole
Discussion-based sessions covering the fundamentals of good regulatory practice, integrity in the authorising environment, integrity in agency operations, and the mechanics of regulatory capture
Refreshments during the break and coffee on arrival where available
Certificate of attendance for CPD and capability records
Complimentary post-masterclass social event from 4-7.30pm including canapes and social drinks at the Thistle Inn (please RSVP by October 21 to adam.slater@sa.gov.au)

Who should attend

Regulatory staff at every level: frontline practitioners in compliance, enforcement, investigations, monitoring and assessment; managers and team leaders responsible for regulatory decisions and relationships; senior leaders and executives accountable for regulatory strategy, culture and capability; integrity, ethics, assurance and governance professionals; policy and legislative professionals; legal advisers to regulators; and academics, researchers and students working on regulatory practice and integrity. Mixed cohorts are encouraged, since integrity risks are tested daily across an agency, not only in senior roles.

Location

This Wellington masterclass is hosted by the Ministry for Regulation at Te Iho (Bowen House).

Rooms 20.01/02.

Pricing

$500 AUD inclusive of GST and booking fees.

Please review the AELERT event registration terms and conditions.

Event sponsors

The Regulatory Masterclass on AI and Emerging Technologies is proudly brought to you by AELERT and our exclusive technology sponsor Objective Corporation.




For full details about this masterclass please visit the AELERT website.

Read less

events.long_description:
Overview

Re-use, Re-Purpose, Beautify with Gold!! Come along and learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Sip & Kintsugi.

Come and experience this unique Sip & Kintsugi workshop at the lovely Bond Store Distillery. You will get a gin tasting tray on arrival with three different gins with tonic. And why not come a little earlier and grab a bite to eat beforehand. (Must be 18+ yrs of age)

Learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop. You can bring along a piece of your own pottery to restore in this beautiful style. (I'll also have a few as back up if you don't have your own piece) (All Levels)


Friday 30th October - 5:30pm - 7:30pm

Kintsugi

It's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.

You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your knew skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.

This class is not just for budding or accomplished artists. It is for everyone to enjoy a relaxing day of art and design with Ema.

What you will take away:

A finished artwork piece

A understanding of Kintsugi

Knowledge and History of this beautiful art form.




Where: The Bond Store, 21 Birmingham St, Paraparaumu, Kapiti Coast 5032. NEW ZEALAND
When: Friday 30th October
5:30 - 7:30pm

Toi Marsden Gala Evening
Be among the first to experience Toi Marsden, and the first to purchase from this exciting new curated exhibition of contemporary art from across Aotearoa New Zealand.

The Toi Marsden Gala Evening offers guests the first opportunity to explore the exhibition, discover work from an exciting mix of established and emerging artists, and purchase artworks before the exhibition opens to the public for the weekend.

Enjoy a special evening of art, food, wine and connection at Samuel Marsden Collegiate School in Karori, as we celebrate the opening of the inaugural Toi Marsden.

The exhibition will also feature a special collection of work by Marsden’s 2026 Artist in Residence, Fleur Wickes.

Toi Marsden will then open to the public across the weekend:

Saturday 31 October
10.00am–4.00pm

Sunday 1 November
10.00am–2.00pm

Public exhibition entry is by koha, with all entry donations going to Dwell Housing Trust.

Toi Marsden is presented by the Marsden Parents & Friends’ Group, with funds raised supporting Marsden’s long-standing Artist in Residence programme.

We’d love to have you with us for the beginning of Toi Marsden.

events.long_description:
INDUNA - FAVOURITE COLOURS (RELEASE SHOW)
Following recent performances supporting internationally acclaimed Nigerian artist Seun Kuti & Egypt 80, Aotearoa-based South African artist InDuna is set to release his new single 'Favourite Colours' and celebrates with a special headline show at Moon, Newtown, Wellington on Friday 30th October 2026.

Blending Afro-pop, R&B and folk, InDuna's live show brings infectious rhythms and uplifting energy alongside the more personal stories behind the songs. 'Favourite Colours' is an atmospheric anthem about identity, healing and resilience, using colour as a metaphor for how anxiety, grief and disconnection can drain the vibrancy from life, and the journey back to yourself.

﻿
InDuna will be joined by a special guest support act, to be announced.


Wheelchair accessible, seated and standing available.


About InDuna

Artist and producer InDuna draws on his South African roots, raised between Johannesburg and Limpopo before moving to Aotearoa at fourteen. His sound fuses African rhythm with contemporary pop and electronic production. Highlights include the King's Trust Young Global Achiever Award (2024), his single 'Dreams' (Best Original Song, International Online Web Fest; Official NZ Hot Singles Chart; featured in 'Ink and Gold'), and his 2025 EP 'Go High' (#16, Official Top 20 Aotearoa Albums Chart). He's supported Seun Kuti & Egypt 80 and opened for JessB, Estère and Deva Mahal, with headline shows across Wellington and Auckland.

'Favourite Colours' is supported by New Zealand On Air.

events.long_description:
WOW: Meet the Makers
Step inside the World of WearableArt® and hear from the people at the heart of the spectacle.

WOW: Meet the Makers is an inspiring evening of stories, creativity and insight, featuring some of the region's most accomplished WOW designers. Hear from 2026 Supreme WOW Award winner Kayla Christensen as she shares her journey to the top of the world's premier wearable art competition, alongside fellow Kāpiti designer Rebecca Bond, whose imaginative work has earned recognition on the WOW stage. Guests will also enjoy reflections from legendary WOW designer Fifi Colston, a 30-time entrant and multi-award winner whose extraordinary body of work has helped shape the competition's history.

Hosted by Sarah Nathan, Head of Competition for WOW, the evening offers a rare behind-the-scenes look at how a WOW entry evolves from an initial spark of inspiration to a world-class performance. Through designer conversations, creative storytelling and insights into the competition process, guests will discover what it takes to create work that captivates audiences and judges alike.

Whether you're a long-time WOW fan, an aspiring creative, or simply curious about the people behind the spectacle, this exclusive event offers a rare opportunity to connect with the makers, stories and artistry at the heart of WOW.


WOW: Meet the Makers is presented by Visit Kāpiti.

Your panel:
Sarah Nathan
Head of Competition
Gain a unique behind-the-scenes perspective on the WOW Competition as Sarah shares insights into artistic excellence, creative innovation, and what it takes for designers to stand out on the world stage.

Kayla Christiansen
Local Artist and WOW Supreme Award Winner 2026
Kayla Christiansen is a local artist with a passion for all things creative, from fine arts to wearable arts and everything in between. Join Kayla to hear about the journey to becoming a WOW Supreme Award winner and where here imagination is taking her for her next creative journey.

Fifi Colston
WOW Finalist Designer
Discover how storytelling, costume, and craftspersonship come together in wearable art as Fifi shares creative insights from three decades at WOW, revealing the imagination and process behind award-winning designs.

Rebecca Bond
Multidisciplinary Artist and WOW Designer
Kāpiti Coast based artist Rebecca Bond works across contemporary jewellery, silversmithing, wearable art, performance drawing and community arts. Hear Rebecca share insights from her creative journey inspired by people and nature and how her practice explores identity and connection.

Overview

Wellington's Friday Halloween takeover. One wristband, 4+ bars, no cover, a host and a live crawl map. Fri, Oct 30. 18+

🎃🕸️ WELLINGTON HALLOWEEN FRIGHT CRAWL 2026 🕸️🎃

One wristband. 4+ of Wellington's best bars. No cover at any of them. The Fright Crawl takes over Wellington on Friday, October 30th, 2026: a host who runs the night, a live crawl map that always knows where the party is, and up to 800 people in costume moving through the city together. Friday is the big takeover, the night the whole city comes out, and the one that fills right behind Halloween night.

📍 Crawl Stops: Sassy Loves Cash, The Rogue & Vagabond, Panhead Tory Street and Cavern Club.

🕙 Kickoff: Doors open at 7:30 PM. Wristbands must be picked up by 10:00 PM. The crawl runs until 2:00 AM.

🎶 Music: Live DJs spinning the biggest hits and Halloween classics all night.

🗺️ Live Crawl Map: frightcrawl.com/map/fright-crawl/wellington. Every stop, every time, updated live on the night.

🎟 Tickets: Prices climb as tiers sell, and the launch tier is capped at a handful of tickets that always go first, so grab yours early. Doing more than one night? The Weekend Pass in the ticket menu covers all four Wellington crawls for less than buying them separately.

Throw on your wildest costume and crawl the city with a crowd that is all in costume. Creepy, cute, or covered in fake blood, this is the crawl to be a part of this Halloween weekend. 🧟‍♀️

⭐ Over 10,000 crawlers joined The Fright Crawl last Halloween.

💬 "Good mix of places. Started off just drinking and talking and by the last couple stops everyone was dancing 💀 Pretty much exactly what we wanted." Kevin D., 2025 crawler

💬 "We bought tickets mostly because our friends were doing it and ended up having such a good night. Would go again next Halloween ❤️" Brianna F., 2025 crawler

🚨 This event is limited to 800 attendees, so grab your tickets early before they sell out! Friday fills right behind Halloween night, and it does not wait for the last minute. Secure your spot before it's too late.

👉 See last year's photos, the full lineup and more reviews at frightcrawl.com/wellington

How It Works

1. Grab your ticket here. The early tiers go first.

2. On the night, show your QR code at the wristband venue between 7:30 PM and 10:00 PM and get your wristband.

3. Follow your host from bar to bar, with the live crawl map showing every stop. No cover anywhere.

4. Everyone ends up at the final venue for one big party.




What's Included in Your Ticket:
🎟️ One wristband, 4+ bars. No cover at any participating venue.
🎤 An on-site Fright Crawl host. Checks you in, hands you your wristband and leads the group to every venue.
🗺️ The interactive crawl map. Every stop, address and time on your phone, with live updates as the night moves.
🟢 Live venue status. See where the crowd is right now and which stop is peaking.
💬 Live online support all night. Ask FrightCrawl on the map, from doors to the last venue, and a real person from the crew when you need one.
📲 Crawl texts. Opt in on the map and you are always in the loop when the group moves.
🏆 Costume contest, judged on the night.
🍹 Drink specials at participating venues.
🎵 Live DJs spinning Halloween hits and party anthems.
🎃 Up to 800 crawlers in the craziest costumes you will see all year. Come with a group or come alone, you will not be alone for long.
🛂 Your Digital Halloween Passport. Stamp every stop as you hit it, straight from the map.
🌿 The Wishing Willow. One wish, made before the crawl. It comes with every ticket, and so does the link.
🎬 Your personalised Crawl Wrapped. When the night ends, the map builds your recap card from your passport, ready to post.
🎧 The official Fright Crawl Halloween playlist. Fifty tracks to get ready to, yours with the ticket.
📱 Your own "you're in" page after you book: your crawl card to post, your nights, and a link to bring your people.
🕺 A massive final party at the last venue, everyone together.

👻 Costume up and crawl your way through Wellington's hottest bars. Expect eerie drink specials, electric energy, and a Halloween you won't forget!

CANCELLATION REFUND GUARANTEE

👌 If a crawl is canceled and not rescheduled, every ticket is refunded automatically. No vouchers, no credits.

🔁 Plans might change? Add the Flexible Ticket at checkout and you can cancel for any reason up to the cutoff shown on this listing.




WRISTBAND PICKUP INSTRUCTIONS & POLICY

Where and When to Pick Up Wristbands

WRISTBAND VENUE:

Sassy Loves Cash

🕒 7:30PM-10:30PM

📍 24 Courtenay Place, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand

🍸 Halloween Menu on Site

Details: Please arrive at our first stop to scan your ticket and collect your wristband. You have from 7:30 PM to 10:00 PM to arrive and pick up your wristband for the night. Your host leads the group on from this venue at 10:00PM.

MIDDLE STOPS:

The Rogue & Vagabond

🕒 8:30 PM – 11:30 PM

📍 18 Garrett Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011

Details: This is a middle stop. Your host leads the group here between 8:30 PM and 11:30 PM. The live crawl map shows every stop and its time window.

This is a hosted crawl with an open format. You must start at the first venue to collect your wristband. Once you have it, you can follow your host, or visit any participating venue labeled as a "Middle Stop" at your convenience between 8:30 PM and 11:30 PM, or stay at the wristband venue until 10:00 PM. WHY THE FRIGHT CRAWL BEATS ONE BAR

One bar means one cover, one room and one vibe for the whole night. The Fright Crawl gives you Wellington's best bars on a single wristband, a host who moves the crowd so nobody has to organise anything, and a finale where every crawler ends up in the same room at the last venue.

THE FRIDAY TAKEOVER

Friday is the night everyone who could not get Saturday off comes out, and the night the Saturday crowd warms up. Wellington's best bars, one wristband, a host moving the crowd, and a final venue where the whole crawl lands together. It fills right behind Halloween night. 🧛‍♀️

WHO THIS IS FOR

Groups who don't want to be the one planning. Visitors who don't know the bars. Birthdays that land on Halloween weekend. Solo crawlers who want a built-in crowd. Anyone whose costume deserves more than one room.

💬 "If you're coming from out of town for Halloween I'd recommend it. We wouldn't have known which places to go to otherwise." Rachel H., 2025 crawler

💬 "First bar crawl I've done and I'd do another one. I liked being able to move around instead of paying cover somewhere and being stuck there all night." Marcus J., 2025 crawler

GET YOUR TICKETS BEFORE THEY VANISH!

Spots are filling fast, so now's the time to lock in your night. Round up your friends, pick your costume, and get ready to sip, dance, and crawl your way through the biggest Friday of the year in Wellington. Halloween only comes once a year. 🎟️

❓ Questions first? Read the FAQ or reach the crew at frightcrawl.com/support.

18+ EVENT / GOVERNMENT ISSUED ID REQUIRED

Pick Up Wristbands On Time: Collect your wristband during the designated check-in window at the wristband venue, before 10:00 PM. Late arrivals will not be accommodated. No wristband, no entry.

🎃🕸️ WELLINGTON HALLOWEEN FRIGHT CRAWL 2026 🕸️🎃

One wristband. 4+ of Wellington's best bars. No cover at any of them. The Fright Crawl takes over Wellington on Friday, October 30th, 2026: a host who runs the night, a live crawl map that always knows where the party is, and up to 800 people in costume moving through the city together. Friday is the big takeover, the night the whole city comes out, and the one that fills right behind Halloween night.

📍 Crawl Stops: Sassy Loves Cash, The Rogue & Vagabond, Panhead Tory Street and Cavern Club.

🕙 Kickoff: Doors open at 7:30 PM. Wristbands must be picked up by 10:00 PM. The crawl runs until 2:00 AM.

🎶 Music: Live DJs spinning the biggest hits and Halloween classics all night.

🗺️ Live Crawl Map: frightcrawl.com/map/fright-crawl/wellington. Every stop, every time, updated live on the night.

🎟 Tickets: Prices climb as tiers sell, and the launch tier is capped at a handful of tickets that always go first, so grab yours early. Doing more than one night? The Weekend Pass in the ticket menu covers all four Wellington crawls for less than buying them separately.

Throw on your wildest costume and crawl the city with a crowd that is all in costume. Creepy, cute, or covered in fake blood, this is the crawl to be a part of this Halloween weekend. 🧟‍♀️


⭐ Over 10,000 crawlers joined The Fright Crawl last Halloween.

💬 "Good mix of places. Started off just drinking and talking and by the last couple stops everyone was dancing 💀 Pretty much exactly what we wanted." Kevin D., 2025 crawler

💬 "We bought tickets mostly because our friends were doing it and ended up having such a good night. Would go again next Halloween ❤️" Brianna F., 2025 crawler

🚨 This event is limited to 800 attendees, so grab your tickets early before they sell out! Friday fills right behind Halloween night, and it does not wait for the last minute. Secure your spot before it's too late.

👉






How It Works

1. Grab your ticket here. The early tiers go first.

2. On the night, show your QR code at the wristband venue between 7:30 PM and 10:00 PM and get your wristband.

3. Follow your host from bar to bar, or use the live crawl map and go at your own pace. No cover anywhere.

4. Everyone ends up at the final venue for one big party.





What's Included in Your Ticket:
🎟️ One wristband, 4+ bars. No cover at any participating venue.
🎤 An on-site Fright Crawl host. Checks you in, hands you your wristband and leads the group to every venue.
🗺️ The interactive crawl map. Every stop, address and time on your phone, with live updates as the night moves.
🟢 Live venue status. See where the crowd is right now and which stop is peaking.
💬 Live online support all night. Ask FrightCrawl on the map, from doors to the last venue, and a real person from the crew when you need one.
📲 Crawl texts. Opt in on the map and you are always in the loop when the group moves.
🏆 Costume contest with prizes, judged on the night.
🍹 Drink specials at participating venues.
🎁 Giveaways on the night.
🎵 Live DJs spinning Halloween hits and party anthems.
🎃 Up to 800 crawlers in the craziest costumes you will see all year. Come with a group or come alone, you will not be alone for long.
🛂 Your Digital Halloween Passport. Stamp every stop as you hit it, straight from the map.
🎬 Your personalised Crawl Wrapped. When the night ends, the map builds your recap card from your passport, ready to post.
🎧 The official Fright Crawl Halloween playlist. Fifty tracks to get ready to, yours with the ticket.
📱 Your own "you're in" page after you book: your crawl card to post, your nights, and a link to bring your people.
🕺 A massive final party at the last venue, everyone together.

👻 Costume up and crawl your way through Wellington's hottest bars. Expect eerie drink specials, electric energy, and a Halloween you won't forget!






CANCELLATION REFUND GUARANTEE

👌 If a crawl is canceled and not rescheduled, every ticket is refunded automatically. No vouchers, no credits.

🔁 Plans might change? Add the Flexible Ticket at checkout and you can cancel for any reason up to the cutoff shown on this listing.

Sassy Loves Cash

📍 24 Courtenay Place, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand

WHY THE FRIGHT CRAWL BEATS ONE BAR

One bar means one cover, one room and one vibe for the whole night. The Fright Crawl gives you Wellington's best bars on a single wristband, a host who moves the crowd so nobody has to organise anything, and a finale where every crawler ends up in the same room at the last venue.

THE FRIDAY TAKEOVER

Friday is the night everyone who could not get Saturday off comes out, and the night the Saturday crowd warms up. Wellington's best bars, one wristband, a host moving the crowd, and a final venue where the whole crawl lands together. It fills right behind Halloween night. 🧛‍♀️

WHO THIS IS FOR

Groups who don't want to be the one planning. Visitors who don't know the bars. Birthdays that land on Halloween weekend. Solo crawlers who want a built-in crowd. Anyone whose costume deserves more than one room.

Spots are filling fast, so now's the time to lock in your night. Round up your friends, pick your costume, and get ready to sip, dance, and crawl your way through the biggest Friday of the year in Wellington. Halloween only comes once a year. 🎟️

Wellington Zinefest is hosting their annual two-day zine festival to celebrate the thriving zine scene here in Te Whanganui-a-Tara.

We're open to the public from 12 til 4 on Saturday October 31 and Sunday November 1 at Te Aro Campus of Te Herenga Waka Victoria University of Wellington - 139 Vivian street.

Each day we'll have sixty+ unique stalls, loaded with self-made zines, comics, prints, and trinkets. We'll have our beloved community table and trading post running too!

Wellington Zinefest markets are free to attend, make sure you bring cash to buy zines tho!

From 11am to 12pm each day we'll run 'accessibility hour'. This is a chance for any visitors who can't attend when Zinefest is crowded. We'll have no music and try to maintain a low-stimulation environment.

events.name: The Opera House: After Dark
events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
This Halloween, step inside The Opera House after hours for an R18 guided experience. Explore the theatre's hidden corners, colourful history, and lingering mysteries. Over the course of an hour, you’ll be led through the building by a guide. They’ll share tales from The Opera House’s past. This includes stories, legends, and strange happenings that have endured long after the final curtain call.   

As you move through the darkness, mysterious figures, unexpected encounters, and eerie effects will keep you wondering what — and who — might be waiting around the next corner. Once you’ve made it back into the light, unwind in the foyer with a complimentary drink and nibbles, included with your ticket.   

Blending theatre history, storytelling, and a touch of Halloween mischief, The Opera House After Dark offers a unique way to experience one of Wellington’s most iconic venues.

Accessibility and safety
You need a good level of mobility to go on this tour. You will be walking through foyers, stairways, and spaces. While there are railings and several rests throughout the tour, you will not have the opportunity to sit for a long period during the tour.   
This tour is currently not accessible for wheelchair users. If you are a wheelchair user, or have other accessibility needs, and would like to attend a tour, please contact us at guestexperience@wellingtonnz.com 
Some sections of the tour will enter seating areas that are steep and may not be suitable for patrons who experience vertigo. 
Closed-toe, flat shoes are required for the tour. No heels or open-toe shoes.

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Posture Perfection is Possible!
Are you a computer slouch, feeling stiff and tense at work? Do you find it difficult to maintain a good posture?  Does your posture cause back, neck or shoulder tension?  Would you like to enjoy more freedom in everyday activities?
Under the guidance of an experienced teacher, we'll explore movement in ways that help you reduce tense unhelpful habits.  Movement lessons are done on the floor or sitting on a chair and are based on the pioneering work of Israeli physicist and engineer Dr. Moshe Feldenkrais.
This workshop is suitable for all ages (over 16) and fitness levels.
By the end of the workshop, you'll be able to:
• Identify and reduce muscle tension
• Move with more lightness and freedom
• Improve your posture
• Describe some basic anatomy
• Have tools to use at home and at work
Bring two blankets (or a mat and a blanket) and wear loose, warm and comfortable clothing. Tea and coffee provided but bring your lunch. Please note that instructions are given verbally rather than by demonstration, so good hearing and understanding of English is required.
Feel free to contact the tutor, Sue Field on 027 466 7123, if you have any questions. 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.long_description:
Auditions – Tom Jones the Operetta
Auditions: Principal Cast & Chorus for Tom Jones (the Operetta)

🕺 Not Tom Jones the Welsh singer
📖 The Tom Jones of classic literature!

🗓 31 October & 1 November
📍 Te Whaea, Newtown

Rehearsals: 28 February 2027 –
Show Dates: 24 April – 9 May, 2027

Directed by Alison Hodge & Michael Vinten

Book your audition slot:
https://sites.google.com/view/wgslo

Tom Jones is a retelling of Henry Fielding's comic novel, a bawdy tale of 18th century virtue and villainy, in a musical setting by Edward German. This production transports our hero to 1960s London, when an explosion of youth culture disrupted the traditional British class divide. The result is a fast-moving musical farce, with a diverse range of characters, full of colour and energy. The production will be accompanied by a small instrumental ensemble.

Operetta = Vintage Musical

An operetta is a comic opera with dialogue, just like musical theatre (but without microphones). Operettas are what came before classic musicals such as The Sound of Music. An operetta can be performed with small orchestra or piano, and does not necessarily require operatic singers. We encourage all confident singers to audition.

Book your audition slot:
https://sites.google.com/view/wgslo

Overview

Re-use, Re-Purpose, Beautify with Gold!! Come along and learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop.

After several SOLD OUT workshops in Wellington here is the next one... Oct 2026

Learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop. You can bring along a piece of your own pottery to restore in this beautiful style. (I'll also have a few as back up if you don't have your own piece) (All Levels)

Saturday 31st October - 10:30am - 12:30pm or 2:00 - 4:00pm

Have you ever wanted to try Kintsugi.... It's an ancient Japanese art form where you fix broken pottery with gold - making its imperfections its beauty. - A truly wonderful philosophy to live by. Nothing is ever really broken but new life and meaning is brought back making your piece a work of art and truly something special. You can also apply this technique on various materials like glass, wood, greenstone and shells.


Kintsugi
It's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.

You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your new skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.

What you will take away:
A finished artwork piece
A understanding of Kintsugi
Knowledge and History of this beautiful art form.

Overview

Join us and learn more about this beautiful town!

🍇 Bienvenue en Charente ! Tucked away in south-west France, this is the land of cognac, comic books and some of the prettiest villages in the country, and most visitors drive straight past it.

Join Thomas for a fun and immersive workshop (en français !) and set off on a journey through the département, one stop at a time. You'll follow the Charente river through centuries of history, from the Abbaye de Saint-Amant-de-Boixe to the château of La Rochefoucauld. You'll wander the villages of Aubeterre-sur-Dronne and Verteuil-sur-Charente, then head through the vineyards to Cognac. And you'll explore Angoulême, the medieval city on the ramparts that became the world capital of la bande dessinée 💥

And of course, no trip to Charente is complete without its specialities: cognac, pineau, la galette charentaise and the famous cagouilles. Don't know what those are? Come and find out 🐌

🗯️ French A2/B1 level required
🗓️ Saturday, 31 October 2026, 11.30am–1pm
📍 Alliance Française Wellington (78 Victoria Street, Wellington)
🎟️ $30 for AF members & $35 for non-members
