Sound Healing Experience at Lotus Yoga Centre
We invite you to a special evening of Sacred Harmonic Sound with multi-instrumentalist Claudio Escutia. This immersive sound journey offers a deeply restorative experience that invites you to settle into stillness, reconnect with the heart, and explore a sense of inner spaciousness through vibration

About the event
Claudio skilfully layers the sounds of gongs, crystal and Tibetan singing bowls, Native American flutes, and other traditional instruments, enhanced through high-quality audio equipment so the sound can be both heard and felt throughout your body.Harmonic sound and vibration offer the nervous system a chance to truly rest. In this state of relaxation, the thinking mind softens, and we find connection to citta — the heart-mind. From this place, silence arises naturally through the vehicle of sound.This experience is open to everyone. No previous yoga or meditation practice is needed.


What to bring:Bring your own yoga mat or camping mattress, small pillows, eye pillows and blanket to assure comfort.

Booking is essential — spaces are limited and this event often fills quickly.

About ClaudioClaudio is a multi-instrumentalist musician originally from Mexico City and now based in Wellington. Born into a family of musicians, he began playing music at a young age and later studied classical guitar. His journey led him to Montreal, where he explored jazz, world music, and spiritual sound traditions.

Extensive travels in Asia and Europe deepened his connection with Indian music and yogic philosophy. He studied Tibetan singing bowls in Kathmandu and Varanasi, and has since worked with a wide range of instruments including the sitar, esraj, bansuri, harmonium, flutes, gongs, and voice.

Claudio’s work blends technical skill, deep presence, and a profound respect for the healing power of sound.

General admission : $45

🎃🕸️ WELLINGTON HALLOWEEN FRIGHT CRAWL 2026 🕸️🎃

Halloween night itself. One wristband. 4+ of Wellington's best bars. No cover at any of them. The Fright Crawl takes over Wellington on Saturday, October 31st, 2026: a host who runs the night, a live crawl map that always knows where the party is, and up to 800 people in costume moving through the city together. This is the biggest crawl of the weekend and the first one to sell out, every year.

📍 Crawl Stops: The Black Sparrow, Panhead Tory Street, El Horno and Cavern Club.

🕙 Kickoff: Doors open at 7:30 PM. Wristbands must be picked up by 10:00 PM. The crawl runs until 2:00 AM.

🎶 Music: Live DJs spinning the biggest hits and Halloween classics all night.

🗺️ Live Crawl Map: frightcrawl.com/map/fright-crawl/wellington. Every stop, every time, updated live on the night.

🎟 Tickets: Prices climb as tiers sell, and the launch tier is capped at a handful of tickets that always go first, so grab yours early. Doing more than one night? The Weekend Pass in the ticket menu covers all four Wellington crawls for less than buying them separately.

Throw on your wildest costume and crawl the city with a crowd that is all in costume. Creepy, cute, or covered in fake blood, this is the crawl to be a part of on Halloween night. 🧟‍♀️

⭐ Over 10,000 crawlers joined The Fright Crawl last Halloween.

💬 "Got our tickets the day before and had no idea if it was going to be worth it. Ended up staying out way later than we planned lol 😭" Chris T., 2025 crawler

💬 "Check-in was pretty straightforward. After that we just grabbed drinks and followed everyone to the next spots. Easy night." Ryan B., 2025 crawler

🚨 This event is limited to 800 attendees, so grab your tickets early before they sell out! Halloween night is the first crawl of the weekend to sell out, every year. Secure your spot before it's too late.

👉 See last year's photos, the full lineup and more reviews at frightcrawl.com/wellington

How It Works

1. Grab your ticket here. The early tiers go first.

2. On the night, show your QR code at the wristband venue between 7:30 PM and 10:00 PM and get your wristband.

3. Follow your host from bar to bar, with the live crawl map showing every stop. No cover anywhere.

4. Everyone ends up at the final venue for one big party.




What's Included in Your Ticket:
🎟️ One wristband, 4+ bars. No cover at any participating venue.
🎤 An on-site Fright Crawl host. Checks you in, hands you your wristband and leads the group to every venue.
🗺️ The interactive crawl map. Every stop, address and time on your phone, with live updates as the night moves.
🟢 Live venue status. See where the crowd is right now and which stop is peaking.
💬 Live online support all night. Ask FrightCrawl on the map, from doors to the last venue, and a real person from the crew when you need one.
📲 Crawl texts. Opt in on the map and you are always in the loop when the group moves.
🏆 Costume contest, judged on the night.
🍹 Drink specials at participating venues.
🎵 Live DJs spinning Halloween hits and party anthems.
🎃 Up to 800 crawlers in the craziest costumes you will see all year. Come with a group or come alone, you will not be alone for long.
🛂 Your Digital Halloween Passport. Stamp every stop as you hit it, straight from the map.
🌿 The Wishing Willow. One wish, made before the crawl. It comes with every ticket, and so does the link.
🎬 Your personalised Crawl Wrapped. When the night ends, the map builds your recap card from your passport, ready to post.
🎧 The official Fright Crawl Halloween playlist. Fifty tracks to get ready to, yours with the ticket.
📱 Your own "you're in" page after you book: your crawl card to post, your nights, and a link to bring your people.
🕺 A massive final party at the last venue, everyone together.

👻 Costume up and crawl your way through Wellington's hottest bars. Expect eerie drink specials, electric energy, and a Halloween you won't forget!

CANCELLATION REFUND GUARANTEE

👌 If a crawl is canceled and not rescheduled, every ticket is refunded automatically. No vouchers, no credits.

Groups who don't want to be the one planning. Visitors who don't know the bars. Birthdays that land on Halloween weekend. Solo crawlers who want a built-in crowd. Anyone whose costume deserves more than one room.

Spots are filling fast, so now's the time to lock in your night. Round up your friends, pick your costume, and get ready to sip, dance, and crawl your way through Halloween night in Wellington. Halloween only comes once a year. 🎟️

events.long_description:
Anthonie Tonnon Presents Cinematographer | Wellington (Late Show)
Taite Music Prize-winning songwriter Anthonie Tonnon presents his immersive new live show, Cinematographer.

Three years in the making, Cinematographer combines live electronic music, cinematic storytelling and visual design into an immersive performance. Featuring visual DJing by Erica Sklenars, videography by Theo Taylor, styling by Karlya Smith and design by Daniel Alexander, the show sees Tonnon playing the roles of DJ, singer, documentarian and revolutionary lecturer.

The show explores two timelines: the Situationist International in France and Italy during the 1960s, and Whanganui, New Zealand at the turn of the millennium - a mysterious, forgotten city where a new battle is being waged against what Guy Debord famously called The Society of the Spectacle.

Swapping his guitar for a vocoder, and transforming two Synthstrom Deluges into honorary turntables, Tonnon connects these seemingly distant worlds through the musical language of turn-of-the-millennium dance culture.

"Cinematographer is part film, part francophile performance lecture, part disco club set," says Tonnon. "It's a world that we've built for this new music, exploring some newfound passions – the French avant-garde, cinema, urban politics of the 1960s, turn-of-the-millennium dance culture and documentary films, and the glorious, mystifying city of Whanganui."

The ambitious audiovisual performance introduces an entirely new body of work developed with Tonnon's band and longtime producer Jonathan Pearce. The new single and video "Executive Assistant" offers the first glimpse into this new world - Tonnon's first new music in three years.

Doors open: 8.45PM I Show 9:15PM

Unallocated seating and standing available.

Early Bird tickets available until Monday 10 August or until allocation sells out.

Presented by: SBM Presents
Killswitch Engage return to New Zealand in 2026, bringing more than two decades of genre-defining metal to the stage with their biggest Antipodean headline shows yet, joined by special guests Sylosis. The Western Massachusetts heavyweights helped redraw the map for modern metal in the early 2000s, fusing blistering European-inspired guitar work, East Coast hardcore energy and emotionally charged, uplifting lyrics into a sound that changed the game for a generation of bands and fans.
Across a landmark career, Killswitch Engage have earned three Grammy nominations for Best Metal Performance, multiple gold and platinum records, billions of streams and a reputation as one of the most powerful live acts in heavy music. From classic albums like Alive Or Just Breathing, The End of Heartache and As Daylight Dies through to chart-topping releases Disarm the Descent, Incarnate and 2019’s Atonement, they’ve consistently raised the bar while packing out venues and festival main stages around the world.
Fresh from celebrating 25 years as a band and the release of their latest album This Consequence – featuring the blockbuster single “I Believe,” the biggest radio hit of their career – Killswitch Engage are set to deliver a career-spanning set for their New Zealand fans.
Expect a night that runs from era-defining anthems to new favourites, all delivered with the intensity and heart that has seen them share stages with everyone from Iron Maiden and Slayer to My Chemical Romance, Mastodon, Slipknot and Parkway Drive.

From classic albums like Alive Or Just Breathing, The End of Heartache and As Daylight Dies through to chart-topping releases Disarm the Descent, Incarnate and 2019’s Atonement, they’ve consistently raised the bar while packing out venues and festival main stages around the world.
Fresh from celebrating 25 years as a band and the release of their latest album This Consequence – featuring the blockbuster single “I Believe,” the biggest radio hit of their career – Killswitch Engage are set to deliver a career-spanning set for their New Zealand fans.

Overview

Re-use, Re-Purpose, Beautify with Gold!! Come along and learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop.

After several SOLD OUT workshops in Wellington here is the next one... Nov 2026

Learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop. You can bring along a piece of your own pottery to restore in this beautiful style. (I'll also have a few as back up if you don't have your own piece) (All Levels)

Sunday 1st November - 10:30am - 12:30pm or 2 - 4pm




Ema Frost is a very clever Kiwi Artist, who has been teaching Kintsugi for 5+ years and regularly travels to Japan to study and learn new techniques. Ema's illustrations and ceramic works sit in many of our countries best galleries, and whose products and merchandise sell in the most stylish design stores and gallery shops. Her style is enchanting - quirky, feminine and colourful, and clearly influenced by her travels throughout the world, usually off the beaten track.

Have you ever wanted to try Kintsugi.... It's an ancient Japanese art form where you fix broken pottery with gold - making its imperfections its beauty. - A truly wonderful philosophy to live by. Nothing is ever really broken but new life and meaning is brought back making your piece a work of art and truly something special. You can also apply this technique on various materials like glass, wood, greenstone and shells.

KintsugiIt's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your knew skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.

What you will take away:A finished artwork pieceA understanding of KintsugiKnowledge and History of this beautiful art form.

Natural Textured Rings - November Taster!
Make your own personalised ring - a gift for yourself or someone special! :-)

Learn the basic technique first in copper or brass, and then craft your final piece in silver!

Over this taster class, you’ll be guided through the process of heating and texturing metal, cutting and shaping with traditional jewellery tools. Use feathers, leaves, or fabrics to create a unique texture for a beautiful ring!

Learn to measure your finger, cut metal to length and texture it without rolling mill, hammers and punches. Then use a jewellers torch, sandpaper and polishing, and your beautiful new ring will be ready to wear.

This 3-hour class is ideal for beginners, groups of friends and visitors to the city.

Included in the class fee are copper and brass for practising on, a sterling silver ring strip and all consumables such as sandpaper, solder and chemicals. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio.

Kids aged 12 (or so) are welcome to attend the class, but any person under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

Workshop fee is $165, Early bird pricing $148 till 4 October.

events.long_description:
Tones of Silence; Futuna Chapel in Black & White with Catherine Hammond & John Grace
Join Catherine Hammond and John Grace for an afternoon exploring black-and-white photography, from Grace’s evocative Chapel images made with vintage cameras and 19th-century French lenses to Hammond’s insights into Aotearoa New Zealand’s early photographic history.

About the speakers

John Grace

John Grace is a commercial lawyer and amateur photographer. John’s black and white photos of Futuna Chapel have been taken on an old tripod camera using 1866 French lenses. A selection of his photos will be exhibited at the Chapel.

Catherine Hammond

"Against Forgetting: Photographic Archives in Aotearoa"

Catherine Hammond is the director of collections and research at Tāmaki Paenga Hira Auckland War Memorial Museum. She was formerly Hocken Librarian at the University of Otago Te Whare Wānanga o Ōtākou, and before that head of documentary heritage at Tāmaki Paenga Hira Auckland War Memorial Museum and research library manager at Auckland Art Gallery Toi o Tāmaki. She co-edited of ‘A Different Light/First Photography of Aotearoa’ (2024).

It's Halloween weekend so bring your dogs in their favourite costume if you want!

The Small Dog Social Walk is on the first Sunday of the month, meeting at 3:30pm during spring and summer.

The meetup will gather for free play from 3:30pm in the back half McEwan Park at Hikoikoi Reserve, Petone Beach, with the walk along the beach and back starting around 4:00pm. After the walk, feel free to hang around and let the dogs play some more.

Water bowl and poo bag bin provided!

Closest street address for GPS is 38 Marine Parade, Petone - we meet in the field across the road! There is plenty of parking along this street.

April - September - Winter time - 2:30 - 3:30
October - March - Summer time - 3:30 - 4:30

Time changes with Daylight Saving Time.

PLEASE DO NOT GATHER ON THE FRONT FIELD
On arrival, please come straight to the back field. We have had a few dogs running over to the car park in excitement to see their friends, with cars driving around we need to be very careful to keep the pooches safe at all times. If your pooch is not good off lead, please keep it on until everyone has arrived and (if you feel comfortable) then let them off.

This is open to the public, and we welcome anyone who has not been before who would like to join our amazing group of pooches and owners!
We also encourage puppies; this is the perfect place for them to socialise safely.

This group is purely a social group with no formal club functions or responsibilities. The park is also used for Disc Golf, so please watch out for people playing thru.

Anti-social small dogs are welcome. If a muzzle is needed, please ensure that they wear it.

PLEASE NOTE- Your dogs are your responsibility at all times, this includes supervising their behaviour and picking up their poop!

Feel free to post in the event or message the page if you need more info!

Would you like to become less busy and more productive? Then our Time Management workshop is for you.

You've all heard the expression 'Time is money' Well actually time is more valuable than money because time is a non renewable resource. Do you ever have those times when you've been busy all day but feel that you have not achieved what you need to?

Effective Time Management is crucial in today's busy and competitive world. Successes and failures in work and daily activities largely depend on how time is managed. Therefore Time Management is the number one skill to master.

Do you ever feel overwhelmed by the sheer volume of work to be done? Would you like to become less busy and more productive? Then our Time Management workshop is for you. Let us show you and your organisation how to get the most out of a day with better time management skills.

WORKSHOP OBJECTIVES

Plan and prioritise each day’s activities in a more efficient and productive manner
Overcome procrastination quickly and easily
Handle crises effectively and quickly
Organise your workspace and workflow to make better use of time
Become less stressed, less busy and more productive
Delegate more efficiently
Handle interruptions and beat time wasters
Use rituals to make your life run smoother
Plan meetings more appropriately and effectively

Time management training most often begins with setting goals. These goals are recorded and may be broken down into a project, an action plan, or a simple task list. Activities are then rated based on urgency and importance, priorities assigned, and deadlines set.

This process results in a plan with a task list or calendar of activites. Routine and recurring tasks are often given less focus to free time to work on tasks that contribute to important goals. This entire process is supported by a skill set that includes personal motivation, delegation skills, organisational tools and crisis management tools.

events.long_description:
Overview

Explore dopamine, break free from everyday distractions, and find deeper fulfilment through modern psychology and timeless wisdom.

Tuesday Wellbeing Seminars:
Inspire Me!
Hooked: Navigating the Age of Dopamine




From endless scrolling and notifications to constant cravings for quick satisfaction, our minds are perpetually wired for the next hit. But why does chasing cheap dopamine leave us feeling so drained and distracted ?

​This interactive 1-hour workshop bridges modern psychology with timeless wisdom to help us break the loop.

Join us for a relaxed, interactive discussion where we explore how replacing cheap distractions with a "higher taste" can quiet the restless mind, reclaim focus, and unlock a deeper sense of fulfillment.




End the session on a high note with a delicious plant-based dinner, dessert, and good conversation.
Meet your host Sivananda

Sivananda’s background is in both science and music, holding a Master's Degree in Data Science, a Bachelor of Science in Physics and a long history of playing and performing on the double bass. His passion for philosophy, music, good food and community attracted him to the bhakti lifestyle. Having studied and practiced the science of the ‘self’ for six years now, he thrives on drawing insights from contemporary science and combining it with yoga wisdom to encourage others to explore new perspectives.

events.long_description:
Overview

Come along to engage with international experts and NZ practitioners to talk about industrial (ICS/OT) cyber security.

The NZ ICS Cyber Technical Network will be running the 2026 NZ ICS/OT Cyber Summit on the 04 th November in Wellington, NZ (in person only)

Come along to engage with experts in ICS Cyber Security.

Topics will be relevant to:

Industrial Control System Engineers, Team Leaders and Managers
ICS/OT Cyber Security Engineers, Architects, Consultants etc.
Cyber Security Managers, Leaders, CISOs working in Industrial Organisations
DETAILS

Location: Lower Hutt Events Centre, 30c Laings Road, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, NZ

Date: Wednesday, 04th November 2026

Time: 08:30-17:00 followed by drinks & nibbles

The current summit agenda includes:

~08:30 – Doors open, reg, opening
~09:15 – Opening keynote
~10:00 – Three talks sequentially (plenary)
~13:00 – Three talks concurrently (streams)
~13:35 – Three panels concurrently (streams)
~14:20 – Eleven round tables concurrently
~15:35 – Afternoon Panel
~16:05 – Closing keynote
~17:00 – Drinks and nibbles

Current agenda includes contributions from:

Bhojraj Parmar (NZ) | Qubit Cyber
Paul Ganter (NZ) | Business Manager | SGS ECL
Pieter van Oudtshoorn (NZ) | ICS Cyber Security Consultant | SGS ECL
Contributions from NCSC
NZ ICS/OT Cyber Summit SANS Scholarship

At the NZ ICS/OT Cyber Summit, the SANS Institute will be awarding one complementary SANS course to a deserving member of the NZ ICS/OT security community.The scholarship will be awarded to a meritorious individual who has made a significant contribution to their NZ industrial organisation and/or the broader NZ ICS/OT security community. This form is to collect nominations.The submissions will be judged, and a recipient will be selected by a panel of judges. The scholarship will be given away in person at the NZ ICS/OT Cyber Summit in New Plymouth. The judges reserve the right to validate nominators and/or nominees. The judges' decision will be final, and no correspondence will be entered into. Submissions close Tuesday 27th October 2026 at 17:00 NZT. Late submissions will not be accepted.

To make a nomination, please complete the following form: NZ ICS/OT Cyber Summit SANS Scholarship (2026).

For questions, comments, or concerns, please email scholarship@icscyber.org.nz

Call for Contributors

Please consider contributing at the NZ ICS Cyber TN Summit if:

You’re in/from NZ and you’re an owner/operator/end-user technical practitioner
You’re an overseas practitioner and either owner/operator/end-user or service/technology provider
Presenters

If you'd like to present a talk, please fill in a CFP at https://form.typeform.com/to/W5JJxr

Round Table Facilitators | Panellists

If you're open to facilitating a round-table or speaking on a panel, please email summit@icscyber.org.nz

Exhibitors

If you'd like an opportunity to present your offering to NZ ICS/OT cyber practitioners, you can buy an exhibitor ticket. An Exhibitor ticket includes 2 indvidual attendee tickets. Exhibitors will not receive a list of NZ ICS/OT Cyber Summit attendees

For any questions on contributing, see the summit github page

The open evening at the Wellington Old High Court provides a unique opportunity to walk through the meticulously restored Category 1 Heritage Building.

The show offers Wellington fans the chance to revisit a landmark release and hear the songs that have shaped the group's enduring legacy.

Overview

Join Āporo Press at Unity Books for the book launch of ‘Mincemeat’ by Anthony Lapwood.

Join Āporo Press at Unity Books Wellington on Guy Fawkes Day, 5 November, to celebrate the debut novel by Anthony Lapwood.




🐶 Thursday 5 November, 6pm

🐶 Unity Books Wellington

🐶 All welcome!




In the years after his disastrous coming out, Lewis kept his old neighbourhood—and his mum and dad, Madeleine and David—at a safe distance. But tragedy has been drawing him back: first his parents separated, and now they’ve vanished.

Tucked away in his family home with Doggo the ageing Labrador, Lewis is plagued by troubles both past and present. Confronted with the inner lives of his parents—discovered on audio tape recordings and scribbled in journals—their voices feed his imagination as he delves into the mystery of their disappearance.

When speculation gives way to paranoia, and his investigations drive him deeper into perilous territory, Lewis is compelled to take control of the narrative.

He’s a writer; he can’t help himself.

Mincemeat, the enthralling debut novel from Ockham award-winning author Anthony Lapwood, is a wry suburban noir with real bite.




About the author:




Anthony Lapwood (Ngāti Ranginui, Ngāi Te Rangi, Ngāti Whakaue, Pākehā) is a fiction writer based in Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington. His writing has appeared in a wide range of publications. He won the Hubert Church Prize for Fiction for his story collection Home Theatre and received the Louis Johnson New Writer’s Bursary to develop Mincemeat. This is his first novel. www.anthonylapwood.com

events.long_description:
Overview

Awaken your energy through guided breath, movement, sound and stillness in a powerful Kundalini activation experience.

Guided Kundalini Activation




Events now start at 6pm. Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.



A guided kundalini activation. Breath of fire and kundalini pranayama, simple repetitive movement, sound and stillness, sequenced to wake up energy that has been sitting dormant along the spine and let it move.

Who is this for

People who already have some breathwork or movement practice and want something more activating than a wind-down class. You are curious about kundalini but want it held by someone who works with the nervous system, not bypasses it. You are willing to feel a lot and stop when you need to.

Not the right fit as a first-ever breathwork experience. The Root or a gentler breath class is a better start.

What to expect
Arrival and a short orientation: what kundalini activation is, what is normal, and how to opt out of anything
Progressive breath and movement rounds that build energy and heat
A peak where the practice is most active: emotion, shaking, heat, tingling, sound can all come up, all normal
A long, quiet integration: stillness, slow breath, nothing to do
A few minutes to land and share if you want to, before you leave
Benefits
A felt sense of energy moving where it had been stuck
Emotional release without needing a story for it
A reset for a system that has been running flat or wired-and-tired
A clearer, more spacious baseline for a day or two afterward

(No health claims. This is a practice, not a treatment.)

Pre-class prep
Skip heavy food and alcohol in the hours before.
Eat something light beforehand, not a full meal.
Come a few minutes early to settle
If you are pregnant, have a heart or blood-pressure condition, epilepsy, glaucoma, recent surgery, or are in acute mental-health crisis, message Lynn before booking so she can advise or adapt
Wear layers you can move in and get warm in.
Contraindications

Kundalini pranayama and breath of fire are intense. Please do not book, or check with Lynn first, if any of these apply: pregnancy, cardiovascular disease or uncontrolled high blood pressure, epilepsy or seizure history, glaucoma or detached retina, recent abdominal or chest surgery, acute psychosis or an unstable mental-health condition. If you feel dizzy or overwhelmed at any point you stop, breathe normally, and rest, that is always allowed.

We'll close the evening with a nourishing plant-based dinner and dessert, a gentle space to connect and ease back into your evening.


Meet your host, Lynn:
About Lynn

Lynn Tiang is an Integrative Somatic Coach, breathwork facilitator, and Reiki practitioner based in Aotearoa, New Zealand. Lynn supports people who are high-functioning on the outside but chronically tense, exhausted, or quietly stuck on the inside.

Lynn’s work blends three pillars:

Somatic breathwork to regulate the nervous system, soften protective patterns, and restore a steadier baseline in the body
Reiki to support energetic clearing, heart coherence, deep rest, and integration, in a gentle, consent-based way
Life coaching to translate what opens in a session into grounded change in relationships, work, boundaries, and daily life

Lynn’s approach is trauma-aware, practical, and spiritually spacious. The focus isn’t on forcing transformation, it’s on creating enough safety for your system to unwind, receive support, and reconnect with its natural capacity for calm, clarity, and connection.

1:1 Integrative Somatic Coaching. A November spot is open

If you feel a yes in your body during this session, you’re invited to go deeper. Lynn is opening a private 1:1 Integrative Somatic Coaching spot in November for someone ready to work with nervous system regulation, somatic inquiry, breathwork, Reiki, and grounded life coaching support.

To enquire, email hi@lynofuro.co.nz with the subject line: November 1:1.

events.long_description:
Overview

A welcoming men’s circle for honest conversation, deep connection and brotherhood in a space of trust, presence and belonging.

Men’s Circle: Rooted in Connection




Events now start at 6pm. Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.




The evening offers a supportive space for men to come together, connect, and speak openly about life. Whether you’re moving through a period of change, looking for deeper connection, or simply wanting a space where you can show up as you are, you’re welcome here.

The conversations are honest, open, and grounded in mutual respect. There’s no pressure to speak, share, or have everything figured out. You’re just as welcome to listen and be present. Together, we create a space rooted in confidentiality and non-judgement, where everyone can feel safe, heard, and free to be themselves.

Structure of the Circle
Gathering in a Circle: Participants sit in a circle to symbolize equality and unity.
A short meditation or moment of silence may be included to help everyone arrive and connect.
Talking Object: A sharing stick or object is placed in the center. Only the person holding the object may speak, ensuring uninterrupted sharing.
Open Sharing: Anyone may choose to share while holding the object. Sharing is optional, and passing is always respected.
Active Listening: While one person shares, others listen attentively without speaking, interrupting, or offering advice. The focus is on witnessing and being present.
No Judgments or Advice: Participants refrain from judging or offering unsolicited advice, creating a safe space for authentic expression.
Closing: The circle may conclude with a group reflection, a moment of gratitude, or a simple acknowledgment of the shared experience.
Circle Agreements
Supportive Environment: We are here to uplift and support one another, fostering trust and brotherhood.
Focus on the Present: Share what's alive for you now, focusing on your emotions and experiences to deepen emotional awareness.
Use "I" Statements: Speak from your personal perspective using "I" statements to promote authenticity and responsibility. Avoid generalizations like "we" or "us."
No Judgment or fixing: Refrain from judging others sharing or offering unsolicited advice, ensuring a safe and non-critical space.
Confidentiality: What is shared in the circle stays in the circle. You may discuss your own experience outside the group but keep others' details private.




After the circle, stay for a wholesome plant-based dinner and dessert ($20 or $10 for students). Sharing a meal is a simple way to extend the sense of community and connection. This gathering is offered on a non-profit basis.
Meet Your Host: Sri Jiva

Since childhood, Sri Jiva has been fascinated by meaning, purpose, and authentic life fulfilment. This, among other things, led him to join a monastery at the age of 19. After years of monastic training, he chose to marry and pursue a career. He felt called to use his monastic experience to help others understand themselves, and to find wisdom, meaning, and purpose in their own lives. Inspired by this calling, he went to university to study counselling. Now, Sri Jiva and his wife live near Wellington, where he works with a small team of counsellors, supporting clients individually and in groups.

events.long_description:
Men’s Circle: Rooted in Connection
A welcoming men’s circle for honest conversation, deep connection and brotherhood in a space of trust, presence and belonging.

About this Event


Men’s Circle: Rooted in Connection





Events now start at 6pm. Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.




The evening offers a supportive space for men to come together, connect, and speak openly about life. Whether you’re moving through a period of change, looking for deeper connection, or simply wanting a space where you can show up as you are, you’re welcome here.

The conversations are honest, open, and grounded in mutual respect. There’s no pressure to speak, share, or have everything figured out. You’re just as welcome to listen and be present. Together, we create a space rooted in confidentiality and non-judgement, where everyone can feel safe, heard, and free to be themselves.


Structure of the Circle
Gathering in a Circle: Participants sit in a circle to symbolize equality and unity.
A short meditation or moment of silence may be included to help everyone arrive and connect.
Talking Object: A sharing stick or object is placed in the center. Only the person holding the object may speak, ensuring uninterrupted sharing.
Open Sharing: Anyone may choose to share while holding the object. Sharing is optional, and passing is always respected.
Active Listening: While one person shares, others listen attentively without speaking, interrupting, or offering advice. The focus is on witnessing and being present.
No Judgments or Advice: Participants refrain from judging or offering unsolicited advice, creating a safe space for authentic expression.
Closing: The circle may conclude with a group reflection, a moment of gratitude, or a simple acknowledgment of the shared experience.

Circle Agreements
Supportive Environment: We are here to uplift and support one another, fostering trust and brotherhood.
Focus on the Present: Share what's alive for you now, focusing on your emotions and experiences to deepen emotional awareness.
Use "I" Statements: Speak from your personal perspective using "I" statements to promote authenticity and responsibility. Avoid generalizations like "we" or "us."
No Judgment or fixing: Refrain from judging others sharing or offering unsolicited advice, ensuring a safe and non-critical space.
Confidentiality: What is shared in the circle stays in the circle. You may discuss your own experience outside the group but keep others' details private.








After the circle, stay for a wholesome plant-based dinner and dessert ($20 or $10 for students). Sharing a meal is a simple way to extend the sense of community and connection. This gathering is offered on a non-profit basis.


Meet Your Host: Sri Jiva

Since childhood, Sri Jiva has been fascinated by meaning, purpose, and authentic life fulfilment. This, among other things, led him to join a monastery at the age of 19. After years of monastic training, he chose to marry and pursue a career. He felt called to use his monastic experience to help others understand themselves, and to find wisdom, meaning, and purpose in their own lives. Inspired by this calling, he went to university to study counselling. Now, Sri Jiva and his wife live near Wellington, where he works with a small team of counsellors, supporting clients individually and in groups.







Agenda

Host: Sri Jiva

Optional Plant-based dinner and dessert!

Join Seleno Health for an inspiring and evidence-informed 2-hour workshop, where you'll discover our transformative 12-Week Gut Reset program. Drawing from ancient Peruvian wisdom (including revered superfoods like maca, cacao, yacon, and tocosh) and modern nutritional neuroscience, this practical guide empowers you to heal your gut, optimize your gut-brain axis, and support profound improvements in mental health, mood, energy, and overall well-being.

The workshop dives deep into the gut-brain axis — the bidirectional communication highway linking your gut microbiome, enteric nervous system, vagus nerve, immune pathways, and brain. Emerging neuroscience shows that a balanced gut ecosystem profoundly influences neurotransmitter production (such as serotonin — with ~90% made in the gut — and dopamine), stress response via the HPA axis, inflammation levels, and even neuroplasticity. Dysbiosis (imbalanced gut bacteria) is increasingly linked to conditions like anxiety, depression, chronic fatigue, brain fog, and mood instability, while nurturing beneficial microbes can promote emotional regulation, reduced stress reactivity, mental clarity, and resilience.

You'll learn science-backed strategies to:

* Rebuild a thriving microbiome with targeted prebiotics (e.g., yacon syrup's FOS and inulin to feed good bacteria), probiotics (e.g., fermented tocosh as a wholefood "Penicillin of the Andes" for potent gut repopulation), digestive enzymes, and gut-healing foods (bone broth, collagen, slippery elm, turmeric).

* Harness mood-enhancing superfoods: adaptogenic maca for hormone balance, stress management, and vitality; mineral-rich cacao loaded with flavanols, theobromine (a gentle energizer), tryptophan (serotonin precursor), phenylethylamine (the "love chemical" that boosts dopamine reward pathways), and bliss molecules that elevate mood, cognition, and creativity while reducing inflammation — all supporting the gut-brain connection.

* Boost detoxification, immunity, and cellular protection with GPx Immune Protect, which enhances your body's natural glutathione peroxidase systems (and related antioxidant enzymes) to combat oxidative stress — a key factor in fatigue, burnout, chronic inflammation, and mood disorders.

* Integrate nervous system reset tools: mindful eating, breathwork, gentle movement/yoga, and daily mindfulness practices to calm the vagus nerve, lower cortisol, and enhance parasympathetic "rest-and-digest" mode — directly benefiting both gut function and mental/emotional health.

The session also explores how these interventions tie into the endocannabinoid system (ECS) — your body's master regulator of stress, mood, inflammation, and homeostasis. A healthy microbiome supports ECS signaling (via microbial metabolites and fatty acid precursors), which can help alleviate anxiety, depression symptoms, and anhedonia (lack of pleasure/motivation), creating a virtuous cycle for brain and gut health.

You'll receive actionable tools, including:

* The full PDF 12-Week Gut Reset daily planner and holistic guidance.

Interactive Q&A, real-life case studies (showing gains in energy, mood stability, skin clarity, reduced inflammation, and emotional well-being), and practical integration steps ensure you leave empowered and equipped.

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Cheesemaking - Brie and Queso Fresco
The ultimate class in practical cheese making!   Learn all you need to know to replicate making NZ style Brie and Queso Fresco at home.  You will be guided through each step of the cheesemaking process while making your very own round of Brie. Then, while the Brie is ripening and setting (don't worry, all terminology will be explained!), we will make Queso Fresco together.  
All ingredients are provided as are recipes and detailed handouts to take away with you. Bring an apron, a dishcloth, 3 or 4 tea towels, a pen to take notes and a 2 litre container and plastic re-sealable food bags to take your cheese home.
During the workshop, the following topics will also be covered: Milk and where to source it, hygiene and sanitation, equipment required and the origins of the cheeses you are about to make.  You will also receive comprehensive instruction on how to mature your Brie cheese over the next few weeks.
A small break will be provided and you will have the opportunity to purchase equipment and cheesemaking ingredients after the workshop should you wish to replicate the experience at home.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
-  Make Brie and Queso Fresco
- Recall the best milk to use and where to source it from
- Name and identify what equipment and ingredients you need to make Brie and Queso Fresco
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Join Monique in this half-day crochet workshop where you will learn how to crochet a range of little projects suitable for the holiday season. events.long_description:
Join Mangaroa Farms for a Sourdough Bread Baking Workshop with Doris Zuur, who has been baking the slow way for decades: rye sourdoughs raised on a living starter, wholemeal loaves that rise through an afternoon, Swiss Zopf plaited by hand, focaccia, and a fermented buckwheat loaf for those who can't take wheat. Her bread is the kind that fills a house with its smell and a table with quiet conversation.

Spend an afternoon with her in our kitchen. You'll mix, knead, plait and bake alongside her. You'll learn how to keep a starter alive, how to read a dough by touch, and the small decisions — temperature, time, a bit of gusto — that turn flour and water into a good loaf.

You'll leave with:

A jar of living starter to take home
A warm loaf from the oven
Doris's full recipe collection (rye sourdough, wholemeal, Swiss Zopf, fermented buckwheat, focaccia, Oaties)
Her "0800 bread helpline" for when you need a hand at home

Afternoon tea included. Bring a clean glass jar with a lid, an apron, and a willingness to slow down.

Good bread likes it slow.

We will begin at Sat 7th November | 10:00am at Wharekai - 298 Whitemans Valley Road

Any questions, please email events@mangaroa.org

events.name: Designing Your Next Permaculture Project

events.long_description:
Join Mangaroa Farms for a Permaculture Design Workshop that goes well beyond the garden patch. This afternoon session introduces you to permaculture as a design tool for life itself — your community projects, your business, your relationships, even your next family meal.

We'll explore the design process together, then apply it to real situations in small groups. You'll learn to use permaculture ethics as a lens: Is what I'm doing caring for the planet and people? Is it ensuring a fair share of resources? This isn't about following recipes — it's about principles, careful assessment, and truly listening to what each unique situation needs.

When you reach a crossroads in life, whether chosen or unexpected, the permaculture design tool offers a framework. A scaffold for moving forward with intention, embracing diversity and care, and making good use of your time and energy.

This is an introductory session. The topic is as vast as life itself, and as diverse and magical as the natural world around us.

We'll gather in the garden if weather allows, otherwise in the Whare Kai. Expect circle work and small breakout groups where we'll learn from each other's experiences.

We will begin at Sat 7th November | 2:00pm at the Mangaroa Events space at 298 Whitemans Valley Road.

Any questions, please email events@mangaroa.org

Beyond the veils, the Unseen Kingdom waits for the day they can meet you again.

I have seen and connected with these races all of my life. There are many, many races that live beyond the veil of our perception. The Green kingdom beings of the Fae and the Elves, the beings of the twigs and leaves. There are the earth-dwelling races of the dwarves and elementals. The “Unseen Kingdom” banner includes the mer people, dragons and the unicorns. In fact, they gave me the term “the Unseen Kingdom” to describe all of the hundreds of races and beings that humans seem incapable of perceiving.
In this experience, we will meet on the margins of the forest. You are invited to bring whatever you need to be comfortable sitting or lying down. We will be inviting whatever beings of the unseen kingdom who wish to, to come and interact with us.
The experience will unfold as it may. I am expecting that it will involve a meditation, lessons in Unseen Kingdom etiquette, and offerings. In my heart, I know more may come, but every time will be unique.
Please come with a calm heart and a gentle voice.
31st January- 4pm- 7pm

events.long_description:
French Pastry for Beginners
A 4-Week Hands-On Series

Step into the world of French pâtisserie with our beginner-friendly four-week course designed to teach you the essential techniques behind some of France's most iconic pastries. Guided by Le Ciel's experienced pastry chef and owner, Shuchi, you'll build your confidence week by week as you learn the foundations of classic French baking.

This progression-based course is perfect for anyone who loves baking, wants to develop professional techniques, or is looking to begin their pastry journey. Each class focuses on a new skill while building on what you've learned in previous weeks, making it easy to continue growing as a baker.

Week 1 – French Macarons

Take on one of France's most famous pastries with confidence. Learn how to create smooth macaron shells, perfect feet, balanced fillings, and troubleshoot common problems so you can recreate them successfully at home.

Week 2 – Choux Pastry

Master the fundamentals of pâte à choux as you learn to mix, pipe, bake, fill, and finish classic French favourites including profiteroles and éclairs. You'll also learn how to make silky pastry cream and achieve perfectly crisp shells.

Week 3 – French Tarts

Discover the secrets to beautiful French tarts by learning sweet pastry dough, blind baking, creamy fillings, fruit finishing, and professional presentation techniques.

Week 4 – Mille-Feuille

Complete the course by creating the elegant Mille-Feuille. Learn how to work with puff pastry, prepare rich vanilla crème pâtissière, assemble delicate layers, and finish with a professional glaze.

What's Included
Four hands-on classes
Step-by-step instructions from professional pastry chefs
All ingredients and equipment are provided
Recipe booklet to take home
Your creations to enjoy and share
Small class sizes for personalised guidance

Who is this course for?

This course is ideal for complete beginners and enthusiastic home bakers. No previous baking experience is required—just bring your enthusiasm and a love of French pastries.

By the end of the four weeks, you'll have mastered a range of foundational pastry techniques and be ready to continue into our future intermediate pastry workshops.

Spaces are limited to ensure every participant receives plenty of individual guidance. Early booking is recommended.

We will be running 2 starts for this course:
Dates for course:
First course: September 5th, 12th, 19th and 26th
Second course: November 7th, 14th, 21st and 28th

events.long_description:
Exhale Evolution
✨ Grounded Grace Counselling x Alchemy Ascending ✨

https://momence.com/Yoga-Corner/EXHALE-EVOLUTION/143442298

3 hour workshop, Movement ~ Breathwork ~ Sound Journey

Saxon Brazier from Grounded Grace Counselling and Kez Milne from Alchemy Ascending bring you a 3-hour immersive workshop combining Somatic Movement, Conscious Connected Breathwork and Sound Odyssey.

A deep dive into the body — creating space to slow down, rest, digest and reconnect with what is happening beneath the surface.

You might arrive carrying stress, emotions, old hurts, tension, overwhelm or simply the weight of everyday life.

Through conscious connected breathwork, somatic movement and sound, we create a safe and supported space to explore what your body may be holding — without needing to force, fix or figure anything out.


🌿 CONSCIOUS CONNECTED BREATHWORK

Conscious Connected Breathwork is a rhythmic breathing practice where the inhale and exhale are intentionally connected, creating a continuous flow of breath without pause.

As we consciously connect the breath, we bring greater awareness into the body. Physical sensations, emotions, thoughts and patterns may begin to come into awareness, creating space to notice and explore what is present.

Rather than trying to think our way through an experience, the breath invites us to move out of the thinking mind and into the body — meeting whatever arises with curiosity, awareness and compassion.

The practice is centred around presence and allowing, rather than forcing an emotional release or trying to create a particular outcome.


🎶 SOUND ODYSSEY

Following the breathwork, Saxon's Sound Odyssey will invite you into a deeply immersive sound experience designed to help you settle, integrate and reconnect with the body.

Having previously sold out her Sound Odyssey experiences, Saxon weaves together drums, medicine drum, guitar and vocals to create a rich and organic soundscape.

Moving from rhythm and activation into softer, settling vibrations, the sound journey offers space to simply lie back, breathe and receive.

A meeting point of sound, vibration, voice and stillness — allowing the body and nervous system time to integrate whatever has arisen during the breathwork.


✨ YOUR FACILITATORS

Kez Milne — Alchemy Ascending
400-hour accredited Conscious Connected Breathwork Facilitator.

Saxon Brazier — Grounded Grace Counselling
Registered trauma-informed counsellor with training in breathwork and somatic facilitation.
https://www.groundedgrace.nz/

Together, Saxon and Kez will hold a grounded, carefully facilitated container for you to explore breath, body, emotion and sound.


⚠️ SAFETY & CONTRAINDICATIONS

Safety is paramount. Breathwork is not suitable for everyone.

Conscious Connected Breathwork involves sustained, active breathing and can produce significant physical and emotional experiences. For this reason, there are certain circumstances where participation may not be appropriate.

This workshop may not be suitable for you if you:

• Are pregnant or may be pregnant
• Have a history of cardiovascular disease, heart attack or significant heart problems
• Have uncontrolled high blood pressure
• Have a history of stroke, aneurysm or significant vascular disease
• Have epilepsy or a seizure disorder
• Have severe or uncontrolled asthma or significant respiratory disease
• Have a current serious psychiatric condition, psychosis or significant difficulty distinguishing internal experiences from external reality
• Are experiencing acute psychological distress or significant mental health instability
• Have recently undergone major surgery or have another significant medical condition that may make intensive breathwork unsafe
• Are under the influence of alcohol or recreational drugs
• Have another medical or psychological condition that may make an intensive breathwork practice unsafe for you

If you are unsure whether this practice is appropriate for you, please speak with your doctor or qualified healthcare professional before booking.

Participation is voluntary and you can stop or modify the practice at any time.

Every participant will be required to read the full disclaimer and contraindications and sign a waiver confirming that they understand and agree to the terms before entering the workshop space.

We take the responsibility of holding this space seriously. Safety, consent, choice and nervous-system awareness are paramount throughout the experience.


🌿 BOOKING & ONBOARDING

Once your booking has been made, we will send you a full onboarding pack with everything you need to know before the workshop, including what to bring, how to prepare and important instructions for arriving and entering the space.


3 HOURS

Somatic Movement • Conscious Connected Breathwork • Sound Odyssey


Come as you are.

Create some space.

Breathe. Move. Feel. Listen. Integrate.

events.long_description:
Tones of Silence; Futuna Chapel in Black & White with Dr Malcolm Doidge
Dr Malcolm Doidge presents his 360-degree time-lapse photography project, captured in Futuna Chapel across the 2023–2024 equinoxes and solstices. A short film of the project will be screened, followed by insights into the digital processes behind its creation.

About the speaker:

After completing his studies at the University of Canterbury School of Fine Art in 1984, Malcolm Doidge worked for the New Zealand Correspondence School as an illustrator. He received his first commission from Lincoln College (now University), producing the work 'Ascent' in 1984.

In more recent years Doidge has taught Creative Technologies at Weltec (Wellington) and completed a Doctor of Philosophy, Inside Arcadia: An immersive virtual phantasmagoria. His degree was conferred by Massey University, Toi Rauwhārangi College of Creative Arts, in 2022.

His work has been recognised by several awards including the Wallace Art Award (2004, 2006, 2009, 2013 and 2016), the Visa Gold Art Award (1998) and he was the premier award winner in the NCC Art Award in 2002.

events.long_description:
Authentic Indian cooking classes in Wellington with panaromic views over Wellington Harbour.

In each class, you will learn 4-5 recipes like: potato stuff roti, roasted eggplant curry, wholemeal, roti, naan; shahi paneer; dhal, samosa; palak paneer; gourmet chickpeas; vegetable korma; gulab jamun; kheer; mango lassi; masala chai, and many more...

The classes start at 6 pm or 10:30 am on weekends and weekdays with a 2-hour session followed by a dinner or lunch afterwards. The ingredients, copies of recipes, organic karma drink will be provided with a full course meal in a banquet setting. Custom made classes available for gluten free, dairy free and any other food intolerance and dietary requirements.The ingredients, recipes, complimentary organic karma drinks will be provided with a full course meal.

There are 2 to 8 people in each class in purpose built cooking studio. Also a private cooking classes available.

The menu for the class can be:

1) Spicy potato stuffed paratha and roti, rajasthani tomato relish, aalu matter or spicy peas- potato curry, roasted cumin yogurt raita and fresh mint- coriander chutney.

2) Shahi Paneer (cottage cheese cubes with spices and rich tomato-cashew gravy), garlic coriander naan, cumin jeera basmati rice and sweet fragrant rice pudding with cardamom. Also I will teach how to make fresh paneer.

The total cost is $130 per person, this includes ingredient cost. (As an alternative we also sell cooking class gift vouchers.The food options are unlimited and the class provides fresh and best ingredients)

events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Almost thirty years after the duo cut their teeth in the comedy clubs of Wellington, Flight of the Conchords are coming home. Fans can expect a career-spanning set. It will include hits from their Emmy-nominated HBO series and two critically acclaimed studio albums. 

After taking an eight-year break from performing, Bret McKenzie and Jemaine Clement burst back onto the live scene in 2026. They played two sold-out shows at Los Angeles’ Greek Theatre. That followed five intimate warm-up shows at Wellington’s Meow Nui. While they put the Conchords on ice for a few years, the pair both remained busy. Bret won an Academy Award for Best Original Song for ‘Man or Muppet’, wrote songs for ‘The Simpsons’ and‘The Minecraft Movie’, and released two solo albums. Jemaine has focused on the screen, creating comedy horror TV shows ‘Wellington Paranormal’ and ‘What We Do In The Shadows’. He’s also appeared in films including the last two ‘Avatar’ instalments. 

Don’t just think about it, get your tickets before they’re gone.

Overview

Presentation & korero to equip youth workers with skills to support rangatahi with addictive traits in a culturally safe & responsive way

Explore how the teenage brain is wired for addictive behaviours, including cellphones, vaping, smoking and other substances. Learn to recognise early warning signs, respond effectively, and gain practical strategies to help young people build healthier habits and make positive choices.

The training is suitable for anyone who works with young people who would like greater knowledge and understanding, along with tools to support rangatahi overcome addictive traits in a safe and culturally responsive way.

This training is presented by the Nelson Tasman Youth Workers Collective, delivered by the Collaborative Trust and made possible thanks to support from Department of Internal Affairs and Rata Foundation. Not a member? Sign up here and take advantage of our free training opportunities.




Meet the kaiako;


Dr/Dame Sue Bagshaw
Dame Sue calls herself a 'youth worker with a medical degree'. Incredibly knowledgeable on all things youth... she has been a champion for positive youth development throughout her life, with notable mentions being that she founded Te Tahi Youth (youth one-stop-shop), The Collaborative Trust, and The Youth Hub in Ōtautahi Christchurch.

Ollie Flett
Youth Tutor Ollie Flett works as a youth wellbeing practitioner at St Bedes College in Christchurch in their wellbeing team and is a whānau support worker. He has a psych degree, a post-grad cert in counselling and has lived experience with neurodiversity, substances, online culture, and harmful gaming/technology use.

events.long_description:
Cooking: Thai Food with Aranya
Thai cuisine is an exciting explosion of tastes and textures. This highly aromatic food has become popular around the globe. Each week you will be shown different Thai dishes and you will get to make these. This course will provide you with tips, tricks and knowledge and it will be fun, easy and yummy!
Not suitable for vegetarians.  All ingredients included in course fee – please bring to each session your apron, a couple of tea towels, a dishcloth and containers to take leftovers home
By the end of the course you'll be able to
Make a range of Thai dishes at home with more confidence

Note:  Our cooking courses are designed to provide a collaborative and immersive learning experience where learners often work in pairs and/or groups. events.name: LINDY LAB: Level up your Lindy!
events.venue: Newtown Community Centre - Te Whare Hapori o Ngā Puna Waiora,Wellington SCL Newtown, 74 Colombo St, Newtown, Wellington 6021, New Zealand, Wellington
events.long_description:
LINDY LAB: Level up your Lindy!
Calling all those who want to level up their Lindy! We have a special two week crash-course designed specifically for those who want to make the jump from beginner to intermediate (and those who want to brush up on their skills)!

Basically, if you're wanting to move up in your Lindy journey but not sure how to get there, these open-level workshops are for you!*

They’re also a great option for any intermediate dancers who want to build a solid foundation for 2027 and beyond, or for those who want to try switching leading/following!

Week 1 | Nov 10, 6:30pm-8:45pm: Swing-out deep-dive

Swing-outs are one of the fundamental moves that make Lindy-Hop, well, Lindy-Hop! They're awesome but can be tricky to master (journey not a destination!) In this 2h workshop we'll hone in on the craft and techniques that make swing-outs feel oh-so good, as well as introduce some fun styling and variations you can incorporate to make them your own!

Week 2 | Nov 17; 6.30pm-8:45pm: Improver essentials

Switching between the fundamental Lindy footwork can be a challenge! This 2h workshop is designed to build your confidence in moving between 6-count, 8-count and Charleston. On top of this, we'll be focusing on expanding your dance vocabulary so you can hit the social dance floor with style!

*For beginners who come to both workshops you’ll (pretty much) be ready to join intermediate classes in 2026! (Please still check in with the facilitators before committing to intermediate classes).

Venue:
Te Whare Hapori o ngā Puna Waiora | Newtown Community Centre.

Price:
$20/workshop. We want to make these workshops as affordable as possible so there's nothing stopping you reaching your Lindy goals!

**Please aim to arrive at least 10min before class starts so we can sign you in**

Think big! Explore bold ideas, fresh thinking and what makes us human, at Massey's hands-on day celebrating humanities and social sciences.

The Big Think is a festival of ideas for high school students, hosted by the College of Humanities and Social Sciences at Te Kunenga ki Pūrehuroa Massey University. Together, we'll explore how making sense of the world is a human and social thing.

Across all three Massey campuses this November, staff, students and graduates will share how the humanities and social sciences help us to understand what it means to be human, to live with others, and to act with care and purpose in a fast-moving, technology-infused, and often demanding world.

From communication and media to psychology, philosophy, planning, ethics, creative writing, emergency management, and even what we can learn about today’s world from history and classics, The Big Think shows how human-centred thinking helps us navigate change, make better decisions, and thrive in contemporary society.

Then, you'll get to have a go yourself, in a wide range of interactive workshops, from broadcast journalism skills to beta-testing a new psychology-based game to hacking the gaps in Wikipedia.

The skills that will future-proof you are human: come discover yours with us.

events.long_description:
National Dog Database
Using the NDD to its full potential. Get hands-on and use realistic scenarios to explore and learn the functionality of the NDD website.

About this Event


Description

The National Dog Database went live 1 May 2006 and provides a countrywide overview of dog control in New Zealand.

It brings great benefits to the animal control industry including the ability to;

track classified owners and dogs
monitor the national infringement count of owners
look up out of district dog and owner details
locate dogs when only limited information is available;
and contribute accurate data to ongoing policy analysis.







Outline

Using the NDD training environment (it looks just like the live NDD system but contains fictional data), the NDD training workshop will explore the following areas:

Background – the history of the NDD project – from 2003 to present
TA Extracts – how information gets from your local system to the NDD and the feedback the NDD will give you as well as the different types of files you can send
Searching – how to get the best out of the search screen and how to interpret the results of your search
The ToDo List – what are errors, warnings, information and system notifications? Detailed discussion about what you need to do with them.
Automated and Manual Linking – National Duplicates – comparing dogs and owners that look similar but are in different districts, and how to manually search for other duplicates.
Security – passwords, adding new users or expiring old accounts, as well as the owner protected status.
Reports – what reports you can run and how to use them in your TA. Did you know there are 18 different kinds of reports that you can generate from the NDD and that you can use some of them to compare your TA’s data to a national summary?







Learning outcomes

With a focus on maintaining data quality, participants in the workshop will learn to use the NDD as a tool for animal control and further understand the importance of administrative roles at the local level. Following the completion of the NDD training workshop, NDD users will have the confidence to use the database to its full potential.







Audience

This course is suitable for managers, team leaders and users with animal control administrator responsibilities.







Prerequisites

To participate in the NDD training workshop you must be a registered user of the National Dog Database (employee or contractor). You are required to bring your own laptop.

events.long_description:
Well Ahead - Wellington Women's Health Event
WELL AHEAD: PUT YOUR HEALTH ON THE AGENDA


An event for women balancing demanding careers, businesses and families, who are already invested in their health and want to understand it more deeply.

As energy, sleep, recovery and body composition shift through midlife, the right information matters.


Well Ahead brings together Dame Susan Devoy and a lineup of experts across health, nutrition, movement and healthy ageing to explore the science and strategy behind:


* Energy and recovery

* Sleep and stress

* Nutrition

* Strength and movement

* Body composition

* Hormonal changes

* Perimenopause and menopause

* Bone health

* Genetics and individual biology



Well Ahead is designed as a connected conversation, not a series of standalone talks.


Each speaker builds on the last, giving you a clearer, more complete picture of your own health rather than a list of disconnected tips.


The day opens with an optional workshop, Your Genes, Your Choices, exploring genetics, DNA testing and the role our genes can play in understanding individual biology. The full programme continues into the afternoon and closes with a live panel and audience Q&A.


Practical information. Expert perspectives. One day, properly invested in your health.


Choose a Morning Workshop pass, Main Event pass, or the Full Pass for the whole day.

----------------------------------------


> > “Women spend so much of their lives looking after everyone and everything else. Well Ahead is about putting your own health on the agenda, hearing from people who really know their field, and coming away with information and ideas you can actually use. You don't have to have all the answers. Sometimes you just need to make the time to start asking the right questions.”

- Dame Susan Devoy



Well Ahead is supported by a growing network of organisations across Wellington's business, professional, health, fitness and wellness communities, all helping us bring women together for an important conversation about health through midlife.

----------------------------------------


ABOUT CONQUER HEALTH

Conquer Health helps men and women understand their unique biology, so they can focus on what matters to their health today and make informed choices for the years ahead. Rather than one-size-fits-all health advice, Conquer Health combines advanced biological testing with a multidisciplinary clinical team to build a personalised picture of your health, delivered remotely anywhere in New Zealand.


Learn More About Conquer Health

Website: https://www.conquerhealth.co.nz

Photography: Unlocking the Secrets to Captivating Images
Elevate your photography from ordinary to extraordinary and ensure your work stands out in the digital age. Creating captivating photographs and understanding what makes a photograph engaging is something every photographer should master. Camera settings are essential, but once you know them, you need to learn how to take photographs that stir emotions, impact your audience, and leave a lasting impression. After all, isn’t that the true purpose of photography? People don’t want to see the same landscapes or flowers they’ve seen thousands of times. But how do you turn what you love into something that makes people go, "Wow"?
Captivation in photography means stopping a viewer in their tracks, making them look, feel, and connect. It’s about delivering a photograph that enthrals, evokes profound emotions, and shifts perspectives.
In a world brimming with images, only a few have the power to truly captivate and linger in our memories.
 This pioneering course is your gateway to mastering the art of creating captivating photographs at a time when AI-generated images are saturating our visual landscape. Create something genuine and memorable—images that spark curiosity, evoke emotions, and inspire changes in perception. It's time to define your unique style, refine your vision, and make your mark.
 Course Outcomes
 By the end of the course, you’ll be able to: 
Identify the foundational elements that transform an ordinary image into a captivating one.
Create photographs that make people say "Wow" by applying techniques that add a spark of wonder to your shots.
Infuse your photographs with curiosity, making each frame a source of intrigue and interest.
Understand why some images linger in memory and how to make your photographs unforgettable.
Develop a unique style and vision that sets your work apart in the crowded digital landscape.

‘He Has His Father’s Eyes’: Horror films and Cornelia Parker
Horror has long flickered at the edges of Cornelia Parker’s practice. This talk traces the network of horror references running through this exhibition, exploring how Parker mobilises classics Psycho and Rosemary’s Baby as found cultural objects—laden with symbolic charge, collective memory and anxieties that continue to haunt the present.

Speakers Aaron Lister (Head Curator Art, City Gallery Wellington, and co-curator of Cornelia Parker) and Chelsea Nichols (Senior Curator, The Dowse Art Museum) collaborate as Curator of Screams—an unholy entity dedicated to the twisted entanglements of contemporary art and horror cinema.

The talk will be followed by a screening of Rosemary’s Baby. Wear your best baby blue dress.

Think big! Explore bold ideas, fresh thinking and what makes us human, at Massey's hands-on day celebrating humanities and social sciences.

The Big Think is a festival of ideas for high school students, hosted by the College of Humanities and Social Sciences at Te Kunenga ki Pūrehuroa Massey University. Together, we'll explore how making sense of the world is a human and social thing.

Across all three Massey campuses this November, staff, students and graduates will share how the humanities and social sciences help us to understand what it means to be human, to live with others, and to act with care and purpose in a fast-moving, technology-infused, and often demanding world.

From communication and media to psychology, philosophy, planning, ethics, creative writing, emergency management, and even what we can learn about today’s world from history and classics, The Big Think shows how human-centred thinking helps us navigate change, make better decisions, and thrive in contemporary society.

You'll meet Humanities and Social Sciences staff, graduates and current students who will share their study and career journeys. Then, you'll get to have a go yourself, in a wide range of interactive workshops, from broadcast journalism skills to beta-testing a new psychology-based game to hacking the gaps in Wikipedia.

The skills that will future-proof you are human: come discover yours with us.

Enigma - Wellington
NZSO Artistic Advisor and Principal Conductor Gemma New with legendary pianist Sir Stephen Hough present a concert of charm, mystery and bold vision.

Programme:
Ross Harris Concerto for Orchestra (World Premiere)
Saint-Saëns Piano Concerto No. 5 Egyptian
Elgar Enigma Variations

Edward Elgar’s greatest masterpiece remains swathed in mystery.

His Enigma Variations, a set of 14 variations on a theme you never actually hear, has been the subject of both intense scrutiny and great love, thanks to the compositional genius and throbbing heart pulsing in these compelling variations.

Similarly, Saint-Saëns’ Fifth Piano Concerto has beguiled audiences with its Eastern-inspired sounds — hence its Egyptian nickname. To weave his own spell on us, legendary pianist Sir Stephen Hough returns to our shores. Praised by Limelight for possessing “an other-worldly stillness and strength [and] the perfect technique combined with the utmost poetic fluency”, Hough promises to transport us to another world.

We proudly premiere Ross Harris’ Concerto for Orchestra. A four-time winner of the SOUNZ Contemporary Award, Harris’ artistry and bold vision electrifies this newly commissioned work, driving the orchestra to new heights.

events.venue: Meow,9 Edward Street, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Sulfate - Live at Meow - And It Wants Album Release Tour
Feral, devolved and running on instinct, the six songs on Sulfate’s third album ‘And It Wants’ grapple between David Harris unleashing on his drum kit, Zac Arnold conjuring fuzz and feedback and Peter Ruddell’s taut, wiry guitar-work and commanding baritone. Written and recorded in New Lynn’s industrial area, this new batch of songs were created on a diet of Cormac McCarthy novels, Adam Curtis documentaries and the madness of gothic horror. Since recording, Sulfate's line up has expanded once more, introducing multi-instrumentalist Louisa Nicklin to the band's inexorable live performances.

Sonically, Sulfate set out some parameters at the outset of the album recordings - and it was important for things to sound real. The band wanted real instruments to be played, and, importantly, sound like they’re being played, by real, living people. This was a conscious reaction to the modern, online, perfect-existence, social media-ness of it all. Audio engineer Emily Wheatcroft-Snape was recommended to the band because of her ability to capture sounds with accuracy and precision - and she encapsulated the live band just as they had hoped.

Thematically, ‘And It Wants’ sees Ruddell clinging to optimism and joy while being subject to the existential nihilism of our current hypernormal, western reality. “Death is all through this record. The songs were born out of the feeling that there are no rules, that nothing matters, and that we all die. That we dance around the fact that death comes for us all, but we never really, truly, acknowledge it - it’s just too big or too heavy to have any kind of impact on our day to day existence. The intent is to provide a sonic backdrop to dance ecstatically, liberated, as the world around you burns. Find comfort and joy in things while you can, even as the end draws near and darkness begins to ruminate.”

‘And It Wants’ is out digitally, and on two exclusive vinyl variants via Flying Nun Records and Holiday Records on October 23rd.

events.long_description:
Raurimu Thunder
Mainline Steam Heritage Trust is embarking on our biggest trip of the year. Modern diesel trains cover this route daily without a second thought, but we are doing something entirely different. We are throwing out the modern dampening, bypassing the mundane, and tackling New Zealand's greatest rail challenge the way it was meant to be conquered: with raw, untamed steam power.

Raurimu Thunder puts you trackside and onboard as our heavy heritage steam locomotive charges into the rugged heart of the North Island to take on the legendary Raurimu Spiral. This is a full day, high horsepower assault on a brutal mountain grade. No filters, no computer assists—just pure, unfiltered vintage engineering working at the absolute limit.

Relax in climate controlled comfort or head to the open air viewing platform to hear and see our heritage steam locomotive charge across dramatic landscapes and tackle the country's most legendary railway challenge. Large panoramic windows frame the unfolding wilderness, ensuring you enjoy every moment of the giant climb in absolute comfort, no matter the unpredictable Central Plateau weather.

How Your Day Flows:
The Scenic Approach: Settle into our premium carriages at your local station as the whistle blows and the journey begins. We steam smoothly through rolling rural valleys toward the base of the Central Plateau. Indulge in fresh barista coffee, artisan snacks, or a local craft beer from the fully stocked cafe carriage as the excitement builds.

Conquering the Spiral: Feel the earth shake as our locomotive battles the 1 in 50 grade of the world famous Raurimu Spiral. This 1898 engineering masterpiece overcomes a massive 139 metre vertical rise through a brilliant layout of horseshoe curves, deep tunnels, and a complete 360 degree loop. Experience the tight, coiling geometry firsthand from the outdoor platform, where you can practically see the front of the train loop right over the back.

The Trackside Photo Runby: Step off the train directly onto the rugged track ballast for the ultimate adventure highlight. Clear your camera lenses and find your vantage point along the tracks. Feel the anticipation build as the massive steam locomotive sets back out of sight, then marvel at the raw power as it charges back up the spiral for an unforgettable, full steam display.

The Atmospheric Return: Board your assigned premium carriage at the summit for a cozy, relaxing journey home. Swap stories with fellow travellers and enjoy a premium glass of regional wine from the salon bar as the train rolls comfortably into the night, concluding an epic day of New Zealand rail history.

Silver Star Dinner Service

As the day draws to a close and the train settles into its evening journey home, make the most of the experience with our Silver Star Dinner Service.

For $26.99 per meal, enjoy a freshly prepared dinner from Hungry Rush Ohakune, served during the return journey. It’s the perfect way to relax after a day of steam, scenery and adventure.

Choose your preferred dinner option when you book, with your selection made and paid for conveniently during checkout.

Your Dinner Choices:

The Wingman
Tender smoked chicken wings, marinated in chipotle buttermilk and served with crispy fries and a smoky hickory cola BBQ sauce.

The Burger & Fries
A juicy New Zealand beef burger with American cheese, grilled onions, pickles and house burger sauce, served in a fresh milk bun with crispy fries.

Fish & Chips
Fresh East Coast tarakihi in a light, crispy batter, served with golden fries, minted peas, fresh lemon and a house-made dipping sauce.

The No Meat Burger & Fries — Vegetarian
A delicious vegetarian burger featuring a seasoned vegetable patty with Swiss cheese, grilled onions, seasonal sauce and vegetable pickles, served in a fresh milk bun with crispy fries.

The Silver Star Dinner Service is completely optional and is not included in the standard ticket price. Dinner can be added to your booking during checkout for $26.99 per meal.

Please note that the timetable below is provisional and may be subject to change pending final approval from KiwiRail. While we aim to operate to the times shown, departure and arrival times may be adjusted as operational planning is finalised.
