Cheesemaking - Farmhouse Cheddar Cheese Workshop
During this hands-on workshop, you’ll be guided through each step of the cheesemaking process while making your very own round of farmhouse style cheddar.
The fee includes a cheese press (value $95.00) which can be used every time you want to make a hard cheese. It holds up to 6 litres of milk and this is what you’ll be taking your cheese home in to press for 12 hours after the workshop. All ingredients, recipes and a full set of course notes are provided.
You’ll also receive comprehensive instruction on how to wax (if you choose to) and then mature your cheese over the next five weeks. Alexis will also demonstrate how to make halloumi cheese which will then be grilled for you to enjoy! There’ll be a short lunch break and cheese making supplies such as wax will be available to purchase.
By the end of the workshop, you’ll be able to:
• Describe the basics of sanitisation and hygiene
• Recognise the difference between raw and pasteurised milk and know where to source them
• Make a round of cheddar cheese using a cheese press
• Describe how to wax and mature the cheese
• Describe how to make halloumi, following a demonstration

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.

If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.

Together, workshop participants will demystify how artificial intelligence actually works, acknowledge some of the harms of this new technology, learn about the characteristics of mis/disinformation, build resilience against fake news, and explore why our brains weren’t built for the infinite scroll. You will walk away from the workshop with a better understanding of the hidden forces shaping your screen, equipped with real-world tools to cut through the digital noise.
 
Dr. Andrew Chen is a leading New Zealand specialist at the intersection of digital technology ethics and public policy. With a PhD from the University of Auckland in Computer Systems Engineering, Andrew brings a deep technical understanding and applies it towards systemic issues and interventions. With extensive experience advising public agencies and private companies on governing emerging technologies, Dr. Chen translates complex technical concepts into clear, accessible insights for the community. He is passionate about helping people understand technology's societal impacts, and thinking more deeply about what’s happening behind the scenes, so we can all navigate today’s complex digital landscape.

A rare opportunity to explore the attic at Old Government Buildings as we celebrate its 150th birthday.

Join our expert guide for a tour around the attic at Wellington's iconic Old Government Buildings.

FAQ’S

🗣️ Why do the tickets come in different price tiers?

Whilst there is no physical difference. There is only a limited amount of tickets we can sell. Therefore we operate a festival style ticketing model. The earlier you buy your ticket the cheaper it will be.

🗣️ Do you do group discount? Stag/Hen etc

Yes, we offer a discounted ticket price for groups of 10 or more. These tickets can be found listed as the “Big Group Package!” above, orders for these tickets are restricted to a minimum of 10.

🗣️ Will there be more tickets available if the event is sold out?

Once this event is sold out, there will not be any additional tickets released. In addition to this we will be unable to sell them at the door due to maximum capacity and health and safety regulations.

🗣️ Is the venue accessible?

Our events take place at a variety of locations across the UK and Ireland. As each varies please ensure to check the specific venue's website for accessibility information.

🗣️ Can I resell my tickets?

Yes, if you are unable to attend an event you are welcome to sell your tickets on. We do not use names on tickets as a condition for entry.

🗣️ Are your events 18+?

All of our events are strictly 18+. A valid photographic ID may be requested on entry.

🗣️ What do I do if I cant find my tickets or confirmation email?

We use Fatsoma to sell tickets for our events. If you’re struggling to find your ticket, you can access their support channels via https://support.fatsoma.com/support/home

🗣️ Are there tickets available on the door?

We always recommend booking in advance as we cannot guarantee on the door entry. However, in certain instances there will be a limited number of tickets on a first come first served basis for sale on the door.

🗣️ I have more questions?

If you have additional questions and wish to contact us directly, don’t hesitate to drop us a DM on either Facebook (Daytime Disco) or Instagram (@daytimediscoevents)

In-line with normal consumer standards for ticket purchases, tickets for Daytime Disco events are non-refundable, on the condition that we not moved the event or canceled it. events.long_description:
Acclaimed indie band Flyte bring their signature blend of heartfelt lyricism and melodic craftsmanship to a special run of New Zealand shows this November.

Flyte have earned widespread acclaim for their refined songwriting and emotionally resonant sound, with a catalogue that showcases their evolution from classic British guitar pop to more expansive and introspective arrangements. Their releases have been celebrated for their lyrical honesty and rich harmonies, cementing their place as one of the UK’s most compelling contemporary bands.

Formed in London, Flyte are led by singer-songwriters Will Taylor and Nick Hill, whose close creative partnership underpins the band’s distinctive identity. They broke through with their debut album The Loved Ones and continued to build momentum with subsequent records, including This Is Really Going to Hurt and Flyte, earning praise for their timeless influences and modern sensibility. Their work captures themes of love, vulnerability and connection, delivered with a stripped-back elegance and attention to detail that has resonated with audiences worldwide.
For audiences in Aotearoa, these shows offer a rare opportunity to experience Flyte’s intimate and immersive live performance, bringing their finely crafted songs to life with warmth, precision and emotional depth.

events.long_description:
Presented by: Astral People & Handsome Tours
Neo-soul artist Greentea Peng arrives in Australia and New Zealand this November, delicately infusing hypnotic dub with seductive hip-hop swings and jazzy neo-soul excursions.
The South London born Greentea Peng is an artist whose work is guided by self-inquiry, shaped by the dualities she inhabits: pain and pleasure, engagement and withdrawal, expression and stillness. Her emotional literacy is transformed into a blend of neo-soul, dub and jazz, all draped in psychedelic textures.
After rediscovering her love for music while travelling - where she joined a local band in Mexico - a renewed sense of self-confidence propelled her return to London and the release of her 2018 EP, Sensi. The project marked the beginning of a distinctive sound carved from heavy, weighty narration, dubby grain, hissy textures and sparse arrangements. The six-track release is anchored by negative space that sits tightly side-chained to the kick, creating a breathing, pumping feel, while minimal melodic movements allow tension to build and swell around her earthy, soulful voice.
This early foundation continued to evolve, punctuated by notable moments such as her performance of "Downers" on COLORS, which garnered millions of views, as well as her television debut on Later... with Jools Holland on the BBC, where she performed her breakout track "Hu Man". These milestones paved the way for her 2021 debut album, MAN MADE, which she described as a record designed to resonate "more in your heart space, and less in your headspace".
Her latest offering, TELL DEM IT'S SUNNY, dives deeper into her enduring practice of self-witnessing - a work of affirmation, emotional maturity and radical self-acceptance. From "BALI SKIT PT. 1", a soundscape that rises and falls like the ribcage of a shadowy spirit, to "RAW", where we're once again met with Peng's poignant voice notes, the album showcases an artist continuing to explore her inner world with clarity and conviction.
Now, the psychedelic R&B soulstress returns to Australia and New Zealand this November, bringing her rich catalogue of deeply personal, genre-defying music to audiences once again.

events.long_description:
Tones of Silence; Futuna Chapel in Black & White with John Walsh, Patrick Reynolds & Andrew Barrie
John Walsh and Patrick Reynolds

Architecture writer John Walsh and photographer Patrick Reynolds discuss their city walking guides and the heritage places they reveal, bringing together Walsh’s deep knowledge of Aotearoa New Zealand architecture and Reynolds’ distinctive photographic eye.

About the speakers:

John Walsh is a leading New Zealand architecture writer. He edited Architecture New Zealand magazine for a decade, and has written numerous books on New Zealand architecture, among them the newly revised Auckland Architecture: A Walking Guide, which features photographs by Patrick Reynolds.

Patrick Reynolds is probably best known for his exceptional architectural and interior photographs that appear in publications such as Urbis and Vogue Living. However, over the past 20 years he has developed a highly successful parallel career as a leading photographer within New Zealand contemporary visual arts. As an exhibiting artist his work is about New Zealand landscape, nature, architecture, patterns of seeing, and – just as importantly – about the art and place of photography.

Professor Andrew Barrie

New Zealand-born architectural critic and designer, Prof. Andrew Barrie discusses the research and publication of Block maps, drawing on his work as an architectural critic, designer, author, and educator with deep connections to architecture in Japan and Aotearoa New Zealand.

About the speaker:

Professor Andrew Barrie is a New Zealand-born architectural critic and designer formerly based in Tokyo. After completing doctoral studies in Japan, Andrew was a project architect in the office of Toyo Ito, one of the world’s most innovative and influential architects, and later at Cheshire Architects in Auckland. Andrew own design work is widely celebrated, having won numerous awards in both Japan and NZ—including a prestigious named award from the New Zealand Institute of Architects—and has been exhibited nationally and internationally. He is a regular contributor to architecture and design journals and has authored three books on the work of Japanese architects. He has made significant contributions to architectural culture in New Zealand, recognized by the award (with the Block Foundation) of the NZIA’s Auckland Cup for services to architecture, and his election to the Royal Society of New Zealand.

Hailing from the music-filled streets of Melbourne, Australia, Shaun Kirk is an award-winning blues and soul troubadour recognized for his exceptional talent as a born entertainer. His unique talent has not only earned him many accolades but also much praise from fellow artists, such as three-time Grammy Award Winner Fantastic Negrito, who has declared his show as "One of the best one-man shows he’s ever seen!"

Kirk's vocals exude a gritty, soulful depth that seems to transcend far beyond his years, with critics continually acclaiming him as "one of the finest blues voices Australia has ever heard" (Buzz Mag). Complementing his vocal artistry, Kirk's vintage guitar tones and raw grooves pay tribute to the timeless influences that have shaped his musical journey, resulting in a distinctive sound fast becoming his own.

Shaun’s musical journey has taken him to stages all over the world, where he's not only performed but consistently sold out shows, leaving audiences enthralled by his magnetic presence. From iconic festival stages like Bluesfest Byron Bay, where he's become a familiar name, to sharing the billing with legends like Robert Plant of Led Zeppelin, John Mayer, Paolo Nutini, John Butler Trio, and The Teskey Brothers; Kirk's artistic prowess is in esteemed company. Moreover, he's also had the honour of opening for household names such as blues maestro Joe Bonamassa, soul sensation Allen Stone, and the indomitable Beth Hart; further solidifying his place in the landscape of contemporary music. This remarkable journey is a testament to Kirk's unmatched talent and ability to connect with audiences across genres and generations.

It’s a 70s rock musical of biblical proportions, and it’s back. Jesus Christ Superstar is heading to St James Theatre, and Wellington audiences are in for a treat. This production won the 2017 Olivier Award for Best Musical Revival and came fresh off an acclaimed 2023/24 tour of the United Kingdom. 
Jesus Christ Superstar explores the biblical events leading to the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ as seen through the eyes of his betrayer, Judas Iscariot. The story, told entirely through song, explores the personal relationships and struggles among Jesus, Judas, Mary Magdalene, Jesus’ disciples, his followers and the Roman Empire.
The 1970s rock score features lyrics and music by Emmy, GRAMMY, Oscar, and Tony winners Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber. Well-known numbers include I Don’t Know How to Love Him, Gethsemane, and Superstar.

Beethoven 9 - Wellington
The grand finale of the NZSO’s 2026 mainstage season features the grandest of symphonies: Beethoven’s Ninth.

Programme:
Dame Gillian Karawe Whitehead Hoata
Beethoven Symphony No. 9

Its audacious juxtaposition of styles, sounds and forces, including the revolutionary inclusion of a choir, marked the Ninth as a landmark work, not just for Beethoven but for music itself. Its monumental achievement and undeniable emotional power will be brought to stunning life with the help of Orpheus Choir Wellington and City Choir Dunedin.

Our essential need for community and connection is also at the heart of Dame Gillian Karawe Whitehead’s Hoata. Named for the Māori phase of the moon where the moon is barely visible, Hoata was written in 1979 during a cold northern hemisphere winter and evokes the icy blizzards and intense isolation that swirled around the composer as she wrote.

With a foot in both New Zealand and Australia, Stan Walker is one of Australasia’s finest pop/R&B singers. His show, Stan Walker: A Symphonic Experience Pōneke, brings him to the capital for an evening of his biggest hits. Accompanied by his full live band and a powerful orchestra, each song has been completely reimagined to create an unforgettable night of music. From Black Box and Take It Easy to I AM, Māori Ki Te Ao, and more, this is Stan Walker elevated into something cinematic, spiritual and powerful. 

Since winning the seventh season of Australian Idol in 2009, Stan Walker has gone on to release seven albums. The concert celebrates 17 years of music-making and cultural connection. It will be a night honouring the journey and the people who have been part of it every step of the way.

events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
GOODNIGHT NURSE ARE BACK… AGAIN

New Zealand pop-punk favourites celebrate 20 years of Always & Never with one final run of shows




To celebrate the 20th anniversary of their debut album Always & Never, the band are coming out of retirement one last time for The Always and Never (Again!) Tour - three final shows across New Zealand before they hang up their studded belts for good.

For the first time ever, Always & Never will also be available on limited-edition purple vinyl, with pre-orders opening Monday 31 August.

Playing Auckland’s Powerstation on Friday 13 November, the band then head south for a show at Loons in Christchurch on Thursday 19 November before what promises to be a final show for the ages at San Fran in Wellington on Friday 20 November. Tickets for all dates go on sale 12pm Thursday 3 September from eccles.co.nz

Released in 2006, their debut album, Always & Never, has remained a favourite among pop-punk fans over the years. That album was the beginning of a nine-year career for Goodnight Nurse. They played hundreds of shows throughout New Zealand and Australia, released two NZ Top 5 albums and scored five NZ Top 40 singles.

“When we got back together in 2023 for the My Chemical Romance show, it felt like there was something special in the air,” says lead singer Joel Little, who has gone on to write and produce hit songs with artists including Taylor Swift, Lorde and Khalid. “So when the 20th anniversary of Always & Never rolled around, we thought, what better way could we possibly celebrate this than by reliving the glory days one last time?”

“We started making music to have fun with our friends, and just for the simple joy of doing it,” says drummer Jaden Parkes, now one of the lead singers of hugely popular band Leisure and the longtime Head of A&R at Sony Music NZ. “Playing these songs live again takes you right back to that feeling.”

And for day one fans, there’s one more reason to make this final tour a must-see.

Original bass player and fan favourite Paul Taite will be joining the band onstage for the tour, playing the songs he helped shape and bringing Goodnight Nurse full circle 20 years after Always & Never first landed.

The Always and Never (Again!) Tour will be Goodnight Nurse’s final three shows in New Zealand. For real this time. Tickets on sale 12pm Thursday 3 September




Limited-edition vinyl avalible for pre-purchase

events.name: Saint Etienne tickets
events.venue: Meow Nui, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Presented by: Destroy All Lines
One of the UK’s most beloved and enduring pop groups, SAINT ETIENNE, are heading to Australia and New Zealand for the very last time. Following the announcement that their 2025 album International would be their final studio release, the iconic trio will take their celebrated catalogue on a farewell tour across the region this November and December.
Released in September 2025, International was met with rapturous acclaim, returning Saint Etienne to the UK Top 10 and reaffirming their status as one of Britain’s most treasured musical institutions. Now, fans across Australia and New Zealand will have the rare chance to experience the band’s shimmering, genre‑blurring sound live, one final time.
With a career spanning more than three decades, Saint Etienne’s songbook is rich with classics including ‘Only Love Can Break Your Heart’, ‘Spring’, ‘Nothing Can Stop Us’, ‘You’re In A Bad Way’, ‘He’s On the Phone’ and ‘Wood Cabin’ tracks that helped define an era of British pop and continue to resonate with audiences worldwide.
Formed in 1990 by Croydon natives Bob Stanley and Pete Wiggs, Saint Etienne struck gold from the outset with their debut single, a transformative cover of Neil Young’s ‘Only Love Can Break Your Heart’, which quickly became a club anthem. The arrival of vocalist Sarah Cracknell in 1991 completed the definitive lineup, her debut on ‘Nothing Can Stop Us’ and the Mercury Prize‑nominated album Foxbase Alpha cementing the group’s place in UK pop history.
Their follow‑up album So Tough soared into the UK Top 10, leading to a landmark moment in 1994 when Saint Etienne became the first band ever broadcast live from Glastonbury Festival.
Now, after decades of innovation, reinvention and irresistible pop craftsmanship, Saint Etienne prepare to say goodbye to Australian and New Zealand audiences.
A final bow from one of Britain’s most cherished groups which is not to be missed.

events.long_description:
Self-Hypnosis - Hypnotise Yourself
Self-hypnosis is a fantastic self-development tool. It can also be used for controlling pain, accelerated healing, letting go of limiting behaviours and a number of other applications. This workshop will provide you with a good insight into the world of hypnosis, demystify it and dispel the myths that surround it.
You’ll learn a structured method of taking yourself into hypnosis (informed by scientific research), some of the classic applications of self-hypnosis and evidence-based skills that will convince you without doubt of your ability to hypnotise yourself.
By the end of the workshop, you’ll be able to:
• Define and discuss hypnosis
• Practice self-hypnosis
• Create and write hypnosis scripts for personal change
• Use the language of self-hypnosis
• Relax hypnotically to deep levels
Tea and coffee provided but bring your lunch, pen and paper.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.long_description:
Beekeeping - Next Step
This is a practical and hands-on experience so bring your beekeeper’s outfit and your lunch. Please check your course instructions for more information on what you need to bring on the day.  The tutor can lend you a veil if you don't have one, please let the CEC office know a week before the course is due to run so this can be arranged.
The workshop starts in the classroom and is followed by a visit to a local apiary.  (Please note that you will working with live bees during the visit so there is a chance of being stung by one.)
If weather isn't suitable on the day, the morning session will still go ahead but the visit will be postponed to the next available Saturday.   Please note that if you can't make the catch-up visit, it's not possible to join in later courses due to number restrictions (a part-refund will be made). You must have done the Beginners' course first.
By the end of the workshop, you'll be able to:
• List the key steps in setting up a hive
• Describe how honey is extracted
• State what causes swarming and some ways of preventing it
• Describe what needs to be done to manage Varoa and American Foul Brood 
• Construct kitset frames for a honey super
• Open up and inspect a hive

Come join us for a fun-filled day of sewing and socializing at Karori Arts & Crafts!

About this Event



Come join us for a fun-filled day of sewing and socializing at Karori Arts & Crafts! Whether you're a seasoned pro or just starting out, this event is perfect for anyone who loves to sew. Bring your latest project or start something new - either way, you'll have a blast chatting with fellow sewing enthusiasts. Please do NOT attend if you are sick (even just a little bit!)

events.name: Courtney Barnett — Creature of Habit Tour
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Australian singer-songwriter Courtney Barnett is heading back to New Zealand five years after her last sell-out tour. The ‘Creature of Habit’ tour coincides with the release of her fourth studio album of the same name. The album is emotionally resonant and explores the central question: how to get out of your own way so you can truly feel your life. With singles Stay in Your Lane, and Site Unseen’ setting the tone, the album and concert mark a decisive new chapter in her musical evolution. Along with the latest music, she will delve into her extensive back catalogue. 
In addition to a Grammy nomination, Courtney has won multiple ARIAs (Australian Recording Industry Awards). She is known for a style that incorporates intimate storytelling with indie rock and bursts of raw grunge-like energy. Her blend of moody guitar, witty, anecdotal lyrics and laconic talk-singing has cemented her as “one of the most distinctive voices in indie music” (The Mancunion).

events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
GOODNIGHT NURSE ARE BACK… AGAIN

New Zealand pop-punk favourites celebrate 20 years of Always & Never with one final run of shows




To celebrate the 20th anniversary of their debut album Always & Never, the band are coming out of retirement one last time for The Always and Never (Again!) Tour - three final shows across New Zealand before they hang up their studded belts for good.

For the first time ever, Always & Never will also be available on limited-edition purple vinyl, with pre-orders opening Monday 31 August.

Playing Auckland’s Powerstation on Friday 13 November, the band then head south for a show at Loons in Christchurch on Thursday 19 November before what promises to be a final show for the ages at San Fran in Wellington on Friday 20 November. Tickets for all dates go on sale 12pm Thursday 3 September from eccles.co.nz

Released in 2006, their debut album, Always & Never, has remained a favourite among pop-punk fans over the years. That album was the beginning of a nine-year career for Goodnight Nurse. They played hundreds of shows throughout New Zealand and Australia, released two NZ Top 5 albums and scored five NZ Top 40 singles.

“When we got back together in 2023 for the My Chemical Romance show, it felt like there was something special in the air,” says lead singer Joel Little, who has gone on to write and produce hit songs with artists including Taylor Swift, Lorde and Khalid. “So when the 20th anniversary of Always & Never rolled around, we thought, what better way could we possibly celebrate this than by reliving the glory days one last time?”

“We started making music to have fun with our friends, and just for the simple joy of doing it,” says drummer Jaden Parkes, now one of the lead singers of hugely popular band Leisure and the longtime Head of A&R at Sony Music NZ. “Playing these songs live again takes you right back to that feeling.”

And for day one fans, there’s one more reason to make this final tour a must-see.

Original bass player and fan favourite Paul Taite will be joining the band onstage for the tour, playing the songs he helped shape and bringing Goodnight Nurse full circle 20 years after Always & Never first landed.

The Always and Never (Again!) Tour will be Goodnight Nurse’s final three shows in New Zealand. For real this time. Tickets on sale 12pm Thursday 3 September




Limited-edition vinyl avalible for pre-purchase

events.id: Richard Dawkins — 50 Years of The Selfish Gene-Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: Richard Dawkins — 50 Years of The Selfish Gene
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Richard Dawkins is a world-renowned evolutionary biologist. When published in 1976, his book, ‘The Selfish Gene’, reframed our understanding of life, behaviour, and human nature. Now, 50 years later, he is coming to Wellington to reflect on the book’s revolutionary legacy. He explores what fifty years of science has confirmed or challenged and explains why its core questions are more urgent today than ever before. 
‘The Selfish Gene’ has remained a cornerstone of modern science. It introduced the gene-centred view of evolution and coined the now-ubiquitous concept of the ‘meme’. The ideas in it ignited global debate and five decades of subsequent research. Richard Dawkins is one of the most consequential scientific communicators of our time, so don’t miss the rare opportunity to hear him speak in person.

events.long_description:
Business Training New Zealand Leadership & Management Part 3 Workshop
Our Leadership & Management Part 3 workshop is a practical skills training course designed for people in a leadership/management position.

About this Event



Leaders today are expected to be the driving force of their teams. They are constantly under pressure to lead effectively in a business environment that is characterised by constant change. Our leadership and management courses offer participants the opportunity to develop the necessary skills to embrace this challenge and lead their teams through these times with confidence and pride.

Our Leadership & Management - Part 3 workshop is a practical skills training course designed for people already in a leadership/management position, or those about to take up a new role, who want to explore the latest thinking and models for effective management and leadership and build on the techniques acquired in our Part 1 and 2 workshops.

In today’s world, emotional Intelligence is a critical and powerful component of effective leadership. This 2-day course will equip leaders with the skills to become more ‘people smart’ by developing ways to lead with emotional intelligence. Participants will also learn how to inspire their people with a shared vision and align teams to company goals, along with the tools to lead and manage change, ways to become a more influential and persuasive leader and the tools to raise awareness and manage unconscious bias in the workplace.

Course Outcomes

Assess your leadership strengths and identify opportunities for growth
Learn how to become a more inspirational and influential leader
Understand the importance of emotional intelligence as a key leadership skill
Learn how to lead with emotional intelligence, develop leadership self-awareness and become more ‘people smart’
Communicate your goals, vision and purpose with greater clarity, confidence and inspiration
Inspire and align your team to your shared vision and goals
Understanding change and learn how to lead change and growth in your organisation
Apply strategies to motivate and inspire your people to embrace change and strive for positive outcomes
Understand what unconscious bias is and recognise its effects on your people and your organisation
Explain how you can manage your own unconscious bias and implement steps to raise awareness and manage unconscious bias in the workplace

Course Prerequisite: Participants must have a good understanding of leadership and management fundamentals and/or have previously attended the Business Training New Zealand - Leadership & Management Part 1 & 2 course.

For more information or to book: email or call 04 974 8790

Explore your creativity through intuitive Neurographic Art and a soothing sound bath, blending mindful expression with deep relaxation.

About this Event


Meditate & Create
Neurographic Art & Sound Bath experience

 


Please try to arrive by 5:45pm so we can get everyone into the event and start on time at 6pm.

 

Neurographic Art is a simple, intuitive art practice that invites you to slow down, soften the mind, and turn your thoughts and feelings into lines, shapes, and patterns. There’s no right or wrong way to create, and no artistic experience is needed.

Alongside the art practice, you’ll be guided through a deeply relaxing sound bath featuring singing bowls, chimes and flutes. Let the sounds create space to settle, listen inward and connect with your creative flow.

Come as you are, explore without expectation, and leave with your own unique piece of art.





Please stay for a delicious plant-based dinner and dessert afterwards, included in your ticket!



Meet your Artist Rowena

Kia ora, I’m Rowena and I’ve been teaching art to kids, adults, retirees, and folks on the margins for 15 years. I aim to make art and creativity as inclusive as possible, especially for the people who say, ‘I can’t do art.’





Meet your Sound Healer Alexandra

Alexandra is a sound healing practitioner devoted to nurturing healing in both mind and body. She believes that sound vibration holds the power to expand consciousness and restore harmony and balance in our lives. Her journey into sound healing began with the realization of how deeply sound vibration was affecting her psyche, making her more mindful of the music she listens to and the intention it carries. Along the way, she has drawn inspiration from the Bhakti Lounge Kirtan. Their music has profoundly influenced her own sound healing practice, inspiring her to explore sound as a tool for transformation, connection, and inner peace.

Los Angeles post-punk band DECEITS has been building something real from the ground up. Since forming in 2021, longtime friends Kevin Moreno (Vocals/Instruments) and Francisco Saenz (Drums/Percussions) have self-released their entire catalog, quietly amassing millions of streams, selling out tours, and pressing vinyl that disappears just as quickly as it arrives. Their momentum has carried them from the underground to stages like Cruel World 2025 and across their first European tour, all while earning coverage from Post-Punk.com and the Los Angeles Times. DECEITS aren’t interested in playing it safe. Their take on post-punk rejects the genre’s colder edges in favor of something more alive, pulling in the color, rhythm, and emotional intensity of the Spanish-language music they grew up with. The result is a sound that feels both nostalgic and distinctly their own: moody, melodic, and impossible to stand still to.

events.name: Yīn Yīn - New Zealand Tour | Wellington
events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
Dutch groove-explorers YĪN YĪN are bringing disco, funk, psychedelia and dance to Wellington’s San Fran Friday 27 November and Auckland’s Tuning Fork on Saturday 28 November. 
Made up of Erik Bandt on guitar, Kees Berkers on drums, Jerôme Schere on keyboards and Remy Scheren on bass, YĪN YĪN are the kaleidoscopic instrumental quartet from Maastricht, Netherlands, renowned for their genre-bending records and transportive live experience. 
Emerging out of an experimental jam session in a remote ballet school village in 2017 that resulted in the making of their debut album The Rabbit That Hunts Tigers, the band have since created another three critically acclaimed albums and spent the better part of the last decade chasing rhythm across continents. 
With relentless international touring and performing everywhere from Fuji Rock Festival and Lowlands to North Sea Jazz Festival and Clockenflap they have been collecting sounds, textures and musical flavours like souvenirs, drawing from a multitude of influences such as ‘70s Thai Funk, Japanese City Pop and crate-dug global disco. Each project has evolved alongside the eager exploration to immerse their worldly experience into a sonic universe of their own.
Their latest of which,Yatta!, arrived in January 2026. A defining influence on Yatta! Is the cosmic allure of Italo Disco - the psychedelic futuristic dance music that emerged in Italy during the late 1970s and flourished throughout the 80s. “It has something of a mystique,” the band explains. 
“Because all the producers were using new recording techniques and effects and stuff like that, but there are not many pictures or videos of how they were creating things in the studio.You have to use your own fantasy and create your own story about how that music is created.”
This one sees the band into their most realised selves yet, translating into an unmissable live experience. “We tried to make a mix of songs that are very energetic and danceable and are party starters, but also have songs that take you on trips and are more easy. People can also just chill and relax and listen to the music and enjoy it.” - YĪN YĪN 

Aotearoa, get ready to move. YĪN YĪN are set to take on Aotearoa for the first time for two shows this November.


San Fran holds a Supervised License. Minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue.

events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
After a sold-out tour in early 2026, Sir Tony Robinson brings his talk show back to Wellington. Catch ‘An Audience with Sir Tony Robinson’ at The Opera House. The television presenter, actor, and award-winning writer has an impressive decades-long career. Tony will divulge behind-the-scenes stories from his life on and off screen. He’ll then read from his fiction debut ‘The House of Wolf’, an epic tale of Alfred the Great and the bloody birth of England. He won’t hog the microphone the whole time — you’ll also get the chance to ask him questions. Expect masterful storytelling from Tony and lots of laughs from the audience. 

You might have seen Tony play Baldrick in Rowan Atkinson’s cult 80s sitcom ‘Blackadder’. In the show, his “I have a cunning plan” catchphrase and comedic timing made him a household name. He’s also celebrated for his work in historical broadcasting, which includes presenting 20 seasons of ‘Time Team’. His infectious enthusiasm for history continued, as he wrote his first novel aged 78. The book delves into the (often grim) realities of life for ordinary people caught between Saxon kings and Viking raiders.

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Bicycle Maintenance for Beginners
Have you recently started riding a bicycle and want to make sure you can take care of it properly? Or have you been riding for ages, but have always been scared to fix anything yourself?
Are you unsure of how to pump your tyres, or how much oil your chain needs? Find yourself fumbling for words when trying to describe that clunking sound to the guy in the bike shop?
This one day course lays bare the nuts and bolts of bicycle mechanics for absolute beginners, as well as those with a little experience. Through practical experience working with your own bicycle, you will find out what needs to be done to keep it running smoothly. We’ll cover what to look out for when things start to wear out, and how to check for problems, so you can be confident your bicycle is safe to ride. You will also learn how to fix some of the most common mechanical problems, and learn about the correct terminology and tools to use.
Those who feel intimidated in bike shops are especially welcome in this course. No question is a stupid question!
Bringing a bike to work on is essential, preferably one that you are riding regularly, because the best way to learn is by building familiarity with your own ride. E-bikes are welcome, although the extra weight can mean they are more challenging to work on. Regardless of whether your bike is in pristine condition, or desperately in need of TLC, it is welcome on the course – bikes showing a bit more wear can be useful for the learning of the whole group.

events.long_description:
Los Angeles post-punk band DECEITS has been building something real from the ground up. Since forming in 2021, longtime friends Kevin Moreno (Vocals/Instruments) and Francisco Saenz (Drums/Percussions) have self-released their entire catalog, quietly amassing millions of streams, selling out tours, and pressing vinyl that disappears just as quickly as it arrives. Their momentum has carried them from the underground to stages like Cruel World 2025 and across their first European tour, all while earning coverage from Post-Punk.com and the Los Angeles Times. DECEITS aren’t interested in playing it safe. Their take on post-punk rejects the genre’s colder edges in favor of something more alive, pulling in the color, rhythm, and emotional intensity of the Spanish-language music they grew up with. The result is a sound that feels both nostalgic and distinctly their own: moody, melodic, and impossible to stand still to.

This show is at Space Academy in Christchurch

events.id: Eric Idle — An Evening of Idle Conversation-St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: Eric Idle — An Evening of Idle Conversation
events.venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Relive the highs and bitter lows of one of the most beloved comedians and writers of all time. Eric Idle sits down to tell his incredible life story, live on stage at the St James Theatre in Wellington. From the giddy heights of Monty Python success to the trauma of childhood — this is unscripted and candid. The audience will also get the chance to put their own questions to him live on stage.

An Evening of Idle Conversation covers sixty years of show business. Eric will recall memories of the friends he has loved and lost including Graham Chapman, George Harrison, and Robin Williams. He’ll also cover fortunes made and squandered, feuds, reunions, a brush with cancer, and why, at 83, he is still looking on the bright side of life.

Along with five other comics Eric formed Month Python in 1969. The troupe’s absurdist sketches continue to influence comedy more fifty years later. Eric is perhaps most famous for writing the song Always Look on the Bright Side of Life, The Rutles (the world’s first mockumentary), and the musical Spamalot.

DOORS OPEN 6:00pm
SHOW START 7:00pm

Leaving Dublin, Ireland where he was born and raised until the age of 22, David got drunk on travel and never quite hit sobriety of it. He has lived and worked in twelve countries and visited over eighty. His shows draw on his wide travels, cultural observations, attempts at language study, (occasional) international drinking session(s) and being a mildly confused immigrant. 
David is the winner of the prestigious annual San Francisco Comedy Competition, (previous finalists include Robin Williams, Ellen DeGeneres and Dana Carvey) and runner-up in the Moth’s largest US Grandslam storytelling competition. Also a bestselling writer, David recorded his debut special Documented for Dry Bar Comedy in 2019, his follow up Cultural Appreciation in 202, and his award winning show Shelf Help in 2025. He has been featured on TED.com, Sirius XM, Just For Laughs, Netflix is a Joke Festival, RTE’s Late Late Show, The Irish Independent, Inc, NPR, and the Huffington Post among others. A festival favorite, David's videos have also gone viral many times over with over 800 million views and a social following of over 2 million people. More info: davidnihill.com

2026 NZFSS Conference
📍1 - 4 December 2026

Conference Theme:
At the Confluence: Communities, Catchments, and our Freshwater Futures - Ngā Rerenga E Tūtaki Ana

Our 2026 conference explores the confluence: the place where flows meet, merge, and reshape one another. In freshwater science, confluences are dynamic hydrological junctions which create unique habitats and environments. For this conference it represents the meeting of people, knowledge systems, innovations, and aspirations that shape the future of wai in Aotearoa.

Hosting the conference in Te Whanganui‑a‑Tara/Wellington, where urban streams like Waimapihi and Kumutoto meet the great harbour Te Whanganui‑a‑Tara provides a powerful metaphor for integration across urban waters, catchments, and communities. As Aotearoa navigates changing climate pressures, evolving policy landscapes, disruptive technologies, and growing community involvement, this confluence becomes a space for meaningful collaboration and forward‑thinking action.

We look forward to welcoming you to WLG!

Keeping Ahead of Change, Managing Risk & Building Confidence

About this Event



9:00 Welcome and Industry Update

Industry update
Key issues to keep on the radar

9:30 Around the Table: What Are You Dealing With?

Share the key compliance issues and challenges you're currently facing
Identify common themes across organisations, buildings and roles
Share solutions, experiences and lessons learned

10:30 Morning Tea

10:45 Compliance Schedules: Keeping Pace with Changing Guidance & Interpretations

Strategies for updating and amending schedules

events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
New York based songwriter and composer Allegra Krieger brings her singular blend of folk, rock and indie pop to San Fran on 3 December, joined by special guest Elly Mae.

Known for songwriting that is intimate, understated and deeply observant, Krieger pairs soulful vocals with raw, vulnerable lyricism, moving through themes of love, loss and self-discovery with a striking sense of emotional clarity. Her work has earned praise from the New York Times, who described her as a “deceptively understated songwriter,” while Paste has celebrated the distinctive poetry running through her music. 

Having shared stages with artists including Jana Horn, Fust, Johanna Samuels, Shalom and Charlotte Cornfield, Krieger has steadily carved out a space of her own within contemporary indie songwriting, creating music that feels equally at home in moments of quiet reflection and full-band intensity. 

Opening the evening is Pōneke songwriter Elly Mae, whose dreamy guitar-led folk-noir draws from the textures of The Brian Jonestown Massacre, PJ Harvey and Mazzy Star. Since first appearing on Wellington stages in early 2025, she has gone on to perform at Newtown Festival, CubaDupa and Flying Nun’s A Month of Saturdays live series, with RNZ describing her sound as a “woozy ethereal slice of dreampop.” 

Together, the two artists make for an evening of evocative songwriting, atmospheric guitars and music built around the power of close listening.







San Fran holds a Supervised License, meaning minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue. Minors are of course not allowed to purchase alcohol under any circumstance.

events.name: Yoga Nidra
events.venue: Awhi Yoga and Wellbeing Centre, 15 Johnston St., Wellington
events.long_description:
Unwind from the stresses of the week and start your weekend in a state of relaxation. Yoga Nidra, often referred to as "yogic sleep," is a deeply restorative practice that promotes physical relaxation, mental clarity, and emotional balance. It's the perfect way to rejuvenate your mind, body, and soul: your hinengaro, tinana and wairua.

Yoga nidra is a powerful technique that directly works to heal your mind by removing samskaras - untying knots and mental impressions. This practice of learning to relax consciously is well regarded as an antidote for stress, anxiety, poor sleep amongst other health benefits.

Everyone is welcome to experience the profound benefits of Yoga Nidra, and no prior experience is required. For some people, however, Yoga Nidra’s prolonged stillness or internal focus can bring up strong emotions, memories, and/or sensations. You are encouraged to listen and respond in a way that feels safe for you — adjusting your position, keeping your eyes open, grounding yourself, or stepping out of the room at any time.

Yoga Nidra may not be suitable for everyone. If you are experiencing acute mental health challenges, unprocessed trauma, or conditions that make stillness or internal focus difficult, we recommend seeking guidance from a qualified healthcare provider or speaking with the teacher before participating.

events.long_description:
Summer Tour - Kāpiti
Don't miss some Baroque French and Italian delights with NZSO Concertmaster Vesa-Matti Leppänen and Aotearoa New Zealand soprano Anna Leese.

It is astonishing to consider the musical impact Giovanni Pergolesi made, considering he died of tuberculosis at the age of 26. Like Mozart, his early demise quickly became the stuff of legend — hundreds of works were (often falsely) ascribed to this Italian late-Baroque genius, while rumours swirled that his death was the result of murderous jealousy from musical rivals.

Led by NZSO Concertmaster Vesa-Matti Leppänen, we survey some of Pergolesi’s most brilliant opera — La serva padrona, Adriano in Siria, L’Olimpiade and Il prigionier superbo. We are delighted to have Aotearoa New Zealand soprano Anna Leese join us as we delve into music that glories in resplendent Italian Baroque colours and textures.

We complete this magnificent concert with a detour into the French-Baroque, with a suite from Jean-Philippe Rameau's Platée. C’est magnifique!

Generously supported by Ainsley Walter

events.long_description:
Kāpiti Food Fair 2026
Make a day of it. Gather your friends and whānau, plan your destination getaway, secure your accommodation and VIP parking early, and get ready to savour the flavours, sounds, and spirit of summer at Kāpiti Food Fair 2026.

Kāpiti Food Fair is where great food, great people, and great summer memories come together. As one of the Wellington region’s most anticipated food festivals, it offers a vibrant celebration of New Zealand’s food culture, bringing together the very best producers, artisans, chefs, entertainers, and food lovers for an unforgettable destination day out.

More than just a food event, Kāpiti Food Fair is a lively summer festival that celebrates the incredible talent and diversity of New Zealand’s food and beverage industry. Visitors can sample and shop their way through an exciting United Nations of flavours, discovering artisan products, boutique beverages, handcrafted treats, international street food, fresh produce, specialty ingredients, and unique home and kitchen products. It is a place to try, buy, eat, drink, relax, and uncover new favourites.

On the menu for 2026 ……. up to 10,000+ visitors, 250 vendor sites including a Kāpiti Artisan Producer Zone, an off-licence Liquor Zone, a Licenced Bar & Main Stage, the Seriously Pickled Kāpiti Kitchen, the Kāpiti Ice Cream Dining Room, FREE kid’s zone, ZEAL Zone buskers, roving street performers and much more!

Mazengarb Reserve Paraparaumu Kāpiti Coast
10am to 5pm RAIN or SHINE

TICKET COSTS
EARLY BIRD by 8 Nov:
$18 Adults | $13 Gold Card or Student ID (+ booking fees)

STANDARD from 9 Nov:
$23 Adults | $18 Gold Card or Student ID (+ booking fees)

AT GATE:
$30 Adults | $25 Gold Card or Student ID (Eftpos ONLY)

FREE up to 12 years ANYTIME

PARKING OPTIONS: $13 VIP & Gold Coin

MERCH (not sold online): $3 Bags

Tickets sold online at Humanitix – OPENING in EARLY September.

Booking fees will be added to the cost of your ticket and paid at check-out. Booking fees cover Humanitix costs, and everything else goes to their education projects that help to change lives. Kāpiti Food Fair has chosen to support Manaiakalani Education Trust that supports Māori, Pasifika, and disadvantaged learners in Aotearoa to increase student outcomes and get equal access to digital education.

TOP TIPS for a FANTASTIC DAY at the Kāpiti Food Fair:

1. Have your VIP parking and gate entry tickets ready for scanning.

2. Bring a gold coin for parking koha donations if VIP parking is not purchased.

3. Pack a hat and sunscreen – complimentary SPF is available if you need it.

4. Bring a picnic blanket to relax, enjoy the ambiance, and savor treats, plenty of seating and a shaded picnic zone under the trees!

5. BYO your own chair and a chilly bin for purchases.

6. Plan your foodie route with the Site Map – Browse the Site Map now >> https://kapitifoodfair.co.nz/visitors/visitor-site-map

7. Visit the Licenced Bar (EFTPOS ONLY) & Main Stage and relax over a local craft brew, wine, cocktails and delicious cider while enjoying the party vibe of the rhythmic grooves all day long! Children welcome with parent or guardian.

8. MOST vendors accept EFTPOS or bank transfer. BYO cash as there is no ATM.

INFORMATION FOR VISITORS:
#KāpitiFoodFair #FoodFestival #KFF2026 #SomethingForEveryone #VisitKāpiti

VISITOR PARKING MAP
Go to our website to view full >> https://kapitifoodfair.co.nz/visitors/visitor-info

GATE ENTRY
BUY tickets ONLINE BEFORE arriving to streamline entry and save money upfront and spend more on delicious food at the Fair! Have your tickets ready to scan at Gate Entry. Skip the queue, walk straight in with your ticket – no waiting in line at Gate Entry to buy a more expensive ticket on the day!

OR ON THE DAY, scan our ticket QR CODE on site to purchase ONLINE at Standard ticket prices:
$23 Adult, $18 Gold Card or Student ID, FREE up to 12 years.

AT GATE on the day for last minute purchase at PREMIUM prices – best option, park off site in a GOLD COIN parking zone and walk to Gate Entry if wanting to buy a ticket on the day:
$30 Adult, $25 Gold Card or Student ID, FREE up to 12 years (EFTPOS ONLY).

TRANSPORT & PARKING
Allow extra travel time as the roads will be busy with many others making their way to the Fair.

BUY VIP parking online when purchasing your tickets to access VIP parking on site at Mazengarb Reserve. Your VIP parking ticket will be scanned once you have entered Scaife Dr and will let you conveniently park all day for just $13!

NO VIP parking ticket? Head to a managed GOLD COIN parking zone shown on our PARKING MAP. Walk the short distance to the Fair and enjoy the vibe along the way with many other visitors arriving and departing!

DISABLED/MOBILITY parking is FREE and near Gate Entry 2, with parking marshals ready to assist. Let VIP parking scanners at the Scaife Dr Barrier Arm know that you need disabled/mobility parking and they will wave you through.

LOCALS: We recommend walking, running, biking (plenty of bike racks and lock-up options on site) – Or catch the train from Waikanae or Paekākāriki and board the FREE bus from Paraparaumu Station (timetable below).

HEADS UP: MEADOW COURT entry will be CLOSED, and Realm Drive car park will be OPEN as a GOLD COIN site with a fenced pathway to tarmac near Gate Entry 2.

FREEDOM CAMPING options in Kāpiti as Mazengarb Reserve is locked each night and camping is not permitted – click here >> https://www.kapiticoast.govt.nz/explore-kapiti/recreation/freedom-camping/

FREE Bus Schedule (no dogs permitted except guide dogs)
CATCH the TRAIN to Paraparaumu Station and board the FREE Bus on the half hour for a short ride to and from the Fair.

Depart Paraparaumu Station Intercity Bus Stop, Main Rd, Southbound:
10.13am, 10.43am, 11.13am, 11.43am, 12.13pm, 12.43pm, 1.13pm, 1.43pm, 2.13pm, 2.43pm, 3.13pm, 3.43pm, 4.13pm.

Depart Mazengarb Reserve:
10.43am, 11.13am, 11.43am, 12.13pm, 12.43pm, 1.13pm, 1.43pm, 2.13pm, 2.43pm, 3.13pm, 3.43pm, 4.13pm, 4.43pm, 5.13pm.

ENTERTAINMENT
ENJOY LIVE MUSIC all day on the Main Stage performed by exciting Kiwi bands that will have you partying to rhythmic grooves all day long! Love cooking? Visit the Seriously Pickled Kāpiti Kitchen Stage for live demos, or head to the ZEAL Zone for local talent and circus acts. There’s also a supervised FREE kids’ zone for families and plenty of roving street performers.

ON SITE
BYO cash as there is no ATM. MOST vendors accept EFTPOS or bank transfer.

Kāpiti Food Fair bags available at Gate Entry or INFO HUB for $3.

INFO HUB will operate to answer ALL visitor questions, and for LOST property, and free BAG STORAGE.

On-site paramedic for any emergency.

Flush portaloos near Gate 1 & 2 and two disabled toilets (one inside Pavilion and another accessed externally from Scaife Dr). Flush wahine/tane toilets available inside Pavilion and at some GOLD COIN parking zones (see PARKING MAP).

Crowd friendly dogs on lead are welcome – FREE water for pets and humans at the INFO Hub and Licenced Bar.

Kāpiti Food Fair Site Map is smoke & vape FREE.

LICENCED BAR
Relax in the Licenced Bar (EFTPOS ONLY) & Main Stage with a local craft brew, wine, cocktails and delicious cider. Children welcome with parent or guardian. CHEERS to that!

ENTERTAINMENT
View full programme details at our website >>
https://kapitifoodfair.co.nz/visitors/entertainment-programme

MAIN STAGE
Expect an exciting line-up with a vibing party theme!

FREE Kids Zone with Kāpiti Castles and Daizy Design Face Painting (donations welcome).

Whether attending with friends, whānau, workmates, or a foodie tribe, there is truly something for everyone. Families can enjoy the welcoming festival atmosphere, food enthusiasts can explore emerging culinary trends, and Christmas shoppers can get a head start on seasonal gifting while stocking the pantry for summer entertaining.

The festival experience extends well beyond food. Visitors can soak up the summer vibe with live performances from exciting Kiwi bands on the Main Stage, watch talented local wahine showcase their culinary skills during inspiring cooking demonstrations, and unwind in the licensed bar before heading back out to continue their delicious adventure. Every corner of the event is designed to create joy, spark curiosity, and encourage people to connect through shared experiences.

SPONSORSHIP
Thank you to our amazing Sponsors who support our sustainability journey. We value their commitment. It's what makes the Kāpiti Food Fair possible!

Kāpiti Ice Cream

Kāpiti Food Fair is a recipient of the Major Events Fund

The Fair is a commercial event however we have a social agenda too. We choose to support Kāpiti Community Patrol, No 49 Squadron Air Cadets, Paraparaumu College, and Work Ready Kāpiti. We contract their services to help run key logistics like visitor parking & gate entry, crowd security and waste minimisation. In 2025 we achieved a remarkable 98% waste diversion from landfill. In 2026 we will work towards achieving the same result.

events.long_description:
Tui Brewery Express: The Ultimate Christmas Party!
Climb aboard The Tui Express for the ultimate end of year office Christmas party! This is the perfect workplace celebration that beats the standard corporate dinner, making it an unforgettable scenic journey aboard our premium carriages. It’s the ultimate way to reward your hardworking team, swap out the boring boardroom, thank your favorite clients, and celebrate the year's wins with a spectacular Sunday on the rails.

The undisputed crown jewel of this journey is our passage through the spectacular Manawatū Gorge. With the old highway permanently closed, the rail line offers an exclusive, front row seat to this rugged natural wonder. Watch the dramatic river below and feel the history as we steam through the gorge's tunnels. There is no better place to capture an epic, casual end of year team photo than from our open air viewing platform, the ultimate vantage point for ditching the laptops, hearing the thunderous echo of the steam locomotive, and catching the crisp air of the Manawatū Gorge.

The festive celebrations start the second you step on board! Throughout the trip, our onboard licensed café carriage will be open. Your crew can sit back, relax, and purchase a range of alcoholic and non alcoholic refreshments to toast to your Q4 wins, along with hot espresso coffees and plenty of food, sweet treats, and snacks right from the rails as the stunning scenery rolls by.

Our tracks lead straight to Mangatainoka Station. Upon arrival, step off the platform and stretch your legs with a flat, leisurely 15 minute walk to the world famous Tui Brewery, or hop directly onto one of our dedicated transfer buses waiting for your group. Once at the brewery, relax and toast to your team's successes in the iconic historic grounds. Forget the awkward office Secret Santa and the sad boardroom sausage rolls, your ticket includes a delicious, hearty BBQ buffet lunch and a complimentary Tui beverage (or non alcoholic alternative) to celebrate a successful year together!

Your ticket covers your return journey from your chosen departure station in beautifully appointed premium carriages alongside exclusive rail only views of the Manawatū Gorge, rugged cliffs, and historic tunnels. You will have unrestricted access to the open air viewing platform for unbeatable team bonding, sightseeing, and staff photography, plus full access to the onboard licensed café carriage selling drinks, coffees, and snacks. At the destination, you get a freshly prepared festive BBQ buffet lunch inside the iconic Tui Brewery grounds, one complimentary Tui beer, cider, or non alcoholic beverage, and free transfer buses between Mangatainoka Station and the brewery.

Approximate Timetable(Sunday 6 December 2026)

events.long_description:
UK music’s biggest underdogs, indie rock juggernauts The Reytons, keep charging forward on their unstoppable rise. Having flirted with overseas territories successfully over the past 5 years, the band are now heading out on their very first World Tour, and have announced their return to Australia and New Zealand this November and December

Renowned for their raucous live shows, and touted by many as the best live act of their generation, the British 4-piece pride themselves on their honesty and pure energy. Having taken their native UK by storm, with number one albums, sold out park shows and major festival headlines, the lads from Rotherham are taking on the world with their upcoming world tour.

In 2025 alone, they toured the UK, headlined Tramlines Festival and the iconic Wembley Arena. The upcoming world tour is a huge statement for a band who have hurdled every obstacle with nothing other than blue-collar grit and determination. It cements them as a band at the top of British music. The Reytons also recently announced their fourth studio album A Love Letter To A Broken Town - due for release in July.

Rooted in the rough around the edges humour and honesty of everyday life, The Reytons continue to channel their origins into everything they do, and A Love Letter To A Broken Town sees them staying true to those roots while pushing their sound forward with confidence and intent.

“I honestly feel like this album is the best we’ve ever done!” explains frontman Jonny Yerrell. "A lot of bands and artists like to change direction later in their careers, but that’s just not us. We absolutely love the style of music we make, the social commentary aspects and the people who turn up to jump around with us. Why would we change? Expect more, just bigger and better with a few surprises on the side! "

San Fran holds a Supervised License, meaning minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue. Minors are of course not allowed to purchase alcohol under any circumstance.

events.long_description:
New York hardcore that’s been flipping off the purists for nearly 20 years.

Blast it with jazz horns. Get it plucked to buggery by banjo (yes, hardcore banjo!). Have a good old stomp in the riff swamp and chug out an irrefutable melody. Keep it dynamic and stab it with venom.

Formed back in 2009, Show Me The Body put the sludge back in the morass of modern life.  

Wielding a clash of banjos, bass, drums and electronics, each song seems to gain gears. From slow burners to crashing crescendoes, and a fresh album in tow that ups the ante and draws a new line in the sand.

Dancing at the end of the end. Under the overpass, down the alley, in the basement.

Joining Show Me The Body at all headline shows is Evanora: Unlimited is a multi-medium project from Oakland, California artist Orion Ohana.

Evanora Unlimited Also known Marjorie W.C Sinclair, a secondary & initially secret “catch-all” side project made up of miscellaneous music separate from the Evanora project; evolving over time, has found a harmonious role to the universe of Evanora.

They helped open the door for a more playful, soulful and inventive style of hip hop, collaborated with a then- emerging J Dilla, worked with visionary director Spike Jonze, and proved that creativity could be just as powerful as bravado. Their influence can still be heard across modern hip hop, while their timeless live show continues to win over audiences around the world.
Featuring Imani, Slimkid3, Fatlip and DJ Cee Brown, this is your chance to experience one of hip hop's defining groups live.

events.name: Uncle Acid and The Deadbeats AUS / NZ Tour
events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
UK psychedelic heavyweights Uncle Acid & The Deadbeats return to Australia and New Zealand this December, bringing their dark, hypnotic live show to stages across the country.
The brainchild of Kevin Starrs, Uncle Acid & The Deadbeats have spent over a decade carving out a singular space within the global heavy music landscape. Since emerging in 2009 from the depths of the British underground, the band have built a reputation for their unmistakable fusion of warped psychedelic pop, downer blues and doom-metal intensity.
Too bold and idiosyncratic to be easily defined, Uncle Acid’s sound is steeped in haunting melodies, layered vocal harmonies and eerie, cinematic arrangements, offset by crushing riffs and a persistent sense of unease. It’s a sonic world that feels both deeply nostalgic and completely otherworldly, cementing Uncle Acid & The Deadbeats as one of the most compelling live acts in contemporary rock.
With their last visit to our shores in 2020, Australian audiences can expect a set that traverses the band’s cult catalogue, delivered with the immersive intensity that has made them a must-see worldwide.

events.name: Somatic Breathwork Journey
events.venue: Mangaroa Farm, 98 Whitemans Valley Road, Te Awa Kairangi, Upper Hutt
events.long_description:
Join Amy Webber and Mangaroa Farms for a journey into your breath.

Somatic Breathwork™ is a full embodiment experience designed to help you release stress, trauma, emotions and stuck energy from the body. This is a modality that utilizes your own breath to help shed the layers of yourself that no longer serve, making room for you to call in what will help facilitate change within your life.

Somatic Breathwork™ uses a consciously connected breath pattern to help you tap into your body's innate inner intelligence and find the areas that need clearing. Coupling the breath with immersive music may result in different forms of cathartic emotional releases such as laughing, moving, crying, yelling, and shaking. All forms of expression are encouraged as it allows the body to move any pent up energy and create space for the second half of the breathwork journey.

A gentler breathing technique is used in the second half of the session to help you connect with who you truly are. Together we can use the breath to call in how you want to show up in the world, the changes you want to make, and allow you to see clearly what it would be like to live your best life.

Join Amy Webber and Mangaroa Farms for this immersive journey into your mind and heart. Any questions, please email amy@mangaroa.org

events.long_description:
North Pole Express Kapiti: 10am - Saturday, 19 December 2026
Be whisked away on the North Pole Express to meet Santa, sing, and celebrate this special time of year.

About this Event


'Nice List' presale: 12pm, 25 June 2026 - 5pm, 1 July 2026. Password required.
Public sales commence 1 September 2026.
No tickets will be held during presale, any remaining tickets will be offered to the public from 12pm on 1 September 2026. To join the 'Nice List' visit the .
If you would like to purchase a private carriage for your group on this service, please email prior to 22 June 2026.



Join the magical journey to meet Santa!
Your tickets include:
Entertainers
Carolling
Iced cocoa
Cookies
Souvenir Mug
A special souvenir from Santa
Santa
Extra surprises along the way
Our Candy Class and Claus Class Guests travel in comfort and receive extra treats along the way.


Prepare to be surrounded by the magic and wonder of the Christmas season!
Families will love the magical train ride in one of our specially decorated carriages. You’ll meet Santa, sing, and celebrate this special time of year.
Set to the sounds of carols passengers are invited to join us to be whisked away on the North Pole Express. Delight in the magic of Christmas as the train departs for a journey to collect Santa who has been magically transported to an undisclosed location along the tracks.
From the distance the North Pole Express arrives then the train Conductors invite you and the other passengers to climb aboard shouting “All aboard!”.


All Aboard
During the first leg of the journey wide-eyed children of all ages are invited to engage with characters who are eager to hear what makes the Christmas season special to them.
You’ll meet the conductor, and join in the fun singing and dancing with your hosts and a few other characters who will appear in your carriage on the journey.
At the 'North Pole' Cocoa Class passengers enjoy their iced chocolate from their souvenir mug, and a delicious cookie served by our North Pole Express hosts. Candy and Claus Class passengers will be served aboard the train on the way to the North Pole.
Along the journey Santa appears in your carriage to present each passenger with their very own Christmas ornament. During the trip, characters in each carriage lead passengers in carolling and entertainment as the train makes its way back home.
Children UNDER 2 years (0-23 months) and travelling on the lap of an Adult are FREE. All Passengers 2 years old and over must hold a purchased ticket.

Please note: Seating in our Candy and Claus Classes is strictly limited. Candy and Claus Class Guests receive some extra surprises and treats along the way.
Seating in all carriages is arranged in a configuration of 4 seats as per normal train travel. North Pole Express always endeavour to ensure those who book more than 4 seats are seated in close proximity to each other to ensure they can enjoy the experience together. Children under the age of 2 and travelling on the lap of an adult travel for free.
Wheelchair access: Due to the age and design of the carriages it is not possible to board whist seated in a wheelchair as the entrance is stairs and the doorways are very narrow. However we will be pleased to convey passengers of limited mobility whenever possible provided they can step onto the train from the platform, climbing a step and move to their reserved seats with the help of an able bodied carer. Our crew would assist guiding the passenger up the step onto the train and arrange for the storage of the wheelchair in the guards van. The wheelchair must be able to be folded up and cannot be used on the train. Please let us know when booking if you need wheelchair assistance.

Photo credit: John Bovis

events.id: Astrophotography Masterclass: Capture the Southern Sky-Star Safari Observatory, 1169 Ponatahi Road, Carterton-Event Finder
events.name: Astrophotography Masterclass: Capture the Southern Sky
events.venue: Star Safari Observatory, 1169 Ponatahi Road, Carterton
events.long_description:
Spend an evening under one of the world’s finest dark skies and learn how to photograph the Milky Way, constellations and deep-sky objects. This immersive masterclass is designed for curious explorers, hobby photographers and anyone who has ever looked up and wished they could capture what they saw.

Your instructor is an experienced astro-educator, and you’ll be taken step by step through the art and science of night-sky photography with DSLR or mirrorless cameras. You’ll learn how to focus at infinity, choose the best camera settings, build compositions under the Milky Way, and work with RAW files, noise control and exposure strategy. You’ll photograph live star fields and leave with images you can genuinely be proud of.

No astronomy expertise or prior astrophotography experience is required — just your curiosity. Bring a camera and tripod if you have them, but if not, you can still attend, learn from telescope-linked imaging feeds, and gain the skills and confidence to shoot the cosmos on your own.

Held at Star Safari, right in the Wairarapa dark-sky heartlands, this experience takes place under the same southern skies recognised by Lonely Planet as one of the world’s top stargazing destinations. If you’ve ever wanted to try astrophotography, this is the moment, and this is the place.

What you’ll gain:
- Confidence to shoot the night sky
- Proven camera settings and workflow
- Real photos of the Milky Way and southern star fields
- Knowledge you can use anywhere the southern sky is visible
- A rare, premium learning experience under a world-class sky

Perfect for couples, travellers, creatives, astronomy lovers, and anyone who wants a deeper connection to the night.

Spaces are limited to keep the experience personal.

events.name: Race Of Champions
events.venue: Hnry Stadium, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Race Of Champions is an internationally renowned event. Winners from a range of racing disciplines go head-to-head on a purpose-built tarmac circuit constructed inside Hnry Stadium. Unlike traditional motorsport events, every driver competes in identical cars, putting the focus firmly on skill behind the wheel. 

The first drivers confirmed for Wellington include four-time Formula 1 World Champion Sebastian Vettel and Formula 1 race winner Valtteri Bottas. Supercars champion Chaz Mostert and New Zealand rally star Hayden Paddon are also coming. More competitors are to be announced for this Wellington exclusive event. 

Since its launch in 1988, Race Of Champions has brought together stars from Formula 1, World Rally Championship, IndyCar, NASCAR, Le Mans, and other top-tier racing series. Previous competitors have included Fernando Alonso, Lando Norris, Valentino Rossi, Mika Häkkinen, and Michael Schumacher.

events.long_description:
Tora Bombora - 2027
The Return of Tora Bombora.

Wellington Anniversary Weekend, 22 - 24 January, 2027

After five incredible festivals and a four year hiatus, Tora Bombora is returning for the sixth edition - Tora Bombora Ono

For four summers, the paddocks sat quietly. The stages slept, the winds kept moving across the hills, and the coast returned to its familiar rhythm. But some things never really leave. They simply wait.

————————————————————

Ticket System and Key Dates

'Tora Bombora Whānau'
To keep the community close and the kaupapa even closer, if you have attended Tora Bombora in the past, you are already 'Tora Bombora Whānau' which gives you first access to tickets (keep an eye on your inbox). The remaining tickets will be released to people who sign up via our website to become a part of the 'Tora Bombora Whānau'.

How it works
1. Enter 'Tora Bombora Whānau': Sign up to the Tora Bombora waiting list and join the whānau before the link closes.
Link opens Monday, 6th July.
Link closes Sunday, 9th August.

2. Keep an eye on your inbox: Once the link has closed, you'll receive an email with a 'Tora Bombora Whānau' access code that gives you access to purchase tickets to Tora Bombora before they are released to the general public. Each whānau member may purchase up to four tickets.
Whānau ticket access and lineup out 10th August

3. General ticket release
Tuesday, 11th August - If any tickets remain after the whānau link has been sent out, they will be released in a public sale.

If this sounds like your kind of gig, put your name in the hat. The coast will do the rest.
All other info can be found at www.torabombora.co.nz

————————————————————

CAMPING: This is included in your ticket price. The festival begins at 3.00 pm Friday the 20th Jan. The camping zone will be situated on-site, right on the Pacific Ocean where you can swim, fish, surf, play and chill out.

FOOD AND SHOPS: Tora is isolated. This means no shops for 45 minutes so please make sure you bring more than enough food and gear as Martinborough is the nearest town. There will be plenty of food trucks at the event.

————————————————————

Festival Terms & Conditions:

*THIS IS AN R18 EVENT & RIGHT OF ADMISSION IS RESERVED.

**WASTE POLICY IS BRING YOUR OWN, TAKE YOUR OWN.

————————————————————

LOCATION

313 Te Awaiti Road, Tora Beach, Martinborough, South Wairarapa, Wellington, 5782

Drive time from Wellington: 2 hours 15mins.

events.long_description:
Summer Meltdown '27

SUMMER MELTDOWN - We're set to ignite your summer with an unforgettable fusion of sound, energy, and culture.

﻿

Bringing you a powerhouse lineup featuring Aotearoa's most iconic artists, SIX60, Katchafire, The Black Seeds, Troy Kingi, Ria Hall and Tiki Taane. This is the moment music fans have been waiting for - and the countdown to one of summer's biggest festivals starts right now!

﻿

TICKET DATES

Pre-sale: Thursday 10th Sept, 8am

Public Sale: Friday 11th Sept, 8am

﻿

SIX60

Returning to Wellington for the first time in 2 years to headline Summer Meltdown, SIX60's story has always felt larger than life, and their music even more so. What began as Dunedin flatmates jamming for fun has evolved into a sound that's unmistakably their own. Get ready for a full-scale spectacle of inescapable anthems.




KATCHAFIRE

Katchafire's journey from the mighty H-Town to the world stage is rooted in pure Māori pride and classic reggae spirit. Blending vibrant rhythms and uplifting grooves with cultural depth, Katchafire bring an authentic, soul-soaked reggae experience to Summer Meltdown.




THE BLACK SEEDS

Returning to their Wellington roots, The Black Seeds bring their reputation for irresistible grooves, signature warmth, rhythm and world-class energy to the Summer Meltdown stage with a live show that hits with big-beat funk, dub, soul and roots-reggae.

﻿

TROY KINGI

One of Aoteraroa's most creative artists, Troy Kingi's 10/10/10 project - ten albums, ten genres, ten years - has earned major accolades and cemented his position as a fearless creative force. Performing with his live band, The Cactus Handshake, Kingi brings a genre-shifting, bold and boundary-defying show to Brewtown.




RIA HALL

One of the country's most compelling voices, Ria Hall effortlessly blends hip-hop, reggae, soul, dancehall ragga and modern beats into a sound that's vibrant and fearless. A powerful live performer shaped by kapa haka and dedicated to elevating te reo Māori, Ria delivers a fierce and deeply soulful set.




TIKI TAANE

With a career that has been defined by innovation, creativity and a deep connection to live performance, Tiki Taane is undoubtedly one of Aotearoa's most influential and versatile artists. When Tiki steps onto the Summer Meltdown stage he'll unleash an immersive, live looping, high-energy one man band set that showcases the iconic energy that has made him a cornerstone of New Zealand music.




Summer Meltdown 2027

Huge anthems, massive performances, and a full-throttle celebration of the music that makes New Zealand unique.




Saturday 23rd January.

All Ages.

Afterpay available.




﻿

events.name: An evening with David Sedaris
events.venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
He’s been referred to as the God of the comic essay. Author David Sedaris is a savant of sardonic wit. Wellington gets to experience his razor-sharp sense of humour when he visits to promote his latest book - ‘The Land and Its People’. David will take to the stage to read from the collection of essays and freshly minted diary entries. This will be followed by a candid audience Q&A session and an extended book signing that — true to form — will run as long as it needs to.   
In ‘The Land and Its People’ he reflects on what it means to be a foreigner, a brother, and a lifelong friend — trying on the role of caretaker after his partner Hugh’s hip-replacement surgery. Equal parts tender and devastating, it’s classic Sedaris: the kind of writing that makes you laugh until you feel guilty, then laugh again anyway. It has been said that listening to him read is an affirming, joyful experience that leaves a person feeling as if their cup has been filled right to the brim.
