events.long_description:
Presented by: SBM
Propagandhi will make their long-awaited return to Australia and Aotearoa in early 2027, marking their first shows in the region in nearly eight years.
The ever-evolving standard-bearers of politically charged punk have actively kicked against musical confines and bro-punk conservatism, promoting a message of anti-fascism since 1986. Distilling their DNA of breakneck riffs, hardcore ethos, and radical consciousness, their message remains as vital, and volatile, as ever.
The tour comes in support of the Manitoba, Canada-based outfit’s eighth album, *At Peace*. In true Propagandhi fashion, it’s smart music for dangerous times. “Everything I’m singing about is still coming from being the same person that wrote and sang our first record *How to Clean Everything* in 1993,” Chris Hannah states, recalling the band’s snarky skate-thrash origins.
“But what we’re putting into the songs now, probably reflects more despair than 30 years ago when we had similar perspectives, but with strands of hope and naivete. Now it’s the existential dread of eking out a life worth living in this completely failed society.”
Propagandhi are set to bring their incendiary live show back to Australia and Aotearoa, drawing from a body of work that continues to challenge, confront, and inspire.
New album "At Peace" out now Propagandhi.com

events.long_description:
Following the sell-out success of their European summer tour, System Of A Down is heading to Hnry Stadium for its only New Zealand concert. Wellington audiences will also be entertained by warm up act and alternative rock icons Faith No More. 
This concert marks System of a Down's first Wellington show, and their first time playing in Aotearoa in more than a decade. Blending metal with diverse influences including jazz, opera, and Armenian folk, System Of A Down have sold more than 42 million albums worldwide. They released their debut self-titled album in 1998, but it was not until the release of 'Toxicity' in 2001 that their popularity exploded. Heavy music fans can expect a massive career-spanning set filled with the songs that have defined the genre for more than 25 years.
It's been a long time between Wellington shows for Faith No More. The last time the San Francisco-based band played in the capital was 1997. Responsible for such classics as Epic, Midlife Crisis, and a distinctive cover of The Commodores' Easy, they've developed a die-hard following over the last 40 years. 
Together the bands will bring decades of hard rock (and its fans) to Wellington for what promises to be one of the most electrifying nights of heavy music the city's ever seen.

events.long_description:
KYLESA have announced their return to Australia and New Zealand. After more than a decade away, the legendary American group brings their iconic blend of stoner rock, psych, sludge, metal and punk to venues across Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Auckland & Wellington.

Tickets here

Kylesa is a force of nature, a band whose sonic range and primal heaviness stunned & awed listeners for 15 years before they went dark in 2016. Formed in Savannah, Georgia in 2001, the group made their name with a series of EPs and records and relentless touring schedule. They gained a legion of fans from all over the world and dipped their toes into several different scenes as “Stoner Metal” or “Psych Metal / Indie Sludge” wasn’t necessarily on the menu. Pulling from indie rock, punk, classic heavy metal, doom, death, psychedelic and kraut rock, the band really sound like no one else.

Journalist David Peisner of Spin described them as dark psych-metal titans, practicing an aggressive, but hazy, stoner vibe...a strange amalgamation of Black Sabbath, Black Flag and early Pink Floyd.
Lead by guitar and vocal duo Laura Pleasants and Phillip Cope, Kylesa have picked up where they left off with a legendary new rhythm section in tow featuring Roy Mayorga ( Nausea, Soulfly, Stone Sour, Ministry, Jerry Cantrell ) & John John Jesse ( Nausea) rounding out the lineup.

Kylesa cemented their place as key figures in creating the Georgia metal scene by bringing forth a unique, unmatched, experimental wall of sound that is as relevant today as it was at the time.

They returned to perform at the 2025 Roadburn Festival, followed by announcements from ArcTanGent Festival, Inferno Fest and A Colossal Weekend. Since then they have made selective appearances at festivals and theatres across the globe and will finally descend on Australian and New Zealand shores in February 2027.

events.long_description:
KYLESA have announced their return to Australia and New Zealand. After more than a decade away, the legendary American group brings their iconic blend of stoner rock, psych, sludge, metal and punk to venues across Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Auckland & Wellington.

This show is at Double Whammy in Auckland

Tickets here

Kylesa is a force of nature, a band whose sonic range and primal heaviness stunned & awed listeners for 15 years before they went dark in 2016. Formed in Savannah, Georgia in 2001, the group made their name with a series of EPs and records and relentless touring schedule. They gained a legion of fans from all over the world and dipped their toes into several different scenes as “Stoner Metal” or “Psych Metal / Indie Sludge” wasn’t necessarily on the menu. Pulling from indie rock, punk, classic heavy metal, doom, death, psychedelic and kraut rock, the band really sound like no one else.

Journalist David Peisner of Spin described them as dark psych-metal titans, practicing an aggressive, but hazy, stoner vibe...a strange amalgamation of Black Sabbath, Black Flag and early Pink Floyd.
Lead by guitar and vocal duo Laura Pleasants and Phillip Cope, Kylesa have picked up where they left off with a legendary new rhythm section in tow featuring Roy Mayorga ( Nausea, Soulfly, Stone Sour, Ministry, Jerry Cantrell ) & John John Jesse ( Nausea) rounding out the lineup.

Kylesa cemented their place as key figures in creating the Georgia metal scene by bringing forth a unique, unmatched, experimental wall of sound that is as relevant today as it was at the time.

They returned to perform at the 2025 Roadburn Festival, followed by announcements from ArcTanGent Festival, Inferno Fest and A Colossal Weekend. Since then they have made selective appearances at festivals and theatres across the globe and will finally descend on Australian and New Zealand shores in February 2027.

events.name: Gillian Welch & David Rawlings
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
The traditional sound of Appalachian music. bluegrass, country, Americana, and folk will fill the Michael Fowler Centre in February. American singer-songwriters Gillian Welch and David Rawlings blend the traditional music practices together in their first New Zealand concert in over a decade. The partners on stage and in life have 30 years of experience collaborating over haunting covers of folk greats. You might hear songs like Look at Miss Ohio, Orphan Girl, and Empty Trainload of Sky. Expect sparse magical arrangements and exquisite lyricism. 

Since their last visit to Wellington, they've been busy writing and producing music. Their recent album, ‘Woodland’, is the first attributed to both of them. Despite collaborating on most things, previous albums were billed individually. The album shares the name of their Nashville studio Woodland, lost to a tornado in 2020. 

You might recognise Gillian’s voice from the Coen brothers film ‘O Brother, Where Art Thou?’. She contributed to the soundtrack and snuck into the film itself. David is also a record producer and fronts the band Dave Rawlings Machine. Together, the pair are winners of multiple Grammy Awards and a slew of other accolades.

events.long_description:
Drax Project and Friends | Town Hall, WELLINGTON
DRAX PROJECT TO HEADLINE GRAND REOPENING OF
TE WHARE WHAKARAUIKA WELLINGTON TOWN HALL SATURDAY 20 FEBRUARY 2027

Hometown heroes Drax Project are set to make history as the first act to perform at Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall when the doors officially reopen on Saturday 20 February 2027, marking the first event in the iconic venue since its closure for refurbishment 13 years ago.

The landmark concert will honour Wellington’s rich cultural and musical legacy, with Drax Project returning to the city where they first captivated audiences as buskers on central Wellington’s streets, before launching a career that would see them become one of New Zealand’s most successful acts.
Joining them on the bill is one of the city’s most beloved global names, Bret McKenzie, who will open the evening alongside his
eight-piece Wellington-based band, The State Highway Wonders.

Tickets go on sale at midday Friday 19 June from ticketmaster.co.nz

The show will also feature a host of surprise special guests throughout the night, including some of Drax Project’s favourite collaborators, inspirations and friends, creating a uniquely Wellington occasion and a celebration of the wider New Zealand
music whānau.

For Drax Project, being invited to reopen the historic 122-year-old building is a true full-circle moment as they explain
“This is going to be a very special gig for us! We all met while at uni here and Wellington is where we got our start. The Town Hall closed before Drax became a thing, but playing there is something we've always dreamt of doing as a band.”

Since emerging from Wellington’s busking scene, Drax Project have built an international career that has seen them amass nearly a billion streams resulting in 34 Platinum certifications globally. Renowned for their live show, they have toured extensively across the world including sharing stages with Ed Sheeran, Christina
Aguilera, Camilla Cabello and George Clinton. Though their music has sustained international success, Wellington remains at the heart of the band's story, making their return to reopen one of the capital’s most treasured venues a fitting homecoming.

Don’t miss your chance to be a part of this historic night. Tickets go on sale midday Friday 19 June from ticketmaster.co.nz

events.name: Shen Yun
events.venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Picture fairies drifting out of clouds and generals charging into battle. Now add tight choreography and a live orchestra. Shen Yun is coming to Wellington’s St James Theatre in February. Bring your kids along to this family-friendly show. It celebrates thousands of years of Chinese culture through classical dance and music. Dreamy scenery and costumes frame every piece. 

The orchestra blends Western symphonic and traditional Chinese instruments. These include the erhu and pipa. You don’t need to swot up about China beforehand. Bilingual emcees introduce each piece, and song lyrics are translated on the backdrop. 

The two-hour show packs in 20 pieces. One moment, you’re experiencing a legend. The next, you’re in a new region or dynasty. Mongolians ride horseback across the grasslands and generals show off their battlefield heroics. You’ll also see the philosophical works of Lao-Tzu and glimpses of heavenly realms. The stories are ancient legends of love, loss, and humour. 

Each year, eight companies, with 500 artists, perform the production across 20 countries. Every season is brand new, from the dances and music to the costumes, stories, and backdrops. Academy Award-winning actor Cate Blanchett called it “exquisitely beautiful”. Come and find out if you agree with her.

events.long_description:
In February 2027, DEL AMITRI return to Australia with Past to Present: Four Decades of Their Greatest Hits a celebratory tour showcasing the songs that defined their remarkable career, from early indie beginnings to international chart success.
Formed in Glasgow in 1982 by Justin Currie, Del Amitri found their long term creative backbone in guitarist Iain Harvie, whose presence has been central to the band’s sound for decades. Their breakthrough came with the 1989 album Waking Hours, featuring the enduring hit ‘Nothing Ever Happens’ and the deliciously catchy ‘Kiss This Thing Goodbye.’ The early ’90s brought further global recognition with ‘Always the Last to Know’ and their biggest US success, ‘Roll to Me,’ which reached Number 10 on the Billboard Hot 100 and remains a worldwide jukebox favourite.
Across seven studio albums, Del Amitri have sold over six million records, earning a reputation for sharp songwriting, wry lyricism and melodic, emotionally resonant rock that continues to connect across generations.
After a hiatus in the 2000s, the band returned for sold out reunion tours and, in 2021, released Fatal Mistakes, their first collection of new music in 18 years, reaffirming their signature sound for both long time fans and new listeners. Del Amitri are currently in the studio recording their new album which is set for a release later this year.
In 2027, the band celebrates their legacy with a powerful, career spanning Australian tour Past to Present: Four Decades of Their Greatest Hits.

🏁 THE GREAT KĀPITI RACE – SUNDAY 7 MARCH 2027 🏁

Kāpiti… THE RACE IS ON!

Grab your team and get ready for a day of clues, challenges, puzzles, mystery locations and probably a fair bit of ridiculousness as you make your way around the Kāpiti Coast.

Think adventure race meets treasure hunt — but this is NOT a fitness race! You don't need to be super fit, fast or particularly coordinated 😂 You just need a team that's ready to have some fun.

🗺️ HOW WILL IT WORK?
You'll start the day at our official starting point, where your team will receive your first clue.
Solve it correctly and it'll lead you to your next location somewhere around Kāpiti.

When you arrive, you might need to:
🧩 Solve a puzzle
🎯 Complete a challenge
🔎 Find something hidden
📸 Take a photo or video
🤪 Do something completely ridiculous
📍 Check in at a local business or location
🗺️ Work out where your next clue is sending you

Complete it and you're onto the next one!

Expect to discover local businesses, attractions, parks, sports facilities and places around Kāpiti you may never have visited before.

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 WHO CAN ENTER?
Teams will be 2–5 people and kids are absolutely welcome!
This is designed to be something families, couples, friends and workmates can all do.

You will need your own vehicle to travel between some checkpoints, and at least one team member will need to be an adult.

📅 THE IMPORTANT STUFF
DATE: Sunday 7 March 2027
TIME: Approximately 10am–4pm
LOCATION: All around the Kāpiti Coast
TEAM SIZE: 2–5 people

🏆 AND YES… THERE WILL BE PRIZES!
We'll have major prizes, spot prizes and plenty of opportunities to win things throughout the day.
And winning won't necessarily just be about being the fastest. 👀

ਜਦੋਂ ਹਾਲਾਤਾਂ ਨੇ ਉਸਨੂੰ ਝੁਕਾਉਣ ਦੀ ਕੋਸ਼ਿਸ਼ ਕੀਤੀ, ਉਹ ਹੋਰ ਮਜ਼ਬੂਤ ਹੋ ਕੇ ਖੜ੍ਹੀ ਹੋਈ।
ਜਦੋਂ ਉਸ ਤੋਂ ਉਸਦਾ ਪੁੱਤਰ, ਉਸਦਾ ਰਾਜ ਅਤੇ ਉਸਦੀ ਆਜ਼ਾਦੀ ਦੂਰ ਕੀਤੀ ਗਈ, ਫਿਰ ਵੀ ਉਸਦੇ ਦਿਲ ਵਿੱਚੋਂ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਲਈ ਪਿਆਰ ਅਤੇ ਸੰਘਰਸ਼ ਦੀ ਅੱਗ ਨਹੀਂ ਬੁਝੀ।

⚔️ ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ ਜਿੰਦ ਕੌਰ — ਸ਼ੇਰ-ਏ-ਪੰਜਾਬ ਮਹਾਰਾਜਾ ਰਣਜੀਤ ਸਿੰਘ ਦੀ ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ ਅਤੇ ਮਹਾਰਾਜਾ ਦਲੀਪ ਸਿੰਘ ਦੀ ਮਾਤਾ — ਦੀ ਇਹ ਗਾਥਾ ਸਾਡੀ ਆਉਣ ਵਾਲੀ ਪੀੜ੍ਹੀ ਤੱਕ ਪਹੁੰਚਣੀ ਚਾਹੀਦੀ ਹੈ।

🎭 Rang Manch Karee Theatre Group Melbourne ਵੱਲੋਂ ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ ਜਿੰਦਾਂ ਦੀ ਜ਼ਿੰਦਗੀ, ਸੰਘਰਸ਼, ਮਾਂ ਦੀ ਮਮਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਪ੍ਰਤੀ ਉਸਦੇ ਅਟੁੱਟ ਪਿਆਰ ਨੂੰ ਜੀਵੰਤ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੰਚ ’ਤੇ ਪੇਸ਼ ਕੀਤਾ ਜਾਵੇਗਾ।

🇳🇿 ਹੁਣ ਇਹ ਇਤਿਹਾਸਕ ਨਾਟਕ Wellington ਵਿੱਚ!

📅 ਐਤਵਾਰ, 7 ਮਾਰਚ 2027
📍 Little Theatre, Lower Hutt, Wellington

❤️ ਆਓ ਆਪਣੇ ਬੱਚਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਵੀ ਨਾਲ ਲੈ ਕੇ ਆਈਏ।
ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਦੱਸੀਏ ਕਿ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੇ ਇਤਿਹਾਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਮਹਾਰਾਜੇ ਹੀ ਨਹੀਂ — ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀਆਂ ਨੇ ਵੀ ਇਤਿਹਾਸ ਰਚਿਆ ਹੈ।

✨ ਇਹ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਇੱਕ ਨਾਟਕ ਨਹੀਂ…
ਇਹ ਸਾਡੇ ਇਤਿਹਾਸ ਦੀ ਆਵਾਜ਼ ਹੈ।
ਇਹ ਇੱਕ ਮਾਂ ਦੇ ਦਰਦ ਦੀ ਕਹਾਣੀ ਹੈ।
ਇਹ ਇੱਕ ਔਰਤ ਦੇ ਅਟੁੱਟ ਹੌਸਲੇ ਦੀ ਕਹਾਣੀ ਹੈ।
ਇਹ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਦੀ ਸ਼ੇਰਨੀ — ਮਹਾਰਾਣੀ ਜਿੰਦਾਂ ਦੀ ਦਾਸਤਾਨ ਹੈ। 👑🔥

🙏 ਇਸ ਇਤਿਹਾਸਕ ਪੇਸ਼ਕਾਰੀ ਦਾ ਹਿੱਸਾ ਜ਼ਰੂਰ ਬਣੋ ਅਤੇ ਇਸ ਸੁਨੇਹੇ ਨੂੰ ਵੱਧ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਧ ਸਾਂਝਾ ਕਰੋ।

📞 ਆਪਣੇ ਸ਼ਹਿਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਸ਼ੋਅ ਕਰਵਾਉਣ ਲਈ ਸਾਡੀ ਟੀਮ ਨਾਲ ਸੰਪਰਕ ਕਰੋ।

👑 MAHARANI JINDAN – THE LAST QUEEN OF THE PUNJAB 👑
🇳🇿 LIVE IN WELLINGTON, NEW ZEALAND 🇳🇿

Wellington, get ready to witness a powerful chapter of Punjab’s history brought alive on stage! ❤️

Wellington Punjabi Women Association Incorporated proudly presents “Maharani Jindan”, performed by the talented Rang Manch Karee Theatre Group Melbourne.

Maharani Jind Kaur was not only the last Queen of the Sikh Empire — she was a symbol of courage, strength, dignity and resistance. Her extraordinary story deserves to be remembered and shared with our next generation.

🎭 Experience her journey through a powerful live theatrical performance filled with history, emotion and Punjabi heritage.

📅 Sunday, 7 March 2027
📍 Little Theatre, Lower Hutt, Wellington

✨ A story of a Queen.
A story of courage.
A story of Punjab.
A story that must never be forgotten.

Bring your family and especially your younger generation to experience this important piece of our history. ❤️

Naina • Sarb • Karminder • Harpuneet • Jasdeep • Harmeet • Navneet

events.name: Új-Zéland kiscsoportos körutazás – kalandtúra a világ végén
events.venue: Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Új-Zéland kiscsoportos körutazás – kalandtúra a világ végén
https://hellovilagvlog.hu/uj-zeland-kiscsoportos-korutazas-kalandtura-a-vilag-vegen/

Készen állsz arra, hogy eljuss a világ egyik legvadabb és legérintetlenebb tájára? Az Új-Zéland kiscsoportos körutazás – kalandtúra a világ végén azoknak szól, akik nem csak látni szeretnének, hanem valóban átélni akarják a természet erejét és változatosságát. Utunkat az Északi-sziget különleges világában kezdjük: Auckland, Hobbiton, Rotorua és Wai-O-Tapu gejzírmezői, gőzölgő hőforrásai és vulkáni tájai már az első napokban megmutatják Új-Zéland nyers arcát. A Lake Taupō partján haladva érkezünk meg a Tongariro Nemzeti Parkba, ahol drámai vulkáni panorámák és alpesi környezet vár ránk — itt nem csak nézelődünk, beleállunk az élménybe. A főváros, Wellington után átkelünk a Cook-szoroson, és megérkezünk a Déli-szigetre. A Picton környéki fjordos partvidéktől az Abel Tasman térség aranyhomokos öblein át vezet az utunk tovább. A vad West Coast mentén elérjük a különleges formájú Pancake Rocks szikláit, majd a lenyűgöző Franz Josef-gleccser világát. A túra csúcspontjai közé tartozik Te Anau és a legendás Milford Sound, ahol hajóra szállva függőleges sziklafalak, vízesések és mély fjordok között haladunk. Ez nem egy klasszikus városnézős túra, hanem egy tartalmas, természetközeli Új-Zéland kiscsoportos körutazás, ahol rövid idő alatt meglepően sok mindent látunk, mégsem rohanunk. Kiscsoportban utazunk, rugalmasan, a legszebb panorámautakon haladva — mert a világ végén nem sietni kell, hanem megélni minden kilométert.

https://hellovilagvlog.hu/uj-zeland-kiscsoportos-korutazas-kalandtura-a-vilag-vegen/

events.name: Tony Martin: From Seedling to Sensation – How New Zealand Creates the Apples and Pears of the Future
events.venue: Hawkes Bay,Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Tony Martin: From Seedling to Sensation – How New Zealand Creates the Apples and Pears of the Future
Have you ever bitten into an apple and wondered where it came from?

Not the orchard.

Not the supermarket.

But the very first idea that eventually became the fruit in your hand.

Creating a new apple or pear variety isn't something that happens overnight. It can take years of research, testing, patience and innovation before a single piece of fruit reaches consumers.

Join Tony Martin, Chief Executive of Prevar, for a fascinating behind-the-scenes Learning Lunch exploring how New Zealand is helping shape the future of fruit.

From understanding changing consumer tastes to developing entirely new varieties, Tony will reveal the remarkable journey from seedling to supermarket shelf and the science, strategy and creativity that make it possible.

You'll discover how some of New Zealand's most successful apple and pear varieties were developed, what makes a fruit variety stand out in global markets, and why innovation in horticulture requires both long-term thinking and bold decision-making.

Best of all, this isn't just a conversation.

Guests will enjoy a guided tasting of different apple and pear varieties, offering a rare opportunity to experience firsthand the flavours, textures and characteristics that breeders spend years developing.

This is a wonderful opportunity to look at something familiar in a completely new way.

Meet Tony 🎤

Tony Martin is Chief Executive of Prevar, the innovation and commercialisation company behind many of New Zealand and Australia's leading apple and pear varieties. events.long_description:
Tragic pop-musical Miss Saigon hasn’t played Wellington in over 15 years. Fabulous soloists, a 40-strong local choir, and a live orchestra are rectifying that in 2027. G&T Productions brings a semi-staged concert to the Michael Fowler Centre. This format puts the performers and music front and centre. Set during the final days of the Vietnam War in 1975, Miss Saigon is a heartbreaking, bold, and gripping musical theatre piece. 

From the songwriting team behind ‘Les Misérables’, Miss Saigon is a tragic love story of a young Vietnamese woman (Kim) who falls in love with an American soldier (Chris). Saigon falls, and their story unfolds alongside the Engineer, a ruthless survivor chasing his own ‘American Dream’. 

Wellingtonian Maya Handa Naff plays Kim. She has previously sung the role in the United States. Maya is an actor, director, and teacher whose Wellington performance credits include ‘Wicked’ (Glinda) and ‘Les Misérables’ (Eponine). Director and actor Kyle Chuen plays Chris. Laurence Mossman returns as Thuy after performing the part on Australian and international tours. Expect to hear songs like I’d Give My Life for You, Why God Why, and Bui Doi.

events.long_description:
The Weave - Sheol
The first weekend game for The Weave LARP campaign, a futuristic fantasy game in Wellington.

About this Event



*********

Don’t look down. The sky is clear and blue. When you breathe in for the first time after your months-long voyage, the fresh air tastes impossibly sweet.

Don’t look down. A single star rests in the heavens, yellow and warm. Shoals of silvery fish dart through picturesque waves.

Don’t look down. The islands quake and churn beneath your feet. Alerts appear hourly on your screens about impossibilities, measurements beyond rational explanation.

You look down. What lies beneath? What might be unearthed from the strata of the past? What has been forgotten? And what should have remained buried?




What's going on?

A week ago, three ships landed on the planet called Etsen. The Highmit Research Mission has journeyed to this planet, across the vast dangers of space, to help the planet’s scientists understand the impossibility of measuring a second star in a 100 kilometre diameter patch of their sky.

You landed at Scion. It’s small, compared to the average communities on your home planets. Not even 5000 people. But it’s the largest settlement in Etsen’s affected zone. And it’s a strange new environment for many of you, perched on an island in a temperate archipelago.

The research mission’s primary team has already set up their main base of operations in Scion. Alongside the limited number of specialised Etsenite scientists, they are beginning initial research into the planet’s anomaly.

A few days ago, a small settlement in the affected zone, Axis, reported abnormal technological errors. Yesterday, a different settlement, closer to Scion, reported similar malfunctions.

You are members of the secondary research team dispatched to Axis. Your task sounds simple enough.

Identify the cause of the errors.
Prevent them from spreading further.

But, just like the impossible second star, you suspect nothing is as simple as it seems.




*********




OOC information

Sheol is the first weekend game of The Weave LARP.

The game is running on 20-21 March 2027 in Wellington at Khandallah Scout Hall (11A Station Road, Khandallah, Wellington 6035).
The game runs for 2 full days. There is no overnight accommodation. You will have the opportunity to leave a small amount of gear on-site overnight.
Players are self-catered. We are currently working with a generous volunteer to see if we can cater our crew. The crew will get confirmation closer to the start of the game if we can cater them.
The game is open to new player-characters, pending available tickets.

This game is 18+.




Tickets

Tickets go on sale Tuesday 29 September at 7pm through Eventbrite. Participants who attended the July 2026 day game will have early bird access. You must buy a ticket to secure your place. Ticket costs do not include Eventbrite fees.

Ticket price:

Players: $110 ($100 with NZLARPs member discount)
Crew: $60 ($50 with NZLARPs member discount)


Find the NZLARPs discount code by logging into your NZLARPs account and looking at the event page ( https://nzlarps.org/events/detail/356). If your NZLARP membership details are still pending or you can't figure out how to log into the website, ask us for the code in an email at .

This is an NZLARPs project. By purchasing a ticket, you are agreeing to follow the NZLARPs Code of Conduct: https://nzlarps.org/join/conduct/.

events.id: NZSQ — Strings in the Earth & Air-Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall-Wellington NZ
events.name: NZSQ — Strings in the Earth & Air
events.venue: Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall
events.long_description:
A concert of traditional Irish airs and folk melodies will be presented at a concert at the newly opened Wellington Town Hall in April 2027. Join Tom Delany and Dave Flynn for traditional and contemporary works in NZSQ — Strings in the Earth & Air. Tom Delany will play the uilleann pipes, while Dave Flynn will be on the guitar. ‘Uilleann’ means ‘elbow’ in Irish. The uilleann pipes are powered by the elbow, pumping air instead of the Scottish bagpipes that use the lungs. 

The concert takes its name from James Joyce’s poetry collection ‘Chamber Music’. Most of the poems in the collection revolve around the twin themes of love and music. ‘Strings in the earth and air’ is the poem that opens the collection. The concert forms part of New Zealand String Quartet’s In Collaboration series. With roughly one in six Kiwis being of Irish heritage, there are enduring connections between Ireland and Aotearoa. This concert brings those ties to life through poetry, song, and strings.

Tom Delany plays uilleann pipes, guitar, and bouzouki, and sings. As a founding member of Irish ensemble FOURWINDS, he has toured the world. He is known for playing traditional Irish music in a daring, free-flowing style. Dave Flynn is a composer and guitarist who offers a unique blend of Irish trad, minimalism, and jazz. His work has been performed by leading ensembles in venues across the globe.

events.venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
There’s never been a group, let alone a supergroup, in rock history quite like it. Now you get to see a tribute to their huge success. In 1988, a group of five rock legends joined together to form The Traveling Wilburys. They were Bob Dylan, George Harrison, Jeff Lynne, Roy Orbison, and Tom Petty. 
Across four years, they produced two mega albums, a slew of hits and won a Grammy. They never toured. Now, a tribute band, The Travelling Wilburys Collective, is on tour and it’s visiting the St James Theatre in Wellington. 
You’ll get to hear some of their biggest and most celebrated hits like Handle with Care, End of the Line, Tweeter and the Monkey Man, and She's My Baby. Along with these original hits, you’ll get served classics from each individual artist and the groups they were in. That includes The Beatles, The Heartbreakers, and ELO. 
The Traveling Wilburys Collection bring together the collective talents, excitement, and magic that the original quintet had to offer. Join them for a night of fun and nostalgia.

events.venue: Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall
events.long_description:
The New Zealand professional premiere of one of Andrew Lloyd Webber’s most celebrated musicals is coming to Wellington. Sunset Boulevard takes centre stage at the newly restored Wellington Town Hall in April. Local company WITCH Music Theatre is presenting an epic site-specific production as part of the venue’s grand reopening programme. 

In a major coup for the production, acclaimed Tony Award-nominated performer Keala Settle will be playing the main role, Norma Desmond. Keala has strong iwi links to New Zealand so she sees this opportunity as a homecoming. She is best known for her role as Lettie Lutz in ‘The Greatest Showman’ and for her powerhouse performance of the Golden Globe-winning song “This Is Me” from the film. 

Sunset Boulevard has earned major acclaim across Broadway and the West End, including seven awards from 11 Tony Award nominations for its original 1994 Broadway production. It’s 2023 revival won seven Olivier Awards from 11 nominations. The production, designed specifically for the Town Hall’s refurbished auditorium, marks the New Zealand professional premiere of the musical.

events.name: Menopause The Musical
events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Described as the ultimate ladies’ night out, Menopause the Musical has been delivering laughs across the globe for years. Now the fun-filled musical about ‘the change’ returns to Wellington for one night.
Set in a department store, four women meet by chance while shopping for a black lace bra. Though they couldn’t be more different, they quickly discover a shared bond over memory loss, hot flushes, night sweats, and mood swings. What follows is a hilarious, heart-warming musical told with love, laughter and the greatest hits of the 60s, 70s and 80s. The laughter-filled 90-minute production gets audiences out of their seats dancing and singing along to clever parodies of beloved pop classics.
Winner of over 40 Tony Awards, Menopause the Musical has entertained more than 17 million fans worldwide. It’s been translated into nine languages and performed in more than 500 cities. The show’s enduring appeal lies in its honesty, hilarity and heart. It celebrates women everywhere and turns shared experiences into shared joy.

events.long_description:
The last in a trilogy of cycling-themed plays skids into The Wellington Opera House in May.  Writer-director Gregory Cooper and seasoned Kiwi actor Mark Hadlow collaborate once more to bring their cycling trilogy to a close. The one-man play 'WOBIL: Wise Old Bugger in Lycra' follows previous installments ‘MAMIL: Middle Aged Man In Lycra’ and ‘GOMIL: Grumpy Old Man In Lycra’. Expect familiar faces, trademark physical comedy, plenty of laughs, and a fair bit of heart too.
Mark is one of New Zealand’s best-known actors. You might have seen him on screen in ‘King Kong’ or ‘The Hobbit’, or a host of live professional theatre shows on stages around the motu.  Gregory's past work includes ‘That Bloody Woman’. This latest chapter sends Wayne on his hardest hill climb yet. With help, and hindrance, from a few old friends and enemies, he’s determined to go out in a blaze of lycra glory. Get ready for one last spin through friendship, ageing, and resilience.

events.long_description:
Presented by: Destroy All Lines
British legends Squeeze are returning to New Zealand in April 2027 with their Tried, Tested and Trixies Tour, celebrating 53 years of classic songwriting and standout music hits from one of the UK’s pioneers of Brit-pop music.
Founded in 1974 by Chris Difford and Glenn Tilbrook, Squeeze are one of pop’s best-loved bands with a catalogue of sky-high classics such as ‘Up the Junction’, ‘Tempted’, ‘Cool for Cats’, ‘Another Nail in My Heart’ and ‘Labelled with Love’, whose live shows are legendary and, as The Guardian wrote, “pop perfection”.
Squeeze remain one of the most revered and distinctive music outfits in UK pop history. Led by the unparalleled songwriting duo Glenn Tilbrook and Chris Difford, their legacy spans over five decades of masterful songwriting, stellar live performance, and cultural impact; between 1978 and 1996 they had no fewer than 11 singles in the UK Top 40, with six in the Top 20. Many more of their songs have been woven into the very fabric of the British songwriting tradition – alongside those of The Beatles and The Kinks – influencing everyone from Lily Allen to The Killers.
Coming to New Zealand to mark 50+ years of Squeeze and celebrate the release of their new album, Trixies, will be Glenn Tilbrook, bassist Owen Biddle, percussionist Steve Smith, keyboardist Stephen Large, drummer Simon Hanson, guitarist Leon Tilbrook and backing vocalist Danica Dora.
events.description:
Presented by: Destroy All Lines British legends Squeeze are returning to New Zealand in April 2027 with their Tried, Tested and Trixies Tour, celebrating 53 years of classic songwriting and standout music hits from one of the UK’s pioneers of Brit-pop music.
Founded in 1974 by Chris Difford and Glenn Tilbrook, Squeeze are one of pop’s best-loved bands with a catalogue of sky-high classics such as ‘Up the Junction’, ‘Tempted’, ‘Cool for Cats’, ‘Another Nail in My Heart’ and ‘Labelled with Love’, whose live shows are legendary and, as The Guardian wrote, “pop perfection”.
Squeeze remain one of the most revered and distinctive music outfits in UK pop history.
Led by the unparalleled songwriting duo Glenn Tilbrook and Chris Difford, their legacy spans over five decades of masterful songwriting, stellar live performance, and cultural impact; between 1978 and 1996 they had no fewer than 11 singles in the UK Top 40, with six in the Top 20.
Many more of their songs have been woven into the very fabric of the British songwriting tradition – alongside those of The Beatles and The Kinks – influencing everyone from Lily Allen to The Killers.

events.long_description:
Portland, Oregon producer, singer-songwriter and storyteller John Craigie returns to New Zealand in April 2027 on his I Swam Here Tour.
 
Following his first New Zealand shows in 2025, Craigie returns with his latest album, I Swam Here, out now on Zabriskie Point Records. Written and produced by Craigie, the album was recorded between New Orleans and Astoria, Oregon, bringing together the musical spirit of the Gulf Coast with the quieter sounds of the Pacific Northwest.
 
For more than a decade, Craigie has built a devoted following through his warm, sharply observed songwriting and live shows that pair music with humour and storytelling. His touring has taken him across the U.S., Europe and Australia, with appearances at Newport Folk, Pickathon, Edmonton Folk Festival and High Sierra, and performances alongside artists including Gregory Alan Isakov, Sierra Hull, Brett Dennen and Jack Johnson.
 

I Swam Here follows 2024’s Pagan Church, Craigie’s collaboration with TK & The Holy Know-Nothings, which spent six weeks at #1 on the Americana Albums chart. Expansive yet intimate, the new record marks another chapter for Craigie while retaining the sincerity and conversational songwriting that have become central to his work.
 

Craigie returns to San Fran, Wellington on Thursday 15 April and The Tuning Fork, Auckland on Friday 16 April 2027, returning to the same venues that hosted his first New Zealand tour in 2025.
 

San Fran holds a Supervised License. Minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue.

events.long_description:
Every May, the capital comes alive with laughter, thanks to the New Zealand International Comedy Festival (NZICF). New Zealand’s homegrown talent shares the stage with some of the world’s most exciting comedians. You could catch a big-name international artist, or discover a new local rising star. 
Since it began in 1993, the aim of the festival has been to champion the craft of comedy so everyone can share a laugh. Every year, a huge group of comedians descend on Wellington from local shores and beyond to deliver three weeks of merriment. 
The festival offers a diverse range of high-quality laughs. It showcases the best of local comedy and gives audiences a taste of some of the world’s best acts. Catch over 100 comics performing at The Opera House, BATS Theatre, Fringe Bar, San Fran, and more.

events.long_description:
Madchester royalty return! Inspiral Carpets are part of Manchester's holy trinity with the Stone Roses and Happy Mondays and will bring The Singles Tour to Australia and New Zealand this April and May. 

Back in the early ’90s, when Madchester was at its peak, Inspiral Carpets were perhaps best known for their “cool as fuck” T-shirts, which were essential wear for any young indie fan looking to annoy their parents 

Expect the hits, and nothing but the hits, including This Is How It Feels, Saturn 5, She Comes in the Fall, Joe, Dragging Me Down + More… you will be reminded of just how great they are and how many of their songs you know and love! 

“Inspiral Carpets were perhaps the best singles band of the Madchester era” (Pitchfork) 

Since reuniting, the band has sold out shows across the UK and Europe as well as a bunch of Australian dates on their 2023 tour. Keyboard player Clint Boon says the live show is the strongest it has been “We’re on fire at the moment. We’re playing better than ever, and I think we’re appreciating it more, too… It’s brilliant that we’re still here doing it”. Critics say “This is arguably the best I’ve seen the Inspiral Carpets over the decades… Saturn 5 ends the set, blowing the roof off the venue” (Louder Than War)

Dig out your Cool as Fuck T-shirt that your parents didn’t approve of and get ready for their trademark vocal harmonies and the unmistakable swirl of Clint Boon’s organ… bucket hats welcome.  

moo!

events.id: Kia Mau--Wellington NZ
events.name: Kia Mau
events.long_description:
Kia Mau is an arts festival that showcases innovative Indigenous performances. Held every two years, the festival lights up Wellington's winter. See contemporary performances by leading Tāngata Whenua , Tāngata Moana, and global Indigenous artists. The two-week festival includes dance, theatre, music, and visual art. Audiences can expect to be challenged and thrilled by new work from Aotearoa and beyond.
Kia Mau was first held in 2015, founded by two leading Aotearoa creatives. Hone Kouka (Ngāti Porou, Ngāti Kahungunu, Ngāti Raukawa, Kai Tahu) is the Artistic Director and Chief Executive. Mīria George (Ngāti Kearoa, Ngāti Tuara, Ngāti Awa, Ngāti Kūki ‘Āirani) is the Executive Director.
Hone and Mīria describe themselves as innovators. They push boundaries, redefine forms, and forge new paths. They say the festival is not just a platform for presentations, it’s a hub for kōrero and whanaungatanga . The festival has a strong influence on many artists and plays an important role in shaping New Zealand’s contemporary arts scene. “Kia Mau has continued to thrive because of the imagination and commitment of our artists. And of us to them,” says Mīria.
